Now Villa were, as the home choirs gleefully announced, top of the league and they received further opportunities to hammer home the point. Alejandro Garnacho saw one of them saved by Østbø after a strong run but Viking remained a threat and Christiansen’s finish, emphatically converting Kristoffer Askildsen’s deep cross, was by some distance the best of the night.

“The second half was much more like the Viking we want to be,” said Morten Jensen, who co-manages the Norwegian champions alongside Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim. “Maybe we had too much respect for them in the first half, they were all over us.”

View image in fullscreen Emiliano Buendía calmly doubles Aston Villa’s lead from the penalty spot. Photograph: Alex Livesey/AVFC/Getty Images

Nine points from nine, not to mention 12 consecutive home wins in Europe, mean Villa are flying. Sweeping Fenerbahce and Viking aside can “give us confidence and comfort for the next challenges,” Emery said. They will need plenty of it given a trip to Barcelona follows the relatively soft run presented so far. Maybe the peak is yet to come.

Sports.title: Champions League: Silva sparks Real Madrid’s demolition of Leipzig as Lask stun Sporting
Sports.content:
Real Madrid claimed a third Champions League victory in as many games by thrashing RB Leipzig 4-1 on Wednesday, with Kylian Mbappé and Yan Diomande among the goals for José Mourinho’s side.

Bernardo Silva opened the scoring for Madrid from close range towards the end of a tight first half, with Arda Guler doubling the record 15-time European champions’ advantage soon after the interval.

Mbappé bent home a third before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back for the German side and Diomande rammed a volley into the top corner to cap Madrid’s triumph late on.

“We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible – we’ve won three and there are five to go,” Mbappé said. The France forward, who hopes to win the Ballon d’Or next week, has netted in each of Madrid’s Champions League matches this season and has 12 goals in 12 games.

“I’m doing well [but] I think I can do more,” he said. “I’m one of the few players who always has to demand more from himself ... right now it’s a good moment, but we have to keep going and I have to do more.”

Lask launched an impressive comeback at Sporting to earn their first Champions League win of the season. The Austrian champions went behind when Luis Suárez scored from the spot after five minutes, but equalised 10 minutes later through Christoph Lang.

The visitors then stunned the Estádio José Alvalade as Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek put them 3-1 up, the former rounding off a smart team move and the latter firing in at the near post. Suárez scored again for the hosts late on, but it was not enough.

View image in fullscreen Victor Osimhen, with Yunus Akgun on his shoulders, after rounding off Galatasaray’s 4-2 win at Lille. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

Galatasaray swept past Lille at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, setting the tone with a goal after two minutes from Yunus Akgun.

Lille levelled the score via Soriba Diaoune, who then put them 2-1 up in the 39th minute. Aleksey Batrakov made it 2-2 just before half-time, however, before an own goal from Nabil Bentaleb and Victor Osimhen, in action against his former club, sealed a 4-2 victory.

Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto’s late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points of the league phase.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bastoni was sent off for two yellow cards in as many minutes, putting Inter on the back foot. Carlos Augusto saved the day in the 77th minute, capping a lightning-fast counterattack with a low finish.

View image in fullscreen Isco wheels away after netting from 12 yards to put Real Betis 1-0 up against Feyenoord. Photograph: Antonio Pozo/PRESSINPHOTO/Shutterstock

Real Betis, who beat Feyenoord 1-0 via a penalty kick from Isco, made it three from three in the Champions League to extend their strong start to the season.

Betis had the lion’s share of the chances, but only broke the deadlock when Jeremiah St Juste was adjudged to have handled in the box. Isco stepped up and fired low into the right-hand corner for what proved to be the winner.

Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 at the Jan Breydel Stadium in a ruthless home performance. The Belgians went 1-0 up through Hans Vanaken in first-half stoppage time before Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs secured the win in the second half.

Sports.title: Paris Saint-Germain sparkle on the pitch while the city of light burns around them | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
PASSION!

GOOOOAL!

MVP!

The security deployment will be massive.

Those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it.

Tell you who would have loved this? Who would have been utterly engrossed scrolling the hashtag #Paris on Tuesday night as two things happened simultaneously, the harrowing of the Barcelona defence at the Parc des Princes, and the harrowing of Paris itself via tales of city-centre thuggery and end-of-days political doom‑mongering.

The big man, Guy Debord himself. The Society of the Spectacle, you say? Actually, I think we’re past that now. Hold the society bit. We’ll just take the spectacle.

The great Parisian Situationist philosopher wasn’t really one for managed fun. But it was impossible not to be bowled over by the extraordinary pre-match show for Paris Saint‑Germain versus Barcelona, Champions League Matchday Three.

The wild pyrotechnics, the plumes of smoke, the full-wrap light show, the lime-green robo‑text spelling out every player’s name on the pitch. Although not the Barcelona names, sadly, for anyone with an unrealised desire to see the words “ANTHONY GORDON” projected in vast letters for the delight of a shrieking crowd.

Admittedly, the Halloween‑themed tifo banner showing a masked Paris Saint-Germain serial killer-type literally butchering the Barcelona badge to death with his bloodied chainsaw was perhaps a bit much. As were the Barça Puta signs, which are now reportedly the subject of a complaint to Uefa.

But it was a wild and all‑consuming spectacle, annihilating every other impulse in your head to a green thought in a green shade. And in the process capturing the profound sense of cognitive dissonance in the city.

View image in fullscreen PSG fans light flares after their team took the lead against Barcelona. Photograph: Julien de Rosa/AFP/Getty Images

Just walking around the streets of central Paris earlier in the day generated its own mild whiplash. On the face of it this was still the same city of flâneurs and tourists and everyday bistro business, and not, repeat not, a civil war drama or some kind of emergent military caliphate.

But the sense of dread was also tangible. You still got the occasional crunch of glass underfoot. Here and there charred bikes and scooters had been politely piled to one side. Even close to the Parc, away from the main hotspots, shopkeepers could be seen emerging warily into their doorways at the sound of a police siren.

By Tuesday night, a total of 2,513 people had been taken into police custody after the events of the weekend. At least 420 rental bikes had been destroyed or maimed. Liberated high-value retail goods were already being sold on Vinted, a commendable show of entrepreneurial energy from the maligned younger generation.

Not that you’d suspect these two worlds had any kind of overlap, lost in the booming triumphalism around PSG’s 4–2 win, one of the most beautifully luminous football matches you’re ever likely to see. Or indeed reading the coverage of an event that seems to have been treated in France like its own clear, clean space, floating above the flames, all the chat about the brilliance of Monsieur Dynamite, Désiré Doué, the wonderful television audiences on Canal+ TV, the whole of European football “kneeling before the machine” (are we sure this isn’t to do with anarchic rejection of social control?). “Paris est insubmersible!” was the headline in Le Parisien. But is it?

Remember when football used to reflect the world? Or just provide clues, a commentary, some kind of metaphor? This is no longer the case. At a time when even the most thunderous of commentators is struggling to summarise all this in suitably trite and damning terms, it was hard to avoid the feeling Paris Saint-Germain, the pet power football project of the state of Qatar, expresses this dualism perfectly.

Sometimes you just have to let football tell you things. “People who want to cause trouble in the city centres next Saturday will be prevented,” Emmanuel Macron announced on Tuesday evening, speaking, as it happens, from Doha, where he met Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani, ultimate owner of PSG.

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué (left) with João Neves after scoring PSG’s first goal against Barcelona. Photograph: David Ramos/Uefa/Getty Images

Macron is said to be considering deploying the French military to keep the peace on the streets before the next planned protests, although even here he may have to ask Qatar’s permission if he wants to deploy any of the French troops currently deployed working its missile systems, or embedded in the Doha security services.

The key event Macron is tooling up for is this Saturday night, 24 October, the date the gilets jaunes social media feed has set for an even greater swell of disorder. And again this will be football adjacent, with PSG playing Lyon at home on Sunday, a top‑of‑the-table capital‑city clash played out against whatever wreckage is left, however many thousands of Dot bikes are savaged, whatever guerrilla skirmishes are still playing out in the Marais.

What does this really have to do with football and the Ici C’est Paris brand appropriated by a state outreach project? Well, what are these demonstrations anyway? There have been many theories put forward as to what exactly is happening here, what is the spark, the kindling, the fire behind this disorder. School protests were the original line. Others have now roped in some kind of nebulous omni-cause, Instagram-activism, perhaps even a barbarian takeover, the decline of the west, savagery at the gates, of the type Donald Trump pretends to see.

Do you need a single reason? Take a look around. Modern life is pretty alarming on a minute‑to‑minute basis. Disaffection, alienation, a sense of being transformed in real time into a passive economic consumer unit, a set of eyeballs, an avatar of consumption. French youth unemployment is close to 20%. Robots nobody wants are being lined up to take jobs that don’t exist. Why don’t these young people want to join a youth club? Why don’t they 

On the other hand, what is PSG in Paris, other than the perfect expression of this? It often seems to surprise people that celebrations of PSG victories end up with riots and burnt-out cars. But Paris is both a beautiful and deeply dysfunctional city, a place of make‑believe and deprivation, where the centre is a perfect, performative relic, the suburbs shunted out to the ring roads, a life lived inside a box, noses pressed up against the glass, peering through your binoculars at the city of someone else’s love.

Paris is the divide between overclass and churn expressed in a single city. It’s everything you might have had but never will. And PSG represent this like no other entity, a football club owned as an act of outreach by a staggeringly rich inherited monarchy, weaponised passion, borrowed culture, engineered spectacle, deeply cynical but also deeply seductive.

View image in fullscreen Damage after the riots in Place de la République. Photograph: Telmo Pinto/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Why are the Qataris splurging hundreds of millions into this project? Because they just really like high-pressing positional football? Qatar is the indentured labour state that employs Colin Kaepernick to promote its outreach projects. It will hymn its connections to the footballers of the banlieue, which is true and real and valuable, but not because of anything this political project wants or needs other than public relations.

It is in its own way a perfect human lab experiment, synthesised beauty, collectivism, with a cold, cold hand at its heart. And this is why there weren’t two versions of Paris in evidence on Tuesday night, just the same one, the dark side and the shiny side, an engine of the same divisions, the same kind of violence, right down to the sight of kids in PSG training gear dodging the police or taunting the barricades at the Place de la République.

And now we have Sunday night to come, more Ici C’est Paris, more PASSION. What kind of background will it be played out against? Does it matter under the lights? Will anyone notice?

Le Monde has described these events as a very basic test of the republic, its ability to bend, to remain essentially itself, the state’s willingness to pit itself against its own people. Football, as ever, holds these answers already. PSG’s Qatari owners have spent the past 15 years flaunting this city like a global luxury brand, extending its reach, creating its own ideal of conspicuous consumption, spectacle, triumph, son et lumière, bread and roses. As ever, if you want to know how and why, football has the answers.

Sports.title: ‘A complete threat’: Rio Ngumoha’s electric display excites Van Dijk and Liverpool
Sports.content:
The shot sailed wide of Peter Gulacsi’s top corner and into the Kop, affording Villarreal much-needed respite at 4-2, but for Andoni Iraola it was a standout moment in a scintillating Champions League display from Rio Ngumoha. To a coach who called for versatility from all of his wingers this summer, here was a significant step forward among many from the 18-year-old at Anfield.

There were questions over how Ngumoha would adapt to playing on the right even before Liverpool increased the likelihood by signing Bradley Barcola for £123m from Paris Saint-Germain. On his fifth start under Iraola on Tuesday, which his side won 4-3, Liverpool witnessed an answer: quickly, incisively and confidently. The teenager’s willingness to cut inside from the right and shoot from distance with his left foot captured Iraola’s imagination as much as the devastating run that created Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the game.

“I’m happy with his attitude because he’s eager to improve the things that we think he needs to improve,” the Liverpool head coach said after the comeback win against their Spanish opponents. “He has played a lot on the right lately. He’s feeling so comfortable now that he’s even adding some shots with the left. He hasn’t scored but he’s getting there, and if he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position.”

Ngumoha’s 71st-minute attempt was reminiscent of Mohamed Salah in its intent, if not in execution. The Liverpool great’s final season at Anfield may have been the exception to the exceptional in terms of his own contribution but, as an education to a gifted and hungry young winger, it was not wasted.

Virgil van Dijk noted that “a few senior players” have taken Ngumoha under their wing. “I would say Cody [Gakpo] is definitely part of that. Everyone is chipping in but for him to work with Mo last year was obviously massive. Mo was one of the best wingers at the club and experienced everything so why not soak in all the information and show it on the pitch and show your own qualities? I think he has shown it this season but there is still much more to come. He’s pretty electric at times and he showed it again. He was a complete threat constantly and their defender had a tough time.”

View image in fullscreen Rio Ngumoha proved a constant threat to Villarreal. Photograph: Richard Martin-Roberts/CameraSport/Getty Images

The Salah comparison was not the only throwback for Liverpool against Villarreal. It was a flawed performance with Van Dijk’s early mistake, Iraola’s initial formation and Liverpool’s lethargy on the ball all punished by Iñigo Pérez’s slick side. “It was a terrible start,” the Liverpool captain said. “I think the saying is you fight an uphill battle and as a defender it is pretty difficult to come back from it. I tried but it was a bad day at the office personally but we do it together with 11 players. We turned it around and that’s the main thing.”

The rousing recovery, the relentless high press, Iraola’s bold changes and the character required to overturn a 2-0 deficit all carried echoes of the Jürgen Klopp era. Given that was where Liverpool wished to return when replacing Arne Slot with the Basque coach this summer, Iraola’s 11th game in charge showed development is not confined only to Ngumoha.

Van Dijk said: “If you look at it from that perspective, it is like that. We train a lot, tactically as well, but because there are so many games you learn playing games and this was a test in that sense because Villarreal were good on the ball. They also rotated a lot so you have to find moments when you can press them and when you can win the ball high.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Is this squad used to that [pressing style] because I don’t think many players have been part of that? What the manager wants us to do is something which resonates with Liverpool and it is down to us to show it in each and every game. It’s not easy, it’s demanding, but if you want to win games and win games in the Liverpool way then we have to do it.

“The first half was obviously not good at all and the second half was solid and we turned it around and that’s a good sign. Now we have to get ready for Brighton, a super team, which is coming.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo asked for punishment ‘without mitigation’, then fought to cut it
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo successfully fought to reduce his punishment for walking out on a Portugal training camp, after saying publicly that his sanction should be imposed “without mitigating circumstances”.

After leaving the training camp in Denmark last month, Ronaldo said in a lengthy statement on social media that he should be punished as the Portuguese Football Federation saw fit and that his role as captain constituted “an aggravating factor”.

However, during the disciplinary council’s inquiry the 41-year-old put forward several arguments for cutting his punishment, including his clean disciplinary record in recent seasons and his services to football.

Ronaldo received a 30-day suspension and a €255 (£215) fine, and the document accompanying the ruling reveals he presented three arguments in mitigation: his disciplinary record this season and in the previous three seasons; his services to football including recognition for sporting merit; and his contribution to establishing the facts of the case.

To support these arguments, Ronaldo listed the club titles he has won and his achievements with the national team: the 2016 European Championship and two Nations League titles. His individual awards were also highlighted, including the fact that the Al-Nassr forward has won the Ballon d’Or five times. Beyond his achievements on the pitch, he mentioned the honours he had received from senior state officials.

The decision-makers accepted Ronaldo’s arguments concerning his achievements and services to the country, using them to halve his suspension and fine. The punishment was then halved again because Ronaldo had accepted responsibility for his actions.

Ronaldo’s suspension will be served in a period during which there are no international matches. It is unclear whether he intends to return to the national team – or whether the head coach, Jorge Jesus, will select him again.

The account of events provides a clearer picture of the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure from the training camp. After head coach Jesus held a press conference in which he reiterated that he was in charge of the team and that no player would influence his selection decisions, Ronaldo requested a vehicle from the FPF and set off for Copenhagen airport.

During the journey, he called the Portuguese federation’s president, Pedro Proença, and told him he was “not in the right frame of mind” to remain with the team.

“The defendant [Ronaldo] did not inform or provide prior justification to the federation or the men’s national team officials regarding his intention to leave the stadium and the training camp,” the ruling states. It says that between 30 September and 4 October, Ronaldo missed more than 30 team activities, including travel, training sessions and meals.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The federation says that Ronaldo’s promise on social media, after leaving the training camp, to tell his fans “the whole truth” brought further negative attention to the incident: “Given his prominence as a public figure on a global scale, the defendant could not have been unaware that his conduct, in the circumstances in which it occurred, would be subject to intense media scrutiny, as indeed it was.”

Ronaldo was therefore “expected to exercise particular caution in choosing the timing and manner in which he expressed his dissatisfaction with the manager’s decisions and conduct”. Instead, the player “further fuelled speculation and public curiosity by posting on Instagram on the very day he left Copenhagen, announcing that, ‘in due course’, he would tell ‘all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to his departure from the men’s senior national team’,” the inquiry concluded.

Portugal are scheduled to play Denmark again in their next game on 14 November in Braga.

Sports.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
Sports.content:
“I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.”

The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.”

Success did not originally look destined, when the Swede took charge 21 months ago, at a time when San Diego Wave were enduring something of an exodus of senior players; the United States defender Abby Dahlkemper’s sale to Bay FC in August 2024 and Alex Morgan’s retirement a month later were followed by the USA forward Jaedyn Shaw’s departing for North Carolina Courage and her international teammate Naomi Girma joining Chelsea in January 2025. A reconstruction was needed.

That is why, on a video call that winter, when Eidevall spoke to his players for the first time after taking charge, he began by quoting a proverb: if you want to go fast, go alone, but if you want to go far, go together. “My ideas are not worth anything if we don’t believe and buy into them altogether,” he says. “We focused everything on just building connections as human beings.” Detailed tactical discussions were initially kept to a minimum. They spent – as he recalls – around four weeks of their six-week pre-season focusing entirely on passing out from the back, to develop their style. Fast forward to the present day and it has paid off, with the Wave defenders Kristen McNabb and Kennedy Wesley being the division’s top two players for passes completed this season. More notable, though, has been the development of young players, such as the 18-year-olds Melanie Barcenas and Kimmi Ascanio.

“From 2024, when the club was not performing well on the pitch and it led to a complete rebuild, we had to find an edge, finding players that could fit into the way we wanted to play,” Eidevall says. “Back then it was a bit different to many other teams in the league, because the NWSL was seen as being dominated by athleticism and transitional play, which obviously then requires really fast players and maybe didn’t put a premium on technical supremacy.”

He adds that the club therefore eyed players who are “really, really good technically. We had some young, talented players already – that has given us a really good advantage because we’ve been able to develop players in a salary cap league. That’s huge, because if you only buy readymade players, you will run out of salary cap space pretty quickly.”

View image in fullscreen Jonas Eidevall took over at San Diego Wave in January 2025. Photograph: SPP /Alamy

It is not just the salary cap that differs in the NWSL, compared to Eidevall’s previous jobs at Arsenal and Rosengård. The broad competitiveness of the American league means that, despite being second in the table, San Diego have lost almost as many games this season as Eidevall’s Arsenal across three English campaigns, and he says: “This was new for me. In European leagues the top teams very rarely go two games in a row without winning. Here, even the team that wins the league might go through spells where they don’t pick up points, so the way you handle those moments becomes very important.

“Training [here] is also a challenge – sometimes it’s very hard to get 22 players because you have a limited roster size. The moment you start to have injuries … there’s no real second-team academy system like we have in Europe, where you can always have the numbers that you want. Here you might not, here you would like to do something XI v XI, but you have 18 players and you just have to be creative with how you coach.”

Trying to play entertaining football has been a target in a campaign during which they have already set new club records for regular-season wins and goals scored. They have done it with the second-highest average possession share in the division, more shots on target than any other team and while facing by far the fewest shots on target.

“That’s the most pleasing part, results through an identity rather than getting results the other way around,” Eidevall says. “The identity we have is to allow the players to be creative.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Eidevall has overseen a necessary overhaul of San Diego Wave’s squad. Photograph: San Diego Wave

We are speaking around two years after Eidevall resigned as Arsenal’s head coach on 15 October 2024, following a disappointing start to that season. In his three full campaigns at the helm in north London he had won two League Cups, reached a Champions League semi-final and secured a second-placed top-flight finish in 2022 – but was unable to win the WSL. Reflecting on what he learned from that spell, he says: “We had a lot of fluidity with how our wide players could play in Arsenal, which at times created too few central options. So, how do we get better central connections? How do we get more players central on the pitch? That was a long-term reflection on my time at Arsenal. And that’s also led to some tactical changes that we’ve done here with San Diego.”

There is an aspect of his Arsenal tenure that he is determined to take inspiration from at San Diego, with his team having secured a home playoff quarter-final at their 35,000-seater Snapdragon Stadium.

The 43-year-old fondly remembers the first sellout crowd for a women’s match at Arsenal’s 60,000-seater Emirates Stadium, for their Champions League semi-final against Wolfsburg in 2023: “We want to sell out Snapdragon Stadium and in order to do so we need to do exactly what we were doing at Arsenal – we need to create special experiences at the stadium,” he says. “That is what’s going to draw people into there. Yes, play exciting football, but we also need to play games that mean a lot to be there. The ripple effect of that, that’s so big.”

Sports.title: CHRIS WHEELER: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender. How much longer can Michael Carrick and his team sleepwalk through this wretched season?
Sports.content:
CHRIS WHEELER: Man United were insipid, lifeless and downright ugly in tame Como surrender. How much longer can Michael Carrick and his team sleepwalk through this wretched season?

As the full-time whistle blew on one of Manchester United’s most embarrassing nights in Europe, Michael Carrick walked over alone to the few away fans still left at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium and held up his hands in apology.

They had stood drenched for two hours, battered by the wind and rain that whipped off Lake Como. This has to be the most picturesque venues in the Champions League by some distance, but on a night like this it was downright ugly and so were United.

Carrick’s apology was reminiscent of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s farewell game at Watford in November 2021, which also ended in a humbling 4-1 defeat.

Solskjaer knew he was a dead man walking that day. If this proves to be Carrick’s last stand, what a lame surrender it was.

How much longer can this go on? How much longer can United sleepwalk through this wretched season as Carrick continues to grasp hopelessly for positives?

Statistically the fifth worst European defeat in United’s history was also Carrick’s fifth in 11 games this wretched season as they were torn apart by Como and the excellent Nico Paz.

Manchester United were completely outplayed by Como as they lost 4-1 to the Italian side

The dreadful result heaps further pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

This was an incredible night for Como, but one of the worst in United's European history

This was meant to be the biggest game in Como’s history and they played like it. Cesc Fabregas’ team are a credit to the former Arsenal midfielder and it’s not by chance that they lie fifth in Serie A.

But Manchester United coming to town is no longer what it was. This is a pathetic imitation of the teams that have represented this great club down the years.

The 700 fans who made the journey to Lombardy stood in one of the areas of this stadium exposed to the elements beneath Giuseppe Terragni’s Monumento ai Caduti that sits at the head of the lake. It means monument to the fallen, and how much further can United keep falling from here?

They were insipid. Lifeless. The confidence and self-belief has been sucked out of this team. It’s eight games since they last won, beating Sabah of Azerbaijan in this competition and recording their only clean sheet of the season.

Como 4-1 Man United: MATCH FACTS Como 1907 (4-2-3-1): Butez 6; Couto 7 (Smolcic 80, 6), Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8 (Dossena 80, 6); Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8 Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76) Booked: Kempf Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens 4; Dalot 3, De Ligt 3 (Amass 79, 5), Maguire 4, Mazraoui 3; Mount 3, Santos 4 (Baleba 46, 5); Mbeumo 4 (Lacey 86), Tielemans 4, Cunha 3 (Amad 46, 6); Fernandes 4 (Zirkzee 67, 6) Goal: Zirkzee (90+1) Booked: Santos, Baleba, Lacey Manager: Michael Carrick 3 Referee: Sven Jablonski 6

Shortly after the half hour mark, their supporters broke into a chorus of ‘attack, attack, attack’ which is never a good sign for any United manager.

From the chance that fell to Diogo Dalot in the opening seconds to Matheus Cunha’s tame effort on the stroke of half-time, they didn’t have another effort on goal in the first half.

Yes, Carrick was without nine senior players, forcing him to put Matthijs De Ligt into the starting line-up without playing a minute of football in the last 325 days due to a back injury, and name Jack Fletcher and Tynan Thompson on the bench even though both players had featured in the UEFA Youth League defeat to Como earlier in the day.

But that was no excuse for another performance that left you wondering just what these United players are doing on the training pitch all week – and what Carrick is saying to them.

If there was concrete evidence that they simply aren’t learning or progressing, it came after two minutes here. A week after United conceded after 50 seconds to Atletico Madrid in Spain, they were behind again.

No sooner had Dalot curled an effort wide after mistakenly creating the opportunity for himself by miscontrolling Cunha’s pass than Paz converted a similar chance at the other end.

United had been warned about the gifted Argentine, but you wouldn’t have know it by the way Harry Maguire stood off the 22-year-old when he received a pass from Lucas Da Cunha inside the box. Paz looked up, picked his spot and guided the ball beyond Senne Lammens.

He was simply too much for United to handle. Andrey Santos was booked for hacking him down with a crude challenge, Cunha resorted to similar tactics, and Lammens was relieved to see the offside flag go up after fouling Como’s No.10 in the box.

Carrick made changes at half-time, sending on Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for Cunha and Santos so that Bryan Mbeumo could play through the middle. He also asked his full-backs, Dalot and Mazraoui, to switch sides.

Argentina wonderkid Nico Paz was Como's star as he scored twice and laid on an assist

Paz put his side ahead in under two minutes after United's defence mistakenly stood off him

United couldn't match Como's intensity and were insipid and error-ridden, which included Carlos Baleba giving the ball away for their second goal

United were awful and Carrick even hooked captain Bruno Fernandes in the second half

Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in added time but it was barely acknowledged

It’s another sign of the growing crisis around Carrick that it only made things worse as United conceded another early goal.

Martin Baturina had gone close twice before half-time, so it was no surprise to see him extend Como’s lead. Paz was the architect this time with a fine pass to Baturina who got away from De Ligt and powered a shot past Lammens.

United were three down eight minutes later. Baleba gave the ball away to Paz close to halfway and no United player looked like getting near him as he surged downfield and finished clinically.

Carrick’s misery was complete in the 76th minute when Jacobo Ramon got the fourth. It was a measure of the brimming confidence in Fabregas’ side that his centre-back felt able to charge forward in open play and meet a left-wing cross from substitute Kaiki Bruno. No-one had tracked Ramon and he beat Lammens with a thumping header.

Carrick sent on teenagers Harry Amass and Shea Lacey which felt like a pathetically response to a pathetic performance, even though Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation from close-range in the 91st minute. The damage was done.

As Carrick and his players flew home on Wednesday night, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the United board were left with a decision to make about where they go from here.

Sports.title: 'It doesn't look good': Mikel Arteta sparks fears over Bukayo Saka injury after Arsenal winger limped off during 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
'It doesn't look good': Mikel Arteta sparks fears over Bukayo Saka injury after Arsenal winger limped off during 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta admitted he is worried about the injury suffered by winger Bukayo Saka in last night’s thrilling 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.

Saka went off with a thigh injury just ten minutes into his team’s Champions League game with the German champions at the Allianz Arena.

Arteta said: ‘It doesn’t look good at all but we will have to wait and see.

‘They [the medical staff] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news.’

Arsenal led through Saka’s replacement Eberechi Eze in the first-half but the brilliant Harry Kane hauled Bayern back into the game and eventually the lead with a first-half assist for Alphonso Davies and then a second-half penalty of his own.

Declan Rice grabbed an 82nd minute equaliser to send Arsenal home content but Arteta hinted that Kane – a Ballon d’Or contender ahead of next week’s ceremony in London – still sets the standards for others to follow.

Mikel Arteta has claimed that Bukayo Saka's thigh problem 'does not look good'

Saka limped off in the first half of Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich on Wednesday night

‘The pass he made for the first goal, that’s the level,’ said the Arsenal manager.

England captain Kane has now scored 58 Champions League goals and is only one away from matching Cristiano Ronaldo’s record of scoring in 11 consecutive Champions League matches.

Asked by TNT about his England team-mate’s Ballon D’Or chances, Rice said: ‘He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves. The year he has had has been remarkable.

‘When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.

‘He is ridiculous, such a good player and I am lucky I can play with him, not so lucky I have to play against him.’

The injury to Saka could prove a real blow to Arteta after the winger's impressive start to the campaign in all competitions.

The England international has scored four goals in ten matches this season, while also bagging an assist in the Champions League.

However, the problem he picked up at the Allianz Arena is his latest in a string of injury issues he has faced over the last few years.

Saka admitted to playing through pain of a persistent achilles problem during Arsenal's final run-in en route to the Premier League last term. That led to limited minutes during England's World Cup campaign in the summer.

The attacker missed 15 games in all competitions last season due to the achilles issue and a hamstring problem. Saka also missed 25 games the season prior due to injury.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's new-look team continue to make strides as Unai Emery shows why he is one of the world's great managers after 3-1 win over Viking, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Two questions sprang to mind on a night of contrasting fortunes for Premier League clubs in the Champions League.

First, why have Manchester United never made a concerted attempt to bring in Unai Emery as manager? And even if they did, why on Earth would the Aston Villa boss choose to move to Old Trafford right now?

Emery is approaching his fourth anniversary in charge at Villa Park. He took over with the club on the fringes of a relegation battle and since then, he has led them to Champions League qualification twice, as well as lifting the Europa League last season.

Not to mention 12 straight home wins in Europe, something only Emery, Pep Guardiola and Sir Alex Ferguson have achieved.

Not long after United had fallen apart at Como, Emery was guiding Villa to their third straight victory in the season’s Champions League.

Ross Barkley’s header and Emi Buendia’s penalty made it 2-0 at half-time, and the excellent Alysson’s cross flew in off Henrik Heggheim for the third goal. Peter Christiansen replied late on for Viking.

Aston Villa thumped Norwegian side Viking 3-1 in the Champions League at Villa Park

The comfortable victory took Unai Emery's side to joint-top of the league phase standings

Villa are joint-top of the league phase with a maximum nine points, which was good enough to reach the play-off round in some cases last term. There are 15 points still to play for.

While United have moved from one baffling appointment to another, sacking Erik ten Hag to hire Ruben Amorim and then replacing the Portuguese with Michael Carrick, Emery has been right under their noses.

But they never made a serious bid to poach the Premier League’s best pound-for-pound manager and if that boat has now sailed, it would serve them right.

Aston Villa’s Sir Alex

In terms of the control he has, Emery is the closest there is to Ferguson in the modern Premier League.

Few managers’ influence stretches across a club as Emery’s does and just like Ferguson, Emery is showing he is comfortable with dismantling a successful team and rebuilding it.

Villa lost six players who started last season’s Europa League Final and their prospects were uncertain. When Emery’s men were hammered at Brighton on the opening day of this season, it seemed they may have changed too much too soon.

Not a bit of it. There will still be bumps in the road, but already Johan Manzambi – absent here – looks one of the signings of the summer, as does Nicolas Jackson.

Ibrahim Mbaye will only improve, Joao Gomes is growing into his role and now Leon Goretzka is fully fit, he will surely have a significant contribution to make, while Alysson is coming to the boil nicely. Zion Suzuki looks an ideal replacement for Emi Martinez in goal.

There are still some doubts about the defence in Ezri Konsa’s absence but Villa’s attacking options are the envy of most across Europe.

Villa's new-look side is starting to come together despite a significant summer overhaul

Underestimated Emery

Despite winning 12 major trophies, Emery still does not receive the recognition he deserves in some quarters.

According to one live blog, BBC summariser and former England defender Matthew Upson described Emery as ‘a safe pair of hands for any club’. Safe pair of hands?

Seriously? With all respect, we are talking about one of the world’s great managers, not someone hired to steer a relegation-threatened side to mid-table.

Emery has coached some of the world’s best players and even improved them. Working under Emery, Youri Tielemans was one of the league’s best midfielders last season. Just look at him now as he struggles under a vastly inferior coach at United.

Emery is comfortably the best-paid employee at Villa. His annual salary of about £15million puts him in the top bracket of world managers and they think him worth every penny.

Unai Emery continues to work wonders and he is one of the world's greatest managers

The odd man out

Alejandro Garnacho continues to have a confusing time at Villa Park. The former United winger, on loan from Chelsea, was a late substitute here and looked lively.

He has yet to start a game though and doubts remain about how much Villa really want him.

The Argentine may start in the Carabao Cup at Bournemouth next week but barring an unexpected series of events, it seems unlikely his £43m permanent move will be triggered. January promises to be interesting for him.

But Alejandro Garnacho is having a confusing time at Villa Park and his future looks uncertain

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars left the Gunners defence exposed too often? Who pulled the strings for Mikel Arteta's men? And who had a 'quiet' night?

Declan Rice stole the limelight from Harry Kane as Arsenal hit back to snatch a thrilling 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in a heavyweight Champions League clash at the Allianz Arena.

Gunners midfielder Rice lashed low beyond Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer eight minutes from time to extend his side’s unbeaten start to this season’s competition following back-to-back wins over Napoli and Lille.

Kane was on course to claim the winner after registering his 16th goal in 23 career outings against Arsenal by converting a 61st-minute penalty following Jurrien Timber’s handball.

The England captain earlier produced a sublime assist for Alphonso Davies to cancel out Eberechi Eze’s opener.

But in their biggest test since losing last season’s final to Paris St Germain on penalties, Mikel Arteta’s Premier League champions responded well to deservedly return home with a share of the spoils.

Here ISAAN KHAN rates Arsenal's top performers on the night.

David Raya - 7

Top save to deny Dayot Upamecano from point-blank range. Impressive with his fast distribution to kickstart counter-attacks.

Jurrien Timber - 4

Out of position for Alphonso Davies’ goal and caught out throughout the match. Conceded a penalty for a handball following Harry Kane's strike.

Jurrien Timber endured a difficult night and was caught out of position for Bayern's opener

Ezri Konsa - 5

Tasked with keeping tabs on Kane, yet the England man found ways to find space. A couple of strong, important blocks, but his positioning ought to be better.

Gabriel - 6

Strong at the back and up for the fight. Stepped up when required, not deterred by the task at hand.

Riccardo Calafiori - 5

A constant threat in the final third but, like his fellow full back Timber, he left the backline exposed too often.

Martin Odegaard - 8

Pulled the strings for Arteta's side and played some classy passes, including a sublime assist for Eberechi Eze. The Norwegian is hard to stop when he’s in this mood.

Martin Odegaard delivered another impressive display as the Arsenal captain rediscovers his best form

Declan Rice - 8

Energetic in the middle of the park and covered lots of ground. His corner-kicks caused havoc in the Bayern area and struck a well-taken goal.

Bruno Guimaraes - 6

All-action display. Put in a number of crucial challenges and was a threat going forwards. Had a header well-saved by Manuel Neuer.

Bukayo Saka - 5

Pulled up with what looked like a quad injury in the opening 10 minutes, signalling to the bench that he would not be able to continue. Massive blow for Arsenal, who will be sweating over the severity of Saka's blow.

Kai Havertz - 4

A quiet night with the German unable to create openings in threatening areas.

It was a quiet night for Kai Havertz, who struggled to make an impact

Noni Madueke - 5

Direct and tried to make things happen. Thoese opportunities dwindled in the second-half as Bayern grabbed control of the tie.

Substitutions:

Eberechi Eze - 7

Deserves credit after an impressive, goalscoring cameo following recent scrutiny.

Viktor Gyokeres - 7

Myles Lewis-Skelly - 6

Manager: Mikel Arteta - 7

A good move to bring on Viktor Gyokeres, who came off the bench to assist Rice. Will be pleased to walk away with a point.

Boss Mikel Arteta will be pleased with his side's performance and the point gained in Germany

BAYERN MUNICH (4-2-3-1): Neuer 7; Laimer 6, Upamecano 7, Min-Jae 6 (Tah 6, 46mins), Stanisic 6; Pavlovic 6, Bischof 6; Gnabry 6 (Karl 68, 6), Saibari 6 (Diaz 6, 68), Davies 8; Kane 8.

Referee: Davide Massa - 6

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Gunners take huge step in the right direction, as Declan Rice earns point that means so much more in Mikel Arteta's bid to build dynasty
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal: Gunners take huge step in the right direction, as Declan Rice earns point that means so much more in Mikel Arteta's bid to build dynasty

A draw in Bavaria will not stand out in the list of achievements carved out stubbornly by Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal as he has taken them from nowhere to somewhere over the last six years or so. But the Arsenal manager will know what this night means, nevertheless.

This is a season that must see Arsenal break fresh ground if they are to become the team we all feel they can be. They know they have questions to answer and they know what they are. They are about style and the ability to bring about repeat success. They are about building a domestic dynasty and winning things in Europe.

At times Arsenal look to be quite close to that but at other times – such as in winning so drearily with one shot on target at Nottingham Forest on Sunday – they look to be rather too far away.

So, yes, this felt like a big step in the right direction. An enterprising attacking performance – Arsenal could have scored four or five goals – against a team that hardly ever loses in its own stadium and then, a come from behind draw just when it seemed everything may be lost.

The feeling the Arsenal team will have had when celebrating Declan Rice’s late equaliser down beneath their own fans here will have been one that should propel them forwards.

Bayern are not used to teams doing that to them here and when the ball flew across Manuel Neuer and into the far corner you could feel the air being sucked out of this cavernous bowl and up into the night sky.

Declan Rice smashed a powerful low effort to make it 2-2 late on against Bayern Munich

Rice latched onto a through ball and his shot had too much for Manuel Neuer

Harry Kane had put Bayern Munich in front from the penalty spot in the second half

For Bayern had thrown their best at Arsenal here. Harry Kane had done so too. Arsenal had led midway through the first half through Eberechi Eze but as time wore on Bayern’s rapid counters threatened to become too much. Defeat beckoned.

Kane – as irrepressibly as inspirational as ever – had supplied a world class assist for Alphonso Davies in the first half and then, on the hour, a penalty of his own.

A loss here would have not been a disaster for Arsenal but it would have felt telling. It would have given their many critics further ammunition with which to do them down. Not good enough in Europe. Flat track bullies. Stuck in the mud. Not moving forwards.

So it was a good night for Arsenal if not a perfect one. An injury to Bukayo Saka, for example, was not on Arteta’s wish list. He was clipped from behind in the tenth minute and went down holding the back of his knee.

That was the end of his evening and the injury will be a worry. The only consolation to Arteta will have been that his replacement took his opportunity.

This has not been a stellar season for Eze but you would not have known it watching him drive a pass from Martin Odegaard across Manuel Neuer and in to the far corner with his left foot in the 25th minute. The supply from Odegaard was exemplary but it needed a finish to match.

At that point, Arsenal were worth the lead, even if Bayern had attacked on the counter to good effect.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya had to save sharply from Serge Gnabry after one such break while a lofted Kane pass a couple of minutes before Eze’s goal could have led to something had Ismael Saibari not applied such a clumsy touch.

Arsenal, meanwhile, had their own moments to ponder. Twice from corners they had opportunities at the far post but Riccardo Calafiori and Bruno Guimaraes couldn’t take them.

Alphonso Davies equalised for the German side with a tidy finish past David Raya

Eberechi Eze fired a composed effort past Manuel Neuer to break the deadlock in Munich

After a slow start, it had become a good game. Arsenal were purposeful and ambitious if a little too square across the back at times. Eventually, they were caught out.

Kane’s pass inside Jurrien Timber from just inside the Arsenal half could not have been more geometrically perfect had he used a set square and Davies ran on to open his body and beat Raya quite comfortably.

Kane’s goal – his 58th in the competition – was eventually to arrive on the hour and arrived after a spell of Bayern pressure. Before that, though, Arsenal had another couple of huge moments.

Almost immediately after half-time, Neuer produced a stunning save to push a Gabriel header up on to the crossbar from another corner. At the other end Raya denied Dayot Upamecano in similarly brilliant fashion.

It was an increasingly engaging game but one that Bayern were beginning to enjoy rather more. Their forays into the attacking third had become more regular and brought with them a greater menace.

Kane, for his part, was showcasing his full repertoire, spending as much time in deep position as he was through the middle.

There were concerning scenes for the Gunners when Saka limped off early on in the game

This was a draw worth far more than the solitary point for Mikel Arteta's side

But he was in the right place on the hour to meet a cross from Konrad Laimer and when his shot struck the sprawling Jurrien Timber on the arm a penalty was the only decision available. Kane took it and, after a little stutter, slotted it to Raya’s right with the keeper committed in the other direction.

Bayern almost sealed the game soon after only for Laimer’s right foot shot to miss Raya’s right hand post.

So Arsenal remained in it and – with Viktor Gyokeres on to change the shape of their attacks – they eventually took what they deserved. The move down the right side was slick and Rice’s finish – after a one-two with the big striker – was perfect, across Neuer with power.

The celebrations that followed were about much more than a single Champions League point.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag reveals failed plot to reunite with Alejandro Garnacho at Leverkusen as ex-Man United boss admits out-of-sorts star is a 'little bit selfish' and 'needs love' amid Aston Villa exile
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has leapt to the defence of Alejandro Garnacho, revealing he tried to sign the winger during his ill-fated spell at Bayer Leverkusen. Garnacho made his transition from United's academy into the first-team under Ten Hag with the Dutchman handing him his debut. Their time together peaked in the 2024 FA Cup final 2-1 win over Manchester City with Garnacho scoring the opening goal. Ten Hag was sacked as United boss in October 2024, before returning to management with Bayer Leverkusen in the summer of 2025. However, he lasted only two Bundesliga matches before he was dismissed - a Bundesliga record. The 56-year-old's fortunes since that FA Cup final win mirror that of Garnacho who was sold to Chelsea for £40million in August 2025. He only lasted a season at the Blues after underwhelming before joining Aston Villa on loan, where he is down the pecking order of manager Unai Emery. But speaking about Garnacho, Ten Hag labelled him as an 'amazing player' who can do 'incredible things', but warned to get the best out of him he has to remain disciplined. 'I regret where he is now. I told him, "Come to Leverkusen". But luckily he didn't. He wanted to stay in England. I understand, the best league, so he denied,' he told The Athletic of an attempt to sign the Argentine in the summer of 2025 before he joined Chelsea. Erik ten Hag (right) has spoken highly about Alejandro Garnacho after their time at Man United Now at Aston Villa on loan from Chelsea, the winger has struggled for first-team minutes so far 'He's a character, you have to manage him, but I had a strong connection with him. 'But it's also up to him, of course, but he needs a coach, a particular coach, who will give him trust, who will give him love. He needs the love, definitely. But he's an amazing player. What's so special about him is he can run all day, high volume at really high speed, all game, back and forward. 'Sometimes his head is not on defending. So mentally, his mindset, you have to make sure he is focused and disciplined and does the job every transition, but he's capable of doing it and attacking-wise he can go forward and do incredible things, making dribbles, finishing. He can do the final pass, but sometimes he's a little bit selfish but you balance this.' Since joining Aston Villa on loan, Garnacho has only made four substitute appearances for a total of 42 minutes. His last appearance under Emery came in the 6-0 win over Fenerbahce in the Europa League on October 15 - where he came on with 11 minutes remaining. Despite that cameo, the 22-year-old was omitted from their matchday squad for Saturday's 2-1 victory at Newcastle United. He hasn't played in the Premier League since his substitute appearance in a 0-0 draw at Hull City on September 5. Ten Hag's thoughts on his former United player comes after he revealed his frustration at the club's hierarchy's decision to sell Scott McTominay to Napoli for £25m in the summer of 2024 against his wishes. 'They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep.' Keeping McTominay at Old Trafford was one of those promises, according to Ten Hag. The Scot was sold to Napoli for £25million in the summer of 2024 and has since gone on to become one of the top midfielders in Italy, becoming a fan favourite at the Serie A club after steering them to the title in his first season. He even earned a Ballon d'Or nomination and was compared to Argentina icon Diego Maradona by adoring Napoli fans. On McTominay, Ten Hag said: 'That's why I got disappointed. In Ibiza, we agreed. I said, "No selling Scott McTominay". We would go aligned in the transfer window. 'I make an argument, a reason: we don't have scoring abilities. Scott brings scoring abilities and great mentality. He has United in all his veins. So when they bring up the subject, "No". And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.' McTominay's transfer to Napoli was used by United's chiefs to raise funds for £42m midfielder Manuel Ugarte, who has struggled to impress since his arrival. The Uruguayan, who is currently out injured with an anterior cruciate ligament tear he suffered at the World Cup, was mostly used as a squad player under Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick last season.

Sports.title: Man United captain Bruno Fernandes questions Michael Carrick's tactics in wake of Champions League humiliation in Como - after boss was left 'angry' by team's display and apologised to supporters
Sports.content:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Michael Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the club’s Champions League humiliation in Como. United were humbled 4-1 as their wretched season hit a new low and Carrick, who expressed his 'anger' at the performance, suffered his fifth defeat in 11 games. A week after Lisandro Martinez had taken aim at his Old Trafford bosses – and director of football Jason Wilcox in particular – Fernandes broke ranks to question why United were so passive again. He said: ‘It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence.’ Asked if he meant that Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: ‘That's on the manager and staff to say, not me. ‘Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable. As you saw with Como, the centre back was coming to mark me in my own half. We need to do that as a team but we were unable to. Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to hit out at manager Michael Carrick Fernandes expressed his frustration after Carrick's side were thrashed 4-1 by Como ‘A team that plays through the middle with small connections, if you give them too much time and space then they can hurt you out wide.’ Having conceded to Atletico after 50 seconds last week, United were behind within two minutes as Como star Nico Paz struck the first of his two goals. ‘It's not the first time, we started on the wrong foot, and they scored very early,’ said Fernandes. ‘Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way. ‘Conceding early makes us go into game with a mood of defeat, it's difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.’ Fernandes was surprisingly substituted by Carrick midway through the second half, and the United skipper shook his head in frustration as he made his way back to the dugout. Carrick refused to be drawn on Fernandes' post-match outburst but admitted he was left 'angry' by his team's performance in Italy. He said: 'I'm angry to be honest. My whole life is wrapped around this. I didn't like what I've seen tonight.' Carrick added: 'There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win.' On their performance more widely, the former United midfielder said: 'It was more than disappointing. I think everyone has to take responsibility for that. 'I'll 100 per cent take responsibility for the overall team and performance; that stops with me and I accept that. But as a supporter of this club for so long and I care so much about this club, to see a performance like that is unacceptable. 'A lot of it is the motivation, intensity and purpose you have to bring in a game of football and we didn't bring that today. You can't turn it on and off or choose when you perform or give absolutely everything. Until you do that you're not going to win enough football matches.' Fernandes was substituted in the second half and looked frustrated as he left the pitch Carrick apologised to United's travelling fans after the match and held his hands up in their direction having marched across the pitch, before he repeated this stance when speaking to the media. He added: 'I care an unbelievable amount about these supporters. They're the heartbeat of this football club and always will be. 'For them to travel, I have to apologise for the performance and everything they've done to get here tonight. To watch a performance like that I feel for them. There's no excuses for that and it's totally unacceptable.' NOW READ: Como 4-1 Manchester United PLAYER RATINGS: Which United stars were totally anonymous?

Sports.title: Como 4-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Which stars fare worst in our most damning ratings EVER after Michael Carrick's side sink to new low?
Sports.content:
Things went from bad to worse at Manchester United as their 'fresh start' under Michael Carrick began with a disastrous 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Como.

In the pouring rain, United capitulated under the pressure put on by Cesc Fabregas' young guns and they were behind inside two minutes in what was the start of a very long evening.

Anastasios Douvikas got himself on the scoresheet, teed up by man of the match Nico Paz, who scored twice, before Jacobo Ramon compounded United's misery with a fourth.

By the time Joshua Zirkzee held his run to stay onside to score a consolation in stoppage time, there was barely a flicker of a smile on the faces of anyone wearing United white.

At that stage, United's wounded supporters had long left in their droves, furious at a performance that suggests this United group are only heading in one direction: backwards.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on a truly hapless Manchester United performance in Italy...

Manchester United have a lot of soul searching to do after a shambolic defeat to Como

Nico Paz ran United ragged with a brace and an assist as United's season gets even worse

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens – 4

What is he meant to do when those in front of him are so hopeless? The defence was about as solid as a house of cards in a gentle breeze. Genuinely hopeless and as long as that continues, Lammens is on a hiding to nothing.

Diogo Dalot – 3

Wasted a golden opportunity after a deflection fell at his feet in the box, shooting a whisker wide of the post. That proved costly when Como scored less than a minute later. Works hard and was willing at right back, where he started, and left back, where he went at half time. Some at United feel Dalot is unfairly criticised when the chips are down, but he was miles away from the required quality here.

Matthijs de Ligt – 3

His first United appearance in 325 days and there was so much hope that the Dutchman could pick up where he left off. The positive is that he came through it unscathed. By the time he went off, it was a disastrous night for United and De Ligt was far from blameless after losing sight of Douvikas before stumbling as Como made it 2-0.

Harry Maguire – 4

Made a super last-ditch, sliding challenge to deny a second goal but it all proved in vain. Maguire called out the team for not showing enough bravery away to Leeds and this as a response was disastrous.

He was the best of the back-line but that's not saying much. Looks one of very few who can actually handle the pressure and navigate the storm now.

Harry Maguire called out the bravery of this team after Leeds and it didn't have any impact

Noussair Mazraoui – 3

Ran ragged at both left back, where he started, and at right back, where he played in the second half. It was Mazraoui who was at fault for Leeds' equaliser at the weekend and his press to close out in the lead up to Como's second goal was dreadful. Looked like a rabbit in headlights by the time Kaiki, gifted the freedom of Como by Mazraoui, crossed in for the hosts' fourth.

Mason Mount – 3

Has won this competition and has plenty of experience at the level but looked way short of the necessary quality required as this youthful Como team made him look distinctly average. Constantly came out second best in duels.

Andrey Santos – 4

Found himself completely overrun in the middle of the park – he wasn't alone in that – and was hooked at half-time after a rash slide to bring down Nico Paz brought a yellow card. Never got close to the speed of the game. The fact it was only 1-0 when he went off goes in his favour.

Bryan Mbeumo – 4

Has looked best at centre forward and so, naturally, he was deployed wide off the right, a position he doesn't ever seem to thrive in. Made a couple of smart runs but chances were at a premium and he was marginalised.

Bryan Mbeumo was pushed out on to the right and it massively limited what he is good at

Youri Tielemans – 4

Keeps starting matches but this one was one where it was easy to forget he was playing. Totally anonymous.

Matheus Cunha – 3

Another who was totally anonymous. Had one touch in the Como box, didn't create a single chance, and had just one shot off target before he was hooked at half-time alongside Santos. Been in and out of the side of late and this didn't do anything to improve his odds of more starts.

Bruno Fernandes – 4

Shook his head as he was taken off just after an hour into this one-sided contest but the truth is his performances have been way below the levels he has previously shown he can reach and he could have few complaints at coming off.

This false-nine experiment they have used in the past two games isn't yielding successful results.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 2

Spoke about a 'fresh start' after the draw at Leeds and then saw his side get totally dominated by a quicker, hungrier and better coached team. This was alarming mostly because United never looked remotely threatening, never mind threatening to pull off a positive result.

Michael Carrick is going to be under enormous pressure now as he bids to keep his job

SUBS

Amad (for Matheus Cunha, 46min) – 6

The brightest player in a United shirt. Looked to actually make stuff happen, and it was his ball in to Zirkzee that led to the late consolation.

Carlos Baleba (for Andrey Santos, 46) – 5

Catastrophic error to concede possession to Nico Paz as he broke to score a third. Did at least add some physicality that is severely lacking in this team. United cannot start matches going forward without him.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Bruno Fernandes, 67)

Scored in what was basically the only positive on a sobering night. Ended his drought.

Harry Amass (for Matthijs de Ligt, 79)

Shea Lacey (for Bryan Mbeumo, 86)

Como (4-2-3-1)

Butez 6; Couto 7, Ramon 7, Kempf 6, Valle 6; Milla 7, Perrone 8; Da Cunha 7, Paz 9 (Ricci 80), Baturina 7 (Caqueret 64, 7); Douvikas 8

Goals: Paz (2, 57), Douvikas (49), Ramon (76)

Manager: Cesc Fabregas 8

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits back at Bruno Fernandes comments in extraordinary press conference

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has responded to some veiled criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes in the wake of the Red Devils' humbling by Como

View 2 Images Carrick hit back at Fernandes in an extraordinary press conference (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick hit back at captain Bruno Fernandes after the Manchester United skipper blasted a 'decision from staff' following the Red Devils' lamentable defeat at Como.

‌



‌



United were hammered 4-1 by Cesc Fabregas' side in a result that has plunged Carrick's future into doubt. His team have won just twice in 11 games so far this term.

‌



Fernandes said the coaching staff had opted not to adopt a man-to-man marking policy in the game, suggesting it contributed to the heavy defeat.

‌



"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave a bit of space in behind and then try to get the ball in the first moment to wait for them, to give them the ball," the Portuguese captain told TNT Sports.

"But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated.

"And then, when we recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work."

‌



But Carrick has hit back, suggesting Fernandes' comments are not accurate. "We actually half-pressed man-to-man the second half and then conceded a goal from that," he said.

"And there's a little bit on whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

‌



Carrick took aim at his side's effort, while accepting the buck stops with him.

View 2 Images Fernandes had aimed a veiled dig at Carrick

‌



"We might win, we might lose, but the way we went about it tonight, I wouldn't say everyone, but the way we went about it in some ways tonight wasn't acceptable. And I just wanted to let the fans know that I feel for them, for sure," he added.

"It wasn't just the goals, if I'm totally honest. It was the manner and the way we played at times, in the way we went about it, that was the difficult thing to watch for me.

‌



"It's not about playing for me, it's about playing for this football club. It's the responsibility that comes with being in the position; I'm responsible for the football club and the supporters.

"I'm giving my best, absolute best all the time, I care about it. My whole life's wrapped around it. I genuinely give everything that I possibly can."

Sports.title: Man City charges: Fresh investigation confirmed as EFL 'ready to agree' punishment
Sports.content:
All the latest news on Manchester City's guilty verdict ahead of their appeal hearing, with the club now expected to receive a 'huge points deduction' and a fine

At the end of September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found guilty on all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between 2009/10 and 2017/18. It was revealed that City had artificially inflated revenue by more than £900million through so-called 'sham' sponsorship deals.

City, however, have vehemently denied any wrongdoing and submitted an appeal against the ruling on October 1. In an official statement, the club maintained they are "innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League" and claim they possess "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" to support their position.

Nevertheless, The Daily Mail have reported that the 'most likely' outcome is a three-pronged punishment for City, with the club expected to receive a 'points deduction which will guarantee relegation' and a 'huge fine'.

It's suggested that the sanction could include an additional points deduction that would virtually ensure City remain in the Championship for at least one further season, though the EFL would not be compelled to accept that penalty for one of their clubs. However, it's understood they would be prepared to agree to the points deduction.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes points finger at 'decision from Man Utd staff' after Como thrashing
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes points finger at 'decision from Man Utd staff' after Como thrashing

Manchester United were humiliated by Como in the Champions League, suffering back-to-back defeats in the competition

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes speaking to TNT Sports

Bruno Fernandes has questioned Manchester United's coaching staff's decision not to adopt a man-to-man pressing approach during their humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como. Michael Carrick's side endured a nightmare start, conceding inside the opening two minutes before finding themselves 3-0 down before the hour mark.

‌



‌



Nico Paz struck twice, while Anastasios Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon also got on the scoresheet to pile further pressure on the Red Devils. Joshua Zirkzee scored a consolation goal in the 90th minute, but the damage had already been done.

‌



United's travelling supporters had seen enough by the 76th minute, with some spotted leaving the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium shortly after their side conceded a fourth goal. The emphatic victory will go down as a historic night for Cesc Fabregas' side, who secured their second win of the Champions League campaign in stunning fashion.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Man Utd transfer plans being put in place as injury timeline emerges for Benjamin Sesko READ MORE :

Erik ten Hag identifies the off-pitch area Man Utd lag behind rivals with INEOS dig READ MORE :

Carrick's men were dominated from start to finish, with the United boss going over to apologise to the travelling supporters immediately after full-time. Speaking after the match, Fernandes was asked about the lack of cohesion as a group after he also endured a tough evening, having been hooked after just 66 minutes.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave a bit of space in behind and then try to get the ball in the first moment to wait for them, to give them the ball," the Portuguese captain told TNT Sports.

‌



"But sometimes when you give too much the ball [away] to these teams, they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot which makes people get frustrated. And then, when we recover the ball, the legs and the brain are much more difficult to make it work."

When asked whether the decision not to press had ultimately cost the team, the midfielder added: "That's on the manager and the staff to see. That's not on me, I just said that I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure.

‌



"Try to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable as they did to us. Their centre-back was coming to mark me all the way into my own half. I think sometimes we had to do that as a team and we were not really able to do it."

On the match, Fernandes reiterated: "Obviously it's not the first time, and I think again. we started with the wrong foot - they scored very early. Not much pressure on the ball, not really many good moments without the ball. It's many things not going our way.

‌



View 2 Images It was a tough night for Man United

"Conceding the goal very early, makes us feel going into the game already in a mood for defeat and it's very difficult to get out of that at the moment, without being ourselves and trying to push and be brave, trying to have the ball."

‌



Ahead of the match, Carrick faced questions about his future but insisted he had the full backing of the club's hierarchy.

"I don't need any reassurance," Carrick told a news conference on Tuesday. "It's pretty clear. I know the role, I know my responsibilities.

‌



"I don't need anyone else to tell me that or tell me when it's going well or when it needs to be better. I know that myself. I know the realities and I've got no problem with that.

"I know we've got to win football games for everything to flow and everything to fall into place. That's the great thing about it, you know? We can do something about it."

‌



Pressure is mounting with Carrick's future hanging in the balance after United managed just two wins across the Champions League and Premier League so far this season.

Sunday's home clash against Bournemouth now looms as a potentially defining moment for the under-fire manager.

Sports.title: John Gosden performs U-turn to rule Ombudsman out of Breeders' Cup Turf
Sports.content:
John Gosden performs U-turn to rule Ombudsman out of Breeders' Cup Turf

John Gosden has decided against running Ombudsman in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland, opting instead for a tentative plan to target the Japan Cup in November after the horse's Champion Stakes win at Ascot

View 2 Images William Buick riding Ombudsman (all blue) to win the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

Ombudsman, brilliant winner of the Champion Stakes at Ascot, will not have his swansong at the Breeders' Cup after a U-turn by trainer John Gosden.

‌



‌



In the wake of the Godolphin horse's defeat of last year's world's best racehorse, Calandagan at Ascot, Gosden had indicated that Ombudsman would tackle 1m4f for the first time in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland, before probably heading to stud next year.

‌



However, in an abrupt change of mind, the Newmarket trainer has now concluded that the race, 14 days after the Champion Stakes, will come too soon, and he is now floating the idea of a tilt at the Japan Cup instead.

‌



Gosden said: "It's very simple, the horse ran four days ago at Ascot and he would have to work tomorrow, get on a plane for a cross-Atlantic flight, quarantine and it's not fair to ask him to do that then ask him to run back within 14 days with a long journey in the middle.

"In fairness, we felt having discussed it with everyone, we shouldn't be trying to do that with him after he ran such a brilliant race in the Champion Stakes and we could consider the Japan Cup now.

‌



"There's plenty of time to that now in November, but to rush him over to America and put him through that we didn't think was in the best interests of the horse."

View 2 Images John Gosden: considering the Japan Cup for Ombudsman (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

Article continues below

He went on: "Japan would be a tentative plan and no more than that. It's the only other race this year he could really run in and an important international race, so to that extent it's a tentative plan.

"After that we're probably talking retirement and it would have been nice to go to America, we wanted to go and do it because we like the Breeders' Cup a lot, but the horse has to come first."
