World.title: Hyron Andrews’s wife breaks silence: ‘Unimaginable pain’
World.content:
Hyron Andrews’s American wife, Maighlin, has broken her silence following his shock death last Friday. Her emotional comments come as the Lions player’s cause of death has been officially released.

The couple wed in 2022 and have welcomed two sons since.

HYRON ANDREWS’S WIFE BREAKS SILENCE

On her Facebook account, Hyron Andrews’s wife, Maighlin, posted a tribute to the late Lions player who collapsed and died last Friday in France ahead of the team’s game against La Rochelle.



Maighlin, a US citizen, shared: “I’m not sure if there will ever be enough words to describe how much you mean to me, our boys, and your family, friends, and teammates all over the world. You were the absolute BEST father, and they were your everything. I know your proudest achievement was our family.

“I’m so so grateful that we got to have you for the time we did, though the pain of having our time cut short is unlike anything I thought was possible. We had so many plans, so much life left to live, and so many things to experience. I feel so blessed for all we got to do together in our short time.

Maighlin recalled meeting Hyron Andrews in Durban a decade ago, when he was playing for the Sharks, and she was studying in South Africa as part of a university exchange programme.



The couple would endure a six-year-long distance relationship before finally getting engaged in Ireland in 2021.

Maighlin moved to Durban in 2022, and the couple wed in Michigan in the US the following year.

They then briefly moved to England, where Hyron played for the Sale Sharks, before returning to South Africa for the last few months playing for the Lions.



Maighlin went on to praise her late husband for his kindness and compassion, even to strangers.

She added, “I pray that God guides us through this unimaginable time.

“I pray that I can raise these boys to be good men like you. I pray that you passed peacefully and knew how much you were adored, and your final thoughts were of your family. I pray that you always look over us and protect us. 

“The devastation is beyond words, but the overwhelming love, support, and kindness we have received is incredible! I could write a million words and post a thousand pictures, but it would never be enough. I love you, I miss you. I’m lost without you. Rest easy, my love”.

CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED

On Wednesday, 21 October, the Lions announced Hyron Andrews’ cause of death following an autopsy conducted by French authorities.

According to the report, the 31-year-old’s death was caused by an aortic dissection. Thi dissection most likely occurred on an aortic aneurysm.



French authorities described the medical incident as “a tear in the aorta, due to natural causes, which led to a significant accumulation of blood within the sac surrounding the heart.”

World.title: Triple murder suspect Tshuma ‘not eating or sleeping well’, court hears
World.content:
Triple murder suspect Ndodana Tshuma has reportedly been struggling to eat and sleep, prompting his lawyer to request a specialist medical assessment during his appearance at the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court.

According to reports from the court proceedings on Wednesday, 21 October, Tshuma’s lawyer, Chrispin Machingura, raised concerns about his client’s condition as the defence and state attempted to resolve outstanding issues surrounding a plea and sentencing agreement.

The proceedings took a turn when Tshuma reportedly told the court that he could not remember pleading guilty or signing the document presented to him.



The case was postponed to 29 October to allow further consultations between Tshuma and his legal representative, SABC News reported.

lawyer requests sApecialist assessment

Machingura reportedly told the court that his client had not been eating and sleeping well. He requested that Tshuma be examined by a specialist for a medical assessment.

The request came as the defence sought to clarify Tshuma’s position on the plea agreement, which had been expected to be finalised during Wednesday’s proceedings.

According to the reports, Tshuma maintained that he was innocent and said he could not remember pleading guilty. When his lawyer showed him the document he had signed, he reportedly said he could not recall signing it.

The development raised further questions about whether the outstanding plea and sentencing arrangements could proceed as planned.

The court granted a postponement to allow the defence more time to consult with Tshuma.



His reported difficulties sleeping and eating should not, however, be taken as a medical diagnosis, and the request for an assessment does not establish that he has a particular condition.

Why Tshuma is appearing in court

Tshuma, a British national of Zimbabwean descent, is wanted in the United Kingdom in connection with the alleged murders of his wife, Zandile, and their two daughters, Natalie and Nala.

He was arrested in Johannesburg in July following an international manhunt.

South African proceedings include charges relating to unlawful possession of a firearm and ammunition, as well as contraventions of the Immigration Act.

Tshuma had previously pleaded guilty to firearm-related and immigration offences in South Africa, with the state and defence working towards a plea and sentencing agreement.

However, outstanding documentation and discrepancies delayed the finalisation of the agreement.

His South African criminal proceedings are separate from the extradition process through which British authorities are seeking his return to face the murder allegations.

The next court appearance on 29 October is expected to allow further consultations between Tshuma and his lawyer as the local proceedings continue.

World.title: SAPS wants YOU: Applications open for 5 500 trainees
World.content:
The South African Police Service (SAPS) has opened applications for 5 500 entry-level police trainee positions for the 2026/2027 financial year.

This is an opportunity for the youth of South Africa to pursue a career in law enforcement.

SAPS opened the recruitment on Wednesday, 21 October and applications officially close on 13 November.



South Africans between the ages of 18-35 are encouraged to apply, with a particular emphasis on those who are fit, disciplined and committed to serving their communities.

Colonel Amanda van Wyk, the National SAPS spokesperson, said the recruitment drive aims to attract young people that are passionate about making a difference and contributing to a safer South Africa.

HOW TO APPLY

If you’re interested in applying, you can do so on the official SAPS recruitment portal here.

Applicants are required to create a profile and verify their account. Once the account has been verified, the applicant needs to follow the step-by-step application process to apply for the positions.

Applicants must not have a previous criminal record or a pending criminal case.

Graduates are encouraged to apply.



“Graduates in Law, Policing, Criminology, Law Enforcement, Forensic Investigation and Information Technology may be considered for placement within the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation (DPCI), also known as the Hawks; Detective and Forensic Services; and Crime Intelligence,” said Van Wyk.

“The targeted recruitment process will also seek to identify suitably qualified young people from underrepresented racial groups who meet the prescribed requirements.”

SAPS warns against recruitment scams

SAPS also emphasised applications are completely free and warned candidates against individuals demanding money in exchange for employment or promising to influence the recruitment process.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to apply early and use only official SAPS recruitment channels.

During the academy institution phase, all trainees receive a monthly stipend of R5 000.

Upon completing basic training and advancing to the probation phase as permanent constables, officers receive a starting salary of R248 175 per annum alongside standard public service benefits.

During the previous recruitment drive closing in July 2025, SAPS received 1 021 563 applications for 5 500 roles, including 334 765 tertiary graduates, highlighting severe youth unemployment in South Africa.

World.title: 'Not on the fence' - ActionSA sets three non-negotiables for coalition partners
World.content:
JOAHNNESBURG - With just two weeks left until South Africans head to the polls, ActionSA has made its stance on coalition crystal clear.

Its leader and Johannesburg mayoral candidate, Herman Mashaba laid down three non-negotiable conditions for any potential coalition partners.

The first is a zero-tolerance approach to corruption, with Mashaba warning that nobody should be shielded from accountability.

“When Herman Mashaba steals a cent of public money, don't protect him because be assured, Herman Mashaba is not going to protect you. Secondly, we have a constitutional obligation as government to provide public services to all residents,” he said.

The second condition is that ActionSA highlighted the importance of constitutional obligation as a government to provide public services to all residents.

READ | IEC receives more than 700 complaints over election-related content

And finally, Mashaba said potential coalition partners must agree that undocumented foreign nationals are not welcomed in municipalities governed by Actions, either alone or in coalition.

“Action SA is happy to remain on their benches because if we enter into an agreement with you before resolving these three issues, we know that coalition is going to collapse. Therefore, we'd rather be on the opposition benches.”

Mashaba affirmed that the only time they will consider coalitions is after the elections.

World.title: Number Of The Day | R10 billion | 21 October 2026
World.content:
Cheaper Fuel Is A Reprieve. Why South Africa Needs More Than Temporary Relief

For South African households already struggling with rising living costs, a reduction in fuel prices offers something increasingly difficult to find: immediate breathing room. But the relief announced in the 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement also exposes a deeper vulnerability. When the price of a globally traded commodity can so quickly destabilise household budgets, the problem extends beyond what motorists pay at the pump.

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced R10 billion in temporary fuel levy relief, reducing the levy by R3 per litre for diesel and R1.50 for petrol from 4 November to 1 December 2026. Smaller reductions will follow until 5 January 2027. The intervention offers meaningful short-term support, particularly after fuel prices rose sharply amid the conflict in the Middle East. But the scheduled withdrawal of the

relief means households cannot assume that November's savings will continue into the new year.

Why Fuel Prices Reach Far Beyond Motorists

Fuel is not merely a cost for private vehicle owners. It affects the movement of food, manufactured goods, construction materials and essential supplies. Businesses that depend on road transport face higher operating expenses when diesel prices rise, while workers who travel long distances to earn a living must absorb additional commuting costs.

These pressures can compound. A household may spend more on transport while also facing higher prices for goods delivered by road. A small business may have to choose between absorbing additional costs, increasing its prices or reducing expenditure elsewhere. A temporary reduction in fuel levies can ease those pressures, but it cannot remove the underlying exposure to international oil markets.

The scale of the relief matters, yet its duration matters just as much. In November, motorists may experience a noticeable reduction in the cost of filling a tank. By January, the temporary levy intervention is scheduled to disappear. That makes the measure a bridge across a difficult period rather than a lasting solution to transport affordability.

The Budget's More Difficult Number

The medium-term budget contained another figure with potentially longer-lasting consequences. National Treasury reduced its forecast for economic growth in 2026 from 1.6% to 1.2%. This follows an extended period of weak growth that has constrained South Africa's ability to create employment and improve living standards.

A stronger fiscal position is welcome. Treasury reports that government debt relative to the size of the economy stabilised at 78.4% in 2025/26, while its revised fiscal projections point towards a narrowing budget deficit. These developments could eventually reduce borrowing costs and create more room for productive investment.

But fiscal stability does not automatically create jobs. Businesses need confidence to expand, infrastructure that works, reliable logistics and sufficient demand for their products and services. Even when government manages its finances more effectively, growth can remain weak if the wider economy cannot turn that stability into investment, production and employment.

The distinction is especially important for households without secure incomes. A reduction in fuel costs can improve disposable income for a limited period. A new job, sustainable wage growth or a more productive local economy can change a household's financial circumstances for much longer.

What Happens When The Relief Ends?

Temporary fuel relief is a legitimate policy response to an extraordinary price shock. It can prevent a difficult period from becoming more damaging, especially when households and businesses have little room to absorb further increases. But relief should not be mistaken for resilience.

The larger test is whether South Africa can use the space created by a more stable fiscal position to improve infrastructure, accelerate economic activity and expand employment. Those outcomes require sustained implementation, not merely favourable budget announcements.

The R10 billion intervention may ease the immediate pressure at the pumps. Its real significance will become clearer when the relief expires and South Africans discover whether anything more durable has changed.

References

· National Treasury, 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, 21 October 2026.

· Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana, MTBPS Speech, 21 October 2026.

· South African Revenue Service, Revised 2026 Revenue Estimate, 21 October 2026.

World.title: Cry of the Xcluded demands pro-poor spending
World.content:
PRETORIA - Workers and frustrated civil society groups have taken to the streets, pushing back against government's austerity measures.

They said budget cuts are not just numbers on a spreadsheet but a direct war on the working class, with jobs, wages, and public services now on the line.

The Cry of the Xcluded coalition submitted a memorandum of demands to the National Treasury office in Pretoria.

The march coincided with the finance minister's Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement.

The Cry of the Xcluded said its fight is far from over after the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement failed to address their concerns.

They warn that if austerity continues, it is the working class that will continue to pay the highest price.

eNCA reporter Bafedile Moerane has more details in the video above.

World.title: No military solution in Sudan: UN envoy
World.content:
GENEVA - There is no military solution to the civil war tearing Sudan apart, the United Nations envoy on the conflict insisted Wednesday following international talks on peace efforts.

A total of 21 countries and five international organisations gathered at the UN headquarters in Geneva for the so-called Sixth Consultative Meeting on Enhancing Coordination of Peace Initiatives and Efforts in Sudan.

The two warring parties were not represented.

The war between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, displaced more than 13 million and created the world's largest hunger and displacement crises.

Talks co-chair Pekka Haavisto, UN chief Antonio Guterres' personal envoy for Sudan, said the regular armed forces and the RSF still believed in a military victory in the war.

"We as the international community are saying that there is no military solution to the conflict in Sudan," the former Finnish foreign minister told a press conference after the talks concluded.

"The solution has to be found from diplomatic talks and discussions.

"One small step that the United Nations has been taking is trying to introduce so-called confidence-building measures: some steps that both parties can agree."

He said one was the possible exchange of prisoners of war or detainees, both military and civilian, and another was on facilitating student exams.

"We think that there are issues that should unite actually both parties of the conflict, but these are, of course, baby steps compared with the terrible destruction that is happening," Haavisto admitted.

- 'Immense suffering' -

The gathering included the Quad (Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United States and the United Arab Emirates), the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, and several of Sudan's neighbours, such as Ethiopia and Chad.

The meeting aimed to align mediation initiatives, promote de-escalation and a negotiated political solution, and bolster humanitarian access.

The talks focused on three chapters: the security situation, political issues and the regional dimension to the war.

World.title: Political parties welcome Medium-Term Budget policy statement
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Most political parties have welcomed the fuel levy reduction that Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana has announced.

But it's clear that more work still needs to be done.

Action SA’s Athol Trollip said interim relief for the fuel levy is welcomed by millions of South Africans who are feeling the pinch.

READ | WATCH | Godongwana delivers Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement

Equally, it recognised SARS's performance for the relief.

“If it wasn't for SARS's performance, we wouldn't have been able to have this R10billion cushion that has been provided,” he said.

DA’s Kingsley Wakelin said that, as a party, they support the current submission that was made by the minister.

“The minister has laid a foundation for this country now to move to the next frontier and the next frontier is clear structural reform and economic growth. We cannot grow employment on a 1.2 percent growth rate. It is time that we move to a 3.5 percent growth rate, and for that we need serious reform.”

Meanwhile, BOSA leader Mmusi Maimane said they had advocated for the relief. But, he acknowledged that a lot more work needs to be done.

World.title: Focus on artificial intelligence and growth at Singularity Summit
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Artificial intelligence offers significant advantages for businesses and the modern economy but well-established AI infrastructure remains essential.

South Africa and the rest of the continent must build their own artificial intelligence infrastructure to keep up with global technology.

Global and local experts at the Old Mutual-sponsored Singularity Summit, underway in Sandton, share this view.

The summit put artificial intelligence, robotics, innovation, and governance centre stage.

The summit continues on Thursday.

eNCA’s Siphamandla Goge shares more details in the video above.

World.title: Jansen, Rabada put Proteas in sight of win over Australia
World.content:
GQEBERHA - Marco Jansen and Kagiso Rabada bowled South Africa to within sight of a series-levelling victory on the fourth day of the second Test at St George's Park on Wednesday.

Australia were 156 for four in their follow-on innings after being shot out for 99 earlier in the day. They were still 170 runs short of making South Africa bat again.

Travis Head survived an early chance and was unbeaten on 87. Steve Smith did not come out to bat in the second innings after appearing to be struggling with a neck injury while making top score of 28 in Australia's first innings.

Jansen took five for 33 as Australia crashed to their fourth-lowest total against South Africa and Rabada made two crucial breakthroughs in the second innings.

Rabada dismissed Australian opening batsman Nic Maddinson cheaply for the second time in the match and later bowled Matt Renshaw, who was man of the match in Australia's 214-run win in the first Test.

With a first innings lead of 326 runs, South Africa enforced the follow-on despite fast bowler Anrich Nortje being out of action with a groin injury. Nortje dismissed Marnus Labuschagne in the first innings but bowled only 3.3 overs before pulling up injured.

In Nortje's absence, South African captain Temba Bavuma used Rabada, Jansen and fellow seamer Wiaan Mulder in short spells and made extensive use of off-spinner Simon Harmer, who bowled 18 overs and took two wickets.

Harmer broke a 92-run second-wicket stand between Head and Labuschagne when the latter went for a big hit and was caught by Jansen running back from mid-on as the ball was held up in a stiff breeze.

Tall left-armer Jansen was superb in the first innings. He struck with his first ball of the match when he had nightwatchman Scott Boland caught behind in the second over of the day.

He followed up with the wickets of Head, Renshaw, Alex Carey and Beau Webster as Australia collapsed.

World.title: Gachagua, Sifuna eye joint presidential strategy against Ruto
World.content:
DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua hosts Edwin Sifuna and Linda Mwananchi leaders at his Wamunyoro residence on October 20, 2026. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

A powerful political wave is expected to sweep across the country from this weekend, when Rigathi Gachagua’s Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) and Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi outfit hold their first joint rally in Nyahururu.

Fresh details emerging from a meeting held at Wamunyoro on Tuesday indicate that a series of joint meetings between the two camps will continue in the coming weeks.

World.title: Drama in church after Mudavadi, Wetang'ula walk out as Sifuna speaks
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna, Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula join mourners at the late Burudi Nabwera's memorial in Nairobi. [Edwin Sifuna, X]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula walked out of the requiem mass of former lawmaker Burudi Nabwera after Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna was invited to address mourners.

In a clip that has since gone viral, the two senior government officials are seen walking towards the entrance of Friends Church in Lang'ata on Wednesday, the venue for the memorial service, while Sifuna took the stage.

Sifuna appeared to acknowledge the departure with a "this is Nairobi" quip that drew laughter from mourners.

The incident appears to lay bare the deepening political divisions ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The two leaders’ departure came as Sifuna used the funeral gathering to condemn tribal politics, lament the breakdown of political friendships and pledge to restore the spirit of national unity that defined Kenya at independence.

“At the beginning of this country, when we got independence, we were all Kenyans; there was nothing like tribalism and everyone of us should be available to all of us to sell our policies,” he said.

The senator appeared to take a swipe at those seeking to restrict political associations along regional lines, saying leaders were being judged based on whom they were seen with.

“Some people saw me somewhere with someone and somehow they are telling us that there is a region in this country where none of us is supposed to associate with,” Sifuna said.

The sentiments appeared to castigate government leaders who he said "are not happy" with his association with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

This happened just hours after he met the Democracy for the Citizens (DCP) party leader at his Wamunyoro home in Nyeri on Tuesday, in the company of other Linda Mwananchi movement leaders.

He pledged that, in honour of Nabwera, he would work towards reviving the spirit of unity that characterised the country at independence in 1963.

“I want to make assurance here, in honour of Burudi Nabwera, we will restore that feeling that was there at the beginning of our country in 1963, that all of us, irrespective of our tribe, are Kenyans and we all belong to this society,” he said.

Sifuna, also used the opportunity to woo the Nabwera's nephew, Nabii Nabwera, who is Lugari MP, with whom they have "shared a long political history."

Sifuna also expressed regret that political divisions had separated him from Nabii, whom he described as a friend with whom they journeyed together in ODM.

“Our politics is so petty that being seen with some of us, you are branded and told you are hanging out with Sifuna; you are now a bad person,” he said.

“I miss Nabii Nabwera. You know the things we have done together. You know the journey we have walked together in ODM. I want you by my side on this journey towards the presidency,” he said.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
