World.title: Liberia: Snowe Seeks Audit Over Alleged Kickbacks in Bomi, Presses Education Ministry on School Closed Three Years
World.content:
Monrovia – Bomi County Senator Edwin Melvin Snowe, Jr. has called for an urgent, independent audit of local government spending in the county, citing allegations that some officials are spending county resources without adequate accountability and inflating contract values to facilitate possible kickbacks.

By Rodney D. Sieh

Speaking as the Liberian Senate resumed its legislative duties, Sen. Snowe told his colleagues that the implementation of the Local Government Act, passed by the Legislature, “raises serious concerns requiring our urgent attention.” He said the allegations warrant an audit “to establish the facts and ensure appropriate action where wrongdoing is found.”



The senator also urged the Legislature to revisit provisions governing the qualifications, selection and responsibilities of County Council members, saying lawmakers must address weaknesses that undermine competent representation, transparency and accountability.

School Closed for More Than Three Years

Sen. Snowe drew particular attention to Bomi Junior High School, which he said has been closed for more than three years because of a damaged roof. Its students are currently being accommodated at C. H. Dewey High School.

He told the Senate that when the Minister of Education appeared before the body, she made a firm commitment to intervene urgently. “Regrettably, that commitment remains unfulfilled,” he said.

According to the senator, he wrote to the Minister offering to use his legislative project funds to repair the roof. The Minister, he said, asked him to hold off, explaining that funding was available and that the repairs were awaiting approval from the Public Procurement and Concessions Commission (PPCC), along with works at other schools across the country.

“Our students cannot continue to bear the consequences of these delays,” Sen. Snowe said, calling on the plenary to require the Minister to explain the outstanding procurement issues and provide a definite timetable for the repairs.

He also asked the relevant Senate committee to examine concerns about the Western Region University’s compliance with its Charter, particularly the constitution of its governing Board and the recruitment of its leadership. The university, he said, is now fully operational.

Development Projects and Student Support

Sen. Snowe listed ongoing projects in the county, including a public clinic in Weajour, an auditorium for the Sess Town High School and a town hall in Lower Zor. He said he continues to provide full scholarships for 100 students at the Western Region University and, during the period under review, gave short-term vacation jobs to 536 students. Each student worked two hours daily for four days and received LRD 5,000 toward returning to school.

He noted that, despite political differences, he and his Bomi colleague, Senator Alex Tyler, maintain a cordial working relationship.

“Follow the Money”

Turning to national matters, the senator acknowledged that Liberia’s budget has crossed the billion-dollar mark, describing it as a significant milestone. But he warned that the Senate “cannot continue to celebrate increased revenues or reported budget surpluses while our communities struggle to see the benefits.”

“Our oversight must follow the money from allocation to release, expenditure, and results,” he said, adding that institutions falling behind on implementation must explain the delays.

As Chairman of the Senate Committee on Hydrocarbon, Energy and Environment, Sen. Snowe said his committee continues oversight of electricity generation and distribution, tariffs, petroleum-sector governance and environmental protection, working with institutions including the LEC, LERC, EPA and NIC.

He also called for sustained legislative and budgetary support for the fight against drugs, covering prevention, enforcement, treatment and rehabilitation.

US$17.5 Million Owed to ECOWAS

Sen. Snowe raised alarm over Liberia’s reported US$17.5 million in arrears to ECOWAS, recommending that the relevant committees engage the Ministries of Finance and Development Planning and Foreign Affairs to establish the status of the debt and secure a practical payment plan.

He said the arrears must be addressed as Liberia eyes major regional roles, including the possibility of President Joseph Nyuma Boakai chairing the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government, and the presidency of the ECOWAS Commission, allocated to Liberia for 2030–2034 subject to meeting the applicable criteria.

He recognized three Liberians serving in regional institutions: Hon. Dehpue Yenpea Zuo, ECOWAS Commissioner for Economic Affairs and Agriculture; Hon. Boima S. Kamara, Director General of the West African Monetary Agency; and Justice Charlyne M. Brumskine, President of the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, whom he described as the first Liberian to head an ECOWAS institution.

Africa CDC Appointment, Diaspora Voting

The senator announced his appointment to the Continental Immunization Advisory Council of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC). He said the council’s new 15-member configuration includes three parliamentarians from across the continent, and he is one of them.

He also recommended that the Legislature begin a structured examination of diaspora voting, saying the continued inability of Liberians in the United States and elsewhere to vote from abroad “deserves serious legislative consideration.”

Sen. Snowe thanked President Boakai for inviting him to development discussions in the United States with American inventor Dr. Lonnie Johnson, and said a formal report on those talks will be submitted to the Senate.

World.title: Liberia: U.S. Embassy Officials Visit Leading War Crimes Investigators in Show of Support, Investigators Say
World.content:
Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group says a visit by U.S. Embassy officials was intended to reassure its staff about their security. From left: Hassan Bility, director of the Global Justice and Research Project; Christopher M. Hofmann, political officer; and Thomas Quaye, political and human rights assistant at the U.S. Embassy in Liberia. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Summary:

Two U.S. Embassy officials visited Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group following death threats against its director of investigations, who was subsequently relocated for security reasons.

Hassan Bility, the group’s director, described the visit as a show of American solidarity while the officials declined to comment on the visit.

The visit comes amid security concerns linked to investigations involving alleged Liberian war criminals, including former senior army commander Moses Wright, whose U.S. trial has been postponed until February 2027.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

Two officials from the U.S. Embassy in Monrovia visited the Global Justice and Research Project, Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group, two weeks after it relocated its director of investigations following repeated death threats . The group’s director said the visit was an expression of American solidarity with his organization.



Christopher M. Hofmann, a political officer at the Embassy, and Thomas Quaye, a political and human rights assistant, visited the organization earlier this month. They allowed this reporter to photograph their visit but declined to comment on the discussions, referring questions to Hassan Bility, the group’s director.

“The U.S. had come to listen to some of our security concerns,” Bility said in an interview after the meeting. “Their coming was a solidarity of support to indicate that the United States stands with us, and the United States will not stand by idly to allow somebody to do harm to the Global Justice and Research Project.”

The visit comes amid growing security concerns involving the Global Justice and Research Project, whose investigations have contributed to convictions of former rebel commanders over their Liberia war-related crimes, in the United States and Europe. The organization has repeatedly faced threats and attacks.

The latest threats were directed at an investigator working on cases involving alleged wartime perpetrators, including Moses Wright, 73, a former senior Liberian army commander accused of concealing his wartime activities when applying for U.S. immigration benefits. Survivors have accused Wright of involvement in the 1990 St. Peter’s Lutheran Church massacre, in which an estimated 600 civilians were killed. He faces federal immigration fraud and perjury charges in Pennsylvania and has denied the charges.

Bility said his organization had sought security assistance from the two-member U.S. Embassy delegation but declined to share what they said. Nevertheless he said he was comforted by the visit.

“I feel more secure,” Bility said of the embassy’s visit. “Every time U.S. embassy officials visit this office, for us, it becomes an expression of solidarity with our works and our belief, what we stand for. And we know what they can do.”

In 2021, Michael McCarthy, then the U.S. ambassador to Liberia, visited the group’s offices and publicly expressed support for Bility’s work amid threats against the organization.

The organization has faced other security incidents. Earlier this year, armed men broke into its Monrovia offices , assaulted a security guard and threatened Bility, prompting renewed concerns about the safety of those investigating wartime atrocities.

A portion of the 16-foot fence surrounding the offices of the Global Justice and Research Project, which the group says were recently broken into by armed men.Credit: Global Justice and Research Project.

Bility said the Liberia National Police had not provided updates on complaints the organization filed concerning the threats. Gregory Coleman, Liberia’s police inspector general, did not respond to the latest request for comment.

The Global Justice and Research Project and its Swiss partner, Civitas Maxima, have helped document atrocities committed during Liberia’s civil wars, gathering evidence and identifying witnesses for investigations and prosecutions in the United States and Europe.

Their work has contributed to several convictions. In the United States, Mohammed Jabateh, a former rebel commander known as “Jungle Jabbah,” was sentenced to 30 years in prison for immigration fraud and perjury. In Switzerland, Alieu Kosiah, another former rebel commander, received a 20-year sentence for war crimes . In France, Kunti Kamara, a former commander of the same rebel group, was sentenced to 30 years imprisonment in 2022 for complicity in crimes against humanity, torture and acts of barbarism.

The organizations’ work has also drawn accusations of witness coaching and bribery from defendants and their supporters, allegations they, investigators and prosecutors in every case have rejected.

In 2022, Beth Van Schaack, then the U.S. ambassador-at-large for global criminal justice, publicly backed Bility and his organization , praising their contribution to international prosecutions.

“These cases would not be possible without the amazing work of the Global Justice and Research Project and other Liberian and international civil society actors who have rigorously, reliably, and with unwavering integrity worked to keep the dream of justice alive,” she said.

Van Schaack also expressed concern about threats and intimidation against the organization’s staff.

Threats against Global Justice have fueled concerns about security for witnesses and officials of Liberia’s proposed war and economic crimes court. The country’s Witness Protection Agency recently unveiled a US$20.54 million plan they said would be needed to support the activities of the court.

World.title: Liberia Ready for Scrabble Nations Cup as 16th Africa Championship Draws Near
World.content:
MONROVIA — Liberia is set to host the 16th Africa Scrabble Championship (ASC) as national delegations from across the continent begin arriving in Monrovia for the four-day event, scheduled to run from October 22 to 25.

By Christopher C. Walker, [email protected]

The tournament will feature players from 24 African nations at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex in Congo Town, positioning Liberia at the center of the continent’s competitive Scrabble landscape.



Anticipation is building ahead of Thursday’s official kickoff. Defending champion Nigeria is eyeing another continental title, Kenya is sending a massive contingent, and neighboring Sierra Leone is making its journey by road.

Participating athletes will compete for both individual and national honors in a sport that requires vocabulary mastery, spatial strategy, board management, and mental stamina.

Contingents Arrive as Nigeria Targets Title Defense

Kenya began its arrivals on Tuesday evening, with an initial group landing at Roberts International Airport aboard ASKY Airlines at 5:50 p.m.

While 15 members of the delegation received government sponsorship, the total Kenyan contingent is expected to be substantially larger, with team officials indicating up to 32 players could represent the East African power.

Meanwhile, Nigeria’s national team officially departed for Monrovia on Tuesday, intent on defending its continental crown against top-tier contenders and emerging nations.

Sierra Leone is also scheduled to enter Liberia by road via the Bo Waterside border crossing, adding a strong West African regional presence.

Association President: “Liberia Is Prepared”

Addressing journalists at the Ministry of Information, Liberian Scrabble Association (LSA) President Lester Morris confirmed that all hosting arrangements are complete and urged Liberians to attend in large numbers.

“Liberia is fully prepared to host this championship,” Morris said, encouraging the public to support local players and witness high-level intellectual sport firsthand.

Liberia, hosting the ASC represents both a test of its sports management capabilities and a major opportunity for local players to test their skills against the continent’s best.

Four Days of High-Stakes Strategy

The championship officially opens on Thursday, October 22, and concludes on Sunday, October 25.

Over ninety-six hours of continuous play, competitors will battle through a grueling schedule where dynamic word knowledge, board control, and quick decision-making will decide the ultimate winners.

By Thursday morning, administrative preparations will yield to live play as Monrovia welcomes Africa’s elite Scrabble community for four days of strategic competition.

World.title: Liberia: Koulibaly Shines on Borough FC Return With Goal and Crucial Saves
World.content:
MONROVIA — Goalkeeper Abdulai Koulibaly marked his return to Borough FC in dramatic fashion on Sunday, scoring a second-half penalty and making a series of crucial saves in a 1-1 draw against Heaven Eleven in the opening fixture of the 2026/27 Liberia Football Association (LFA) First Division season.

By Christopher C. Walker, [email protected]

Playing at the D. Twe Sports Pitch in New Kru Town, Koulibaly who recently rejoined Borough on a two-year deal following his departure from LPRC Oilers proved decisive at both ends of the pitch.



The shot-stopper broke the deadlock in the 70th minute, calmly step-stepping up to convert from the penalty spot to give the hosts a 1-0 lead.

Beyond his goal, Koulibaly produced a commanding display between the posts, turning away several dangerous efforts from Heaven Eleven to preserve Borough’s advantage.

However, Borough’s bid for all three points was thwarted in the 84th minute when Heaven Eleven’s Moses Cooper rose above the defense to head home the equalizer.

Experienced Head Back in New Kru Town

Despite conceding late, Koulibaly’s individual performance provided a major highlight for Borough as the club aims to build momentum in the new campaign.

Koulibaly brings a rich legacy back to the club, having featured prominently across its previous names from Monrovia Club Breweries to Global Pharma FC and now Borough FC.

During his previous stint, he helped the club secure two Orange FA Cups and two Second Division titles.

After departing at the end of the 2024/25 season for LPRC Oilers, Koulibaly mutually terminated his contract with Oilers to pave the way for his return to New Kru Town.

Borough FC will look to claim its first victory of the new season on Thursday, October 22, when they travel to Tusa Field to face Gardnersville FC.

World.title: Mpulungu Kapenta traders hail Solar-powered dryer support
World.content:
Women involved in drying Kapenta in Mpulungu District have thanked the Fish for African Caribbean and Pacific Countries Project (FISH4ACP) for supporting them with a solar-powered dryer, saying it will help improve the quality of their Kapenta.

Twazwane Women’s group chairperson Callen Nakazwe said the equipment will provide a more reliable and hygienic way to dry Kapenta, a small fish that is an important source of food and income in the area.

Mpulungu, Ms Nakazwe said traditional drying methods have for a long time left the Kapenta exposed to dust, insects and changing weather conditions, which may affect its quality.

She disclosed that the solar-powered dryer is expected to help protect the fish during the drying process and produce a cleaner, more consistent product.

‘’We are very grateful for the welcome support because it is a practical investment in our work and livelihoods as improved drying will reduce losses and help us preserve more of the Kapenta as we process it,’’ she disclosed

Ms Nakazwe explained that better-quality fish will also attract buyers and strengthen the women’s ability to compete in local markets especially during the rainy season periods when weather conditions make open-air processing difficult.

She added that the dryer will make their work more efficient while helping them maintain better standards for the Kapenta fish they sell.

The women also expressed hope that the equipment will encourage more people in their communities to adopt improved fish-handling practices.

Ms Nakazwe said they were grateful for the support and pledged to use the dryer responsibly and also called for continued training and support to help them operate and maintain the equipment effectively.

The women said the solar-powered dryer offers an opportunity to improve Kapenta quality, increase the value of their work and support their livelihoods.

FISH4ACP supports sustainable and inclusive development in fisheries and aquaculture value chains.

Its assistance to the women is intended to strengthen Kapenta processing in Mpulungu District.

World.title: Government prioritises tailings Dam safety
World.content:
The Government has identified tailings dam safety as a priority, calling for increased training of regulators and mining operators to strengthen the management of these facilities.

Minerals Regulations Commission Director Mine Inspections and Audits Elite Mhone warned that climate change and increasingly heavy rainfall heighten the risk of tailings dam failures.

Mr Mhone was speaking during a plenary session at the Mining and Investment Insaka in Lusaka.

He said that unlike conventional water dams, tailings facilities continue to grow as mining waste accumulates, requiring ongoing monitoring, stronger safety measures and improved regulatory oversight to protect surrounding communities and the environment.

“The size of rainfall we receive now is not the same as rainfall that was being received in 1964, right now we have got a lot of rainfall,” Mr Mhone

Mr Mhone further said that Zambia’s tailings dam management and safety standards remain inadequate, raising concerns as the country targets annual copper production of three million tonnes.

He has since called for stricter regulatory inspections, independent engineering oversight, a national tailings dam registry and greater accountability for mining companies.

And Zambia Environmental Agency (ZEMA) Acting Director Licensing and Compliance Constantino Mweembela said mining companies should strengthen water quality monitoring and engage communities to protect shared water resources in increasingly water-stressed areas.

“Environmental impact assessments must go beyond regulatory compliance to include practical measures for preventing pollution, monitoring groundwater and surface water, and detecting contamination early,” he said.

Mr Mwembela has also urged mining operators to invest in real-time monitoring systems and adhere to international tailings management standards to safeguard water resources and surrounding communities.

Meanwhile, Seed Global Health Country Director, Chikusela Sikazwe has urged mining companies to integrate health considerations into environmental and social impact assessments from the earliest stages of mining projects.

Dr Sikazwe said this will help to ensure that their investments align with government priorities.

He warned that uncoordinated investments can lead to duplication and underutilised health facilities, calling for stronger collaboration between mining companies and the Ministry of Health.

“The approach should strengthen Zambia’s health system throughout the mining lifecycle, including emergency care and preparedness for disease outbreaks, climate-related health risks and future pandemics,” Dr Sikazwe said.

World.title: President Hichilema attends SADC extraordinary meeting virtually
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema participated in the Extraordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Heads of State and Government virtually.

President Hichilema’s participation underscores Zambia’s resolve and commitment to supporting discussions and decisions that strengthen the SADC Secretariat, advance regional integration and promote peace, security and stability among Member States.

The Extraordinary Summit was chaired by SADC Chairperson and President of South Africa, Cyril Ramaphosa.

In his opening remarks, President Ramaphosa said the strength of SADC rests not only on political commitments but on strong institutions with the leadership, capacity and resources to translate decisions into tangible improvements in people’s lives.

He said regional integration must be measured by the extent to which it creates jobs, attracts investment, reduces poverty and improves citizens’ livelihoods, while peace and stability remain indispensable foundations for development.

Meanwhile, the Summit has elected Lesotho as the new Chairperson of the SADC Organ Troika on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation, taking over the leadership of the Organ charged with promoting peace and security in the region.

The Organ plays a central role in preventive diplomacy, mediation, conflict resolution and addressing security challenges, including the situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the threat of terrorism and violent extremism in northern Mozambique.

The Summit also appointed and swore in Treasure Maphanga as Deputy Executive Secretary responsible for Regional Integration.

Ms Maphanga’s appointment fills a key treaty position expected to accelerate implementation of the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP), drive cross-border infrastructure development, expand electricity generation and transmission, and deepen regional value chains and intra-regional trade.

President Ramaphosa congratulated both Lesotho and Ms Maphanga and urged the strengthened SADC institutions to work towards building a region where peace prevails and economic opportunities expand.

Eelier, Southern African Development Community (SADC) Executive Secretary, Elias Magosi said the Extraordinary Summit was convened to conclude two matters deferred from the Durban Summit in August this year.

The first is the election of the incoming Chairperson of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation, after two member states expressed interest in the position in Durban.

He said the Summit had referred the decision pending further consultations, and consultations have since been concluded with a common position for approval today.

Mr Magosi said the Organ remains indispensable in advancing peace, security, stability, democracy and good governance in the region, as well as in providing an enabling environment for accelerating regional integration and sustainable development.

“The second item is the appointment of the Deputy Executive Secretary for Regional Integration, following a recruitment process, he added

Mr Magosi said the Deputy Executive Secretary for Regional Integration is a key pillar and driver of regional integration, overseeing progress on regional integration as guided by the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) and relevant protocols.

Meanwhile, Mr Magosi congratulated President Daniel Francisco Chapo of Mozambique for successfully hosting the inaugural International Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction and Resilience in Africa in Maputo from 13th to 15th October, 2026, under the theme on strengthening governance and strategic investment for disaster resilience.

He said the conference called for accelerated implementation of disaster risk reduction commitments, strengthened partnerships and increased investment in resilience-building initiatives across Africa.

Mr Magosi also congratulated Dr Navanethem Pillay of South Africa on being awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of her distinguished contributions to peace, justice, human rights and international law, describing it as a source of pride for South Africa, the SADC region and the international community.

World.title: Chinsali Council engages businesses on 2027 budget
World.content:
The Chinsali Municipal Council has engaged the business community in the preparation of its 2027 Output-Based Budget (OBB) to ensure that proposed projects and programmes reflect the development priorities of the district.

Council Public Relations Manager Lolavye Simukoko said the engagement provides a platform for stakeholders to contribute ideas and propose projects for consideration in the 2027 financial year.

Mr Simukoko said the meeting is part of the Council’s efforts to promote public participation in the budgeting process.

The council public relations manager said this in a statement released to ZANIS in Chinsali district.

He said the meeting also featured presentations on services provided by the local authority, the performance of the 2026 Council budget and the role of the Council’s Integrity Committee.

He said the engagement is also intended to ensure that proposed projects aligns with the Chinsali Integrated Development Plan (IDP), the Eighth National Development Plan (8NDP) and the national Grow Zambia Agenda.

During the meeting, stakeholders proposed the construction of an ablution block and fencing of the Council sports facility near the Zambia Army Mess, as well as the provision of waste bins in the Central Business District (CBD) to improve sanitation.

Other proposals include the construction of a transit bus station at Nambuluma Junction, additional Council houses and the rehabilitation of the community hall at the old market in Chinsali CBD.

He explained that the business community also proposed the establishment of parks and recreational spaces near Nkakula Guest House and Bread of Life Church, alongside the development of modern market infrastructure at Choshi, Mishishi and Chinsali Main Market.

Mr Simukoko said stakeholders further proposed the introduction of fire extinguisher supply and refilling services to strengthen fire safety and emergency preparedness in the district.

He said the Council will consider the submissions as part of the budgeting process, with the aim of identifying priority interventions that respond to the needs of the local community.

Mr Simukoko said stakeholder participation is important in promoting transparency, accountability and collaboration between the Council and the business community in advancing development in Chinsali District.

World.title: Kaputa health Director calls for cholera vigilance
World.content:
Kaputa District Health Director Jonathan Bwalya has urged members of the public to remain vigilant against cholera and take extra precautions to prevent the spread of the disease.

Dr Bwalya told the media in an interview that it is important for residents to observe preventive measures and remain alert to the risks posed by cholera, a waterborne disease that can spread through contaminated water and food.

He said his medical team is on the ground and working to ensure that cholera does not spread to Kaputa District.

Dr Bwalya emphasised the importance of public cooperation in preventing the disease, urging residents to take personal hygiene and sanitation seriously.

He further encouraged the public to practice proper hand washing, drink safe water, eat properly handled food and maintain clean surroundings as part of efforts to protect communities from cholera.

Residents were also urged to seek immediate medical attention if they developed symptoms such as acute watery diarrhea and vomiting, which may indicate cholera.

Dr Bwalya’s call comes as health authorities continue to emphasise the importance of vigilance and preventive measures in protecting communities from cholera outbreaks in the wake of reports of a cholera outbreak.

World.title: How long will Kalampa stay top?
World.content:
Nkana’s perfect start to the transitional Super League season is no accident.

Three games, three wins, nine points. Top of Stream A. At Nkana Stadium in Wusakile on Sunday, Elijah Tana’s side did not just beat Nchanga Rangers 2-0, they sent a statement about what a balanced team can achieve.

What is most impressive about this Nkana side is not just the results, but the method.

On one hand, there is Lazarous Kambole, a seasoned striker who knows where the goal is. His opener against Rangers, created by Kedrick Mumba’s vision from his own half, was a reminder that experience still matters in Zambian football. On the other, there is Patrick Gondwe, alert and hungry to pounce when Captain Harrison Chisala’s effort was parried by keeper Victor Chabu.

Nkana are deservedly top. Tana has blended young, energetic players with experienced heads like Kambole and Chisala, and for now, the chemistry is working. But the perfection of nine points masks a lack of clinical edge that better opponents will exploit.

This blend of youth and experience that Coach Tana has spoken about is beginning to produce results. The young, energetic players provide pace and hunger, the experienced heads provide guidance and composure. It is a formula that has served Nkana well throughout its decorated history, and it is working again.

Tana deserves credit for his honesty. “We won’t relax,” he said after the win. “We will continue pushing until the end.” That is exactly the mentality Kalampa needs. Too many times in recent seasons, Nkana have started well only to fade when pressure mounts. This transitional league is short, but it is competitive, and consistency will be key.

Now, spare a thought for Nchanga Rangers. Assistant Coach Israel Mwanza was candid enough to admit his side is under pressure after three straight defeats. Conceding early goals has become a worrying habit for Brave. Yet Mwanza insists their system is fine. Football, however, is a results business. Systems mean little if they cannot stop early setbacks.

For the league as a whole, Nkana’s resurgence is good news. A strong Nkana makes a strong Super League. When Kalampa are firing, attendances improve, rivalry intensifies, and the standard goes up. Their next test away to Konkola Blades will tell us whether this perfect start is a false dawn or the beginning of a genuine title charge in the transitional campaign.

For now, Kalampa are showing the way. The challenge is to stay there.

World.title: Zambia, Botswana, DRC recommit to strengthening regional cooperation
World.content:
Zambia, Botswana and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation through infrastructure connectivity, integrated value chains and cross-border industrial development.

Botswana’s Minister of Minerals and Energy, Bogolo Kenewendo, says the three countries have an opportunity to transform their mineral wealth into shared prosperity through investment, partnerships and coordinated implementation of agreed initiatives.

Ms Kenewendo adds that the African continent possesses some of the world’s most valuable minerals, as well as the talent and partnerships required to unlock their full economic potential.

The Minister was speaking in Lusaka last evening during a networking cocktail party held on the sidelines of the 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment engagement.

Ms Kenewendo stressed that the continent must move beyond discussions and translate commitments into tangible projects that would benefit its people.

She said the focus should now be on implementation to ensure that the mineral resources of Zambia, Botswana, the DRC and other African countries contribute to sustainable economic growth and prosperity.

Ms Kenewendo said the discussions and engagements held over the past few days had opened up opportunities for stronger collaboration and a brighter future for African mining.

She further stressed that the continent must move beyond discussions and translate commitments into tangible projects that would benefit its people.

And Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Minister of Mines, Louis Kabamba says African countries must take responsibility for their own development by strengthening leadership and cooperation.

Mr Kabamba said the Insaka has demonstrated the importance of African countries drawing on their own strengths, sharing experiences and exchanging best practices to accelerate development.

He said all stakeholders, including government officials, mining investors and industry leaders, had a responsibility to contribute to the continent’s development.

Mr Kabamba urged African countries to take ownership of their development aspirations and work together to build prosperous economies.

Passing a vote of thanks, Zambia’s Acting Minister of Mines and Mineral Development, Gilbert Siame, said the Insaka has come at an opportune time to showcase the mineral wealth and investment opportunities available in Zambia, Botswana and the DRC.

Dr Siame said the participation of Botswana and the DRC demonstrated the growing importance of the Insaka as a platform for regional trade and investment.

He said the meeting is also expected to facilitate business deals and joint ventures while supporting the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda, particularly the target of increasing annual copper production to three million metric tonnes by 2031.

President Hakainde Hichilema officially opened the Insaka on October 19, 2026, with business expected to conclude on Friday, October 23.

The event has attracted more than 1,500 participants, including representatives of the World Bank, European Union, African Development Bank and business communities from Australia, China and the United Arab Emirates.

The cocktail party was held at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre in Lusaka, and brought together government officials, investors, mining companies and development partners to explore investment opportunities and strengthen regional cooperation in the mining sector.

World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema is today expected to participate in the Extraordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Heads of State and Government to be held virtually.

The summit will consider outstanding matters, including the recruitment of treaty positions and the election of the incoming Chairperson of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation.

Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mulambo Haimbe, says the summit will be preceded by the virtual Extraordinary Meeting of the SADC Council of Ministers which is also scheduled for today.

World.title: Africa: Africa Needs More Than Envoys to Secure the Red Sea
World.content:
analysis

The Horn's proliferating diplomatic appointments have done little to bolster African influence amid new Middle Eastern alliances.

In September, Ansarullah (the Houthis) took control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, shattering the assumption that the insurgency was confined to northern Yemen. The group is now at the epicentre of the Middle East conflict and is the channel through which crises flow between the Horn of Africa and the Middle East.

Countries on either side of the Red Sea have responded asymmetrically to this shared shock. The Horn has dispatched more envoys while Middle Eastern countries, led by Saudi Arabia, are strengthening political institutions and hardwiring them with military deals. These include the newly signed Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) and the politically oriented 14-member Multinational Maritime Defense Coalition (MMDC).

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Although the Red Sea has a history of instability, current upheavals are distinct. Ansarullah is not only at war with the Saudi Arabia-backed Yemeni government, but is linked to the Israel-Hamas conflict, the Israel-United States war with Iran, and escalating conflicts in the Horn. These interwoven crises require equally interlinked responses from both shores of the Red Sea.

Red Sea and bordering countries

The assertion by Iran, commentators and Ansarullah itself that its conflict is solely with Saudi Arabia is untenable. Iran's strategy of hedging its bets across the Middle East has enabled Ansarullah to evolve from an ally targeting Yemen's government into a self-tasking surrogate whose operations also serve Iran's interests. Having cultivated Ansarullah, Iran did not need to act on its earlier threat to close Bab al-Mandab.

Ansarullah's deepening ties with al-Shabaab have helped transform the Yemeni group from a transnational criminal actor involved in smuggling and illicit financial activity into a force choking a Red Sea gateway carrying nearly 15% of global trade. The two Islamist groups now run a corridor of instability, migration and economic disruption from Tehran to Nairobi and Kampala.

The Horn of Africa's four biggest conflict hotspots - Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and Ethiopia - have become intertwined with Middle Eastern crises. Although conflicts on both sides of the Red Sea stem from local grievances, Middle Eastern actors are the main drivers of conflict in the Horn. The United Arab Emirates (UAE) alone is entangled with Ethiopia, Somalia, and Sudan and has multi-purpose investments in every country in the Horn.

In the past, the Horn's Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and the League of Arab States coordinated over Somalia's crisis and conflict resolution in Sudan. But countries on either side of the Red Sea are now using markedly different tools to address their shared challenges.

In March, the AU designated former Tanzanian president Jakaya Kikwete as its High Representative for the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea. Kikwete, who opted to focus on South Sudan, joined a crowded field of IGAD envoys already deployed in the Horn - covering Somalia, Sudan and South Sudan. Others include the Special Envoy for the Red Sea and Maritime Affairs, and the AU High Representative for Sudan.

A corresponding bench of envoys from outside Africa also covers the Horn - from the UN, EU, China, Germany, Japan, France, Norway, United Kingdom, Netherlands and Switzerland. While each is responsible for a piece of the interconnected conflict resolution puzzle, this 'envoyflation' adds little leverage to individual portfolios or to the Horn's stability. Instead, Horn envoys and their external partners shuttle between capitals, with little progress to show.

Source: ISS based on open-source data

By contrast, Middle Eastern countries are moving away from institutions such as the Gulf Cooperation Council and Council of Arab and African Coastal States of the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, in favour of political-military frameworks. Although there are envoys in the region, they represent external powers, the United Nations (UN) and European Union (EU), not Middle Eastern countries.

The MMDC, established to safeguard freedom of navigation, was launched in Saudi Arabia on 30 July with members including Red Sea and non-Red Sea countries in Africa, the Arab world and Asia.

While it includes Djibouti, Somalia and Sudan, the exclusion of IGAD highlights the Horn's limited regional control over its coastline. This was already evident from Turkey's wardenship of Somalia's maritime defence, the UAE's port expansion in the region and numerous countries' military bases in Djibouti. Eritrea's absence from the MMDC reflects its rejection of military solutions to Yemen's conflict.

Days after launching the MMDC, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan unveiled the MJDA on 7 August. Conspicuously, it excludes Horn countries but includes non-Red Sea Pakistan and Turkey. On 5 October, Saudi Arabia conducted its first military operation against Ansarullah within the MJDA framework.

Both the MJDA and MMDC exclude landlocked Ethiopia and the UAE, which could weaken these frameworks. The exclusions reflect a political dispute over which countries qualify as Red Sea states - a debate that has undermined IGAD's Red Sea efforts. Eritrea's departure from IGAD in December 2025 further limits the organisation's diplomatic leverage over the coastline.

Ethiopia, meanwhile, wants access to the Red Sea but faces opposition from Eritrea and Egypt, a founding MMDC member. This conflates Nile water disputes with disputes over the definition of the Red Sea.

The Horn has military institutions that could help secure the Red Sea. The East Africa Standby Force and Eastern Africa Fusion and Liaison Unit could have complemented IGAD's efforts, but neither has a maritime focus. Consequently, African envoys are increasingly relegated to 'managing' inland conflicts, while their external counterparts are oriented towards the Red Sea.

Close 

Envoyflation reflects IGAD and the AU's political inertia and financial weakness. Envoys are appointed in temporary posts and rely on external donor funding. In the Horn, this has led to fragmented responses and the exclusion of African actors from conflict resolution efforts. Middle Eastern states, by comparison, largely fund their own interventions.

AU and IGAD efforts to institutionalise their position on the Red Sea and engage with the League of Arab States were appropriate steps. However, the league has also been weakened by the altered context.

Going forward, the AU and IGAD should be ready to capitalise on emerging opportunities, reconceptualise their maritime mechanisms, streamline existing diplomatic efforts and work closely with their Middle Eastern partners.

World.title: Uganda: Uganda Has No Active Ebola Cases, Health Ministry Assures Public
World.content:
A tent used to isolate Ebola patients is disinfected in Bunia, DR Congo (file photo).

Uganda has reiterated there are no confirmed active Ebola cases, following reports of a confirmed infection in Nigeria involving a woman who travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) for business.

In a statement, the Director General of Health Services in the Ministry of Health, Prof. Charles Olaro

said preliminary information indicated that the woman transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms but developed them after arriving in Nigeria.

He cautioned against concluding that the infection originated in Uganda, noting that investigations were still underway to establish where the woman was exposed to the virus.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation," Prof Olaro said.

He added that Uganda had no confirmed active Ebola cases at the time of the statement and urged the public to remain calm as authorities continued to monitor the situation.

"We wish to clarify that, as at the time of this statement, Uganda has NO confirmed active Ebola cases," Prof. Olaro said.

The Ministry added that the government of Nigeria had not yet provided detailed information about the woman's travel itinerary and clinical history, which would help guide further investigations and determine whether contact tracing was necessary.

Meanwhile, the Ministry said it would work with relevant government agencies to strengthen screening and public health controls at Uganda's points of entry.

It noted that limited provisions had been maintained for humanitarian and diplomatic movement and that additional measures would be taken to reinforce public health safeguards.

The Ministry urged Ugandans to remain vigilant and observe preventive hygiene measures, including regular handwashing and the use of sanitiser.

"We urge the public to remain calm, vigilant and to practice regular handwashing and sanitising," the statement said.

The Ministry said it would continue to provide verified information through its official communication channels as investigations progressed.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 21, 2026
World.content:
Nigeria Confirms First Ebola Case as Outbreak Spreads

Nigeria has confirmed one case of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) after a woman who recently travelled from Uganda tested positive. The patient is in isolation and receiving treatment at a private hospital. The authorities have begun tracing 44 people identified as contacts of the patient. The government has called on health facilities to step up surveillance, isolate suspected cases and implement infection prevention measures. It also advised the public to maintain good hand hygiene and avoid contact with bodily fluids from suspected cases. Nigeria has become the latest country to report an Ebola case as the virus spreads across the region. Kenya has recorded nine infections. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases, but it later declared itself free of the virus.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

UN Warns Pulling Peacekeepers From CAR Will Fuel Regional Chaos

The United Nations has warned against a premature withdrawal of peacekeepers from the Central African Republic (CAR) as Sudan's war fuels instability along the country's eastern borders. UN Special Representative Valentine Rugwabiza told the Security Council that an attack on Am-Dafock on June 30 killed civilians and security personnel, displaced 17,000 people and injured six UN peacekeepers. She said the rapid response by the UN peacekeeping mission, MINUSCA, helped restore state authority and prevent further casualties. Between June and September, suspected Lord's Resistance Army fighters were linked to 26 serious incidents in the southeast, including sexual violence and the abduction of 68 civilians, about 40 of them children. Despite progress in disarming 1,907 fighters since July 2025 and establishing municipal councils in 127 of 177 municipalities, large areas remain unstable. Nearly two million people faced acute food insecurity between April and August, while the UN humanitarian plan was less than half funded. As the Security Council considers renewing MINUSCA's mandate, members remain divided over troop reductions, with the UN Secretary-General recommending a one-year extension that preserves the mission's capacity to respond rapidly to violence.

15 Years After Gaddafi's Fall, His Legacy Still Haunts Libya and the Sahel

Fifteen years after Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi was captured and killed in 2011, his political legacy continues to influence debates about Libya's instability and security across the Sahel. Libya specialist Virginie Collombier says Kadhafism combined the Green Book's proposed alternative to capitalism and communism with centralised rule, Arab and African nationalism, anti-imperialism and the redistribution of oil wealth. However, the regime was also marked by severe repression, restrictions on political opposition and policies that alienated sections of the population. Kadhafi's overthrow, following an uprising and Western-backed military intervention, left Libya divided between rival political and military factions, with insecurity spreading across the region. Some African leaders and political elites remain nostalgic for his investment and support for African development, while criticising foreign powers for removing him without a clear plan for the country's future. The assassination of his son Saif al-Islam in February 2026 has further weakened the movement, leaving supporters without a prominent leader or a clear political project. Collombier argues that Kadhafi's legacy reflects both his personalised rule and Libya's complex history.

South African Woman Dies in Shark Attack Off Eastern Cape Coast

A 65-year-old South African woman, Janine Lochrenberg, has died following a shark attack while swimming off Orient Beach in KuGompo City, formerly East London. Lochrenberg was swimming with her local open-water swimming club at about 08:00 when she was bitten on her thigh and upper arm. Fellow swimmers brought her towards shore, but she is believed to have died before reaching it. Her sister, Margot, said Lochrenberg had a deep love of the ocean despite being aware of the elevated shark presence in the area. Her partner, Barbara Briceland, described her as an experienced swimmer who regularly ventured into the breakers. The retired medical physicist was reportedly wearing a magnetic shark-repellent band when the attack occurred. Authorities have closed Orient Beach and another nearby beach following the incident. According to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File, fatal shark attacks in South Africa are rare, with about 10 recorded since 2012.

Morocco's First Female Prime Minister Faces Test on Women's Rights

Morocco's appointment of Fatima Zahra El Mansouri as its first female prime minister has been welcomed as a historic milestone but has also reignited debate over women's leadership and gender equality in the Muslim-majority country. Former justice minister Mustafa Ramid questioned whether a woman should lead the government, citing a religious saying that countries led by women will not succeed. Many younger Moroccans welcomed El Mansouri's appointment. However, conservative views remain influential, particularly on inheritance, polygamy, marriage and divorce. Women's rights advocates say reform of the country's family code, known as the Moudawana, will be a key test of whether the new government can deliver meaningful change. Education is another concern, with official figures showing that only 55% of girls aged 15 to 17 in rural areas attended school in 2025, compared with 100% in urban areas. However, analysts said that El Mansouri's ability to drive reform is constrained by the king's extensive powers and the influence of religious authorities. But critics also question whether her appointment is a true step forward, or simply an attempt to bolster the monarchy's image at a time of low voter turnout. Advocates argue that her record in office, rather than her gender alone, will determine whether the appointment translates into lasting improvements for Moroccan women.

World.title: Nigeria: Presidential Panel Submits Draft National Policing Bill to Justice Ministry for Review
World.content:
press release

The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill has completed the drafting stage of its assignment. It has formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), along with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting, review, and validation.

The submission was made on 19 October to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group's work plan.

The ministry's review will ensure the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions and do not conflict with existing laws.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30 October. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to President Bola Tinubu, thereby concluding its mandate.

The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous, transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for the President's consideration and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

Work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the States Houses of Assembly's ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.

Femi Gbajabiamila, CFR

Chief of Staff to the President

Chairman, Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill

World.title: Kenya: Kenya Confirms Ninth Ebola Case, Says All Patients Improving
World.content:
Health workers in protective gear inside the Ebola treatment centre at Buniaâs referral hospital in Ituri province, eastern DRC, October 2026.

In a statement published on its X account on Tuesday and signed by Patrick Amoth, the Director-General for Health, the ministry said all nine cases belonged to one known cluster.

Kenya has confirmed a ninth case of Ebola, with health authorities saying all eight surviving patients are improving.

The latest Kenyan case involves a 24-year-old man who is a close relative of the first patient. He developed symptoms while in quarantine and tested positive on 19 October, according to the Kenyan Ministry of Health.

In a statement published on its X account on Tuesday and signed by Patrick Amoth, the Director-General for Health, the ministry said all nine cases belonged to one known cluster, with no evidence of transmission beyond the group.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Kenya's first patient was a 40-year-old man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) through Uganda before arriving in Nairobi on 3 October. He died at a Nairobi hospital on 5 October.

Treatment and contact tracing

The ministry said the eight surviving patients were stable and responding well to supportive care. It added that it had received 500 doses of medicine to support treatment for confirmed patients.

Contact tracing has also progressed, with 134 of the 135 identified contacts (99.3 per cent) traced and placed in quarantine.

The ministry said contacts who entered quarantine on 6 October and remain symptom-free would complete their 21-day monitoring period and begin returning home from 25 October.

It added that authorities had distributed protective equipment, diagnostic kits, and sample-collection materials to high-risk counties, and established a dedicated laboratory at Kenyatta National Hospital to support testing and prevent disruption to other hospital laboratory services.

Kenya, it noted, has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings. The cases in Kenya are linked to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the DRC, where the Bundibugyo virus has caused thousands of infections and deaths.

WHO reported more than 8,700 confirmed cases and more than 4,200 deaths in the DRC as of 6 October, with transmission continuing across dozens of health zones.

Nigeria confirms first case

The Kenyan update comes as Nigeria confronts its own Ebola infection, with the federal government confirming the first case in Abuja on Tuesday.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the patient was a woman who arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. She is receiving treatment in isolation at a private hospital in the Federal Capital Territory.

Close 

In a statement signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, the federal government said it had begun contact tracing and identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers, and travel contacts.

The government urged healthcare facilities nationwide to remain vigilant, promptly isolate suspected cases, maintain strict infection prevention measures and report suspected infections to public health authorities.

The development has heightened concerns about cross-border transmission, particularly as the outbreak in East and Central Africa coincides with frequent international travel and movement between countries.

Nigeria's response includes surveillance, laboratory testing, isolation and contact tracing to identify possible infections and limit further transmission.

World.title: Nigeria: 12 Years After First Outbreak, Nigeria Records Fresh Ebola Case
World.content:
A tent used to isolate Ebola patients is disinfected in Bunia, DR Congo (file photo).

Twelve years after Nigeria was declared free of Ebola following an outbreak that killed eight people, the country has confirmed a new case of the disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

The federal government disclosed the case on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, following laboratory confirmation of the infection in a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda.

The patient had been admitted to a private hospital in Abuja, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed.

The coordinating minister of health and social welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, announced the development in a statement, adding that the woman was in isolation and receiving medical care.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He said 44 close contacts had been identified as authorities intensified efforts to contain the infection and prevent further transmission.

According to the minister, contact tracing had commenced, with public health teams working to identify and monitor people who might have been exposed to the virus, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.

He added that surveillance had been intensified and the hospital where the patient received treatment was receiving immediate support to strengthen infection prevention and control measures.

Pate directed public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert and maintain a high index of suspicion for possible Ebola cases.

He also urged healthcare workers to identify and isolate suspected cases promptly, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected infections to public health authorities.

The minister advised Nigerians to remain calm but vigilant, stressing that early detection and compliance with public health measures were critical to preventing further transmission.

He said containing the infection would require public cooperation and coordinated action by the federal government, FCT authorities and other partners.

Pate assured Nigerians that investigations were ongoing and pledged that the government would continue to provide accurate and timely updates.

Remembering Nigeria's 2014 Ebola Battle

Nigeria's first major encounter with Ebola occurred in July 2014, when an infected Liberian-American, Patrick Sawyer, arrived in Lagos by air.

Sawyer was admitted to a private hospital, where he died five days later. His arrival triggered an outbreak investigation in Lagos, a densely populated commercial city with extensive domestic and international travel connections.

The incident posed a significant risk of wider transmission because Sawyer had interacted with people at the airport and in healthcare facilities before his infection was confirmed.

However, Nigeria's response, including the sacrifice of the late Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, demonstrated how rapid case identification, contact tracing, isolation, coordinated emergency management and public awareness could help contain a dangerous infectious disease.

According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), the outbreak resulted in 20 cases and eight deaths, including the index case. Nigeria was officially declared free of Ebola transmission on October 20, 2014, after completing the required 42-day period without a new case.

The response involved the Federal Ministry of Health, Lagos State authorities, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), international health partners and other stakeholders.

An emergency operations structure was established to coordinate the response, investigate suspected infections, identify contacts and monitor people who might have been exposed.

Public awareness campaigns and engagement with community, traditional and religious leaders also helped communicate the risks associated with the disease.

The successful containment of the 2014 outbreak established Nigeria as an example of how a country could interrupt transmission even when confronted with a potentially devastating epidemic.

However, the confirmation of another case 12 years later underscores the fact that previous success does not eliminate the risk of new infections entering the country.

Nigeria's Ebola Preparedness

Before the latest confirmation, Nigeria had intensified its preparedness following the spread of Ebola in parts of Central and East Africa.

On October 6, 2026, the NCDC announced heightened vigilance after Kenya confirmed an imported case linked to an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

At the time, the agency said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola case.

It also disclosed that preparedness activities were being strengthened in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Port Health Services, state governments and other partners.

The measures included surveillance, early detection, laboratory diagnosis, isolation and referral, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, risk communication, and the protection of healthcare workers.

The NCDC also reported that a national Ebola preparedness tabletop simulation exercise had been conducted to test response arrangements and identify gaps requiring attention.

LEADERSHIP reports that President Bola Tinubu established a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats in June 2026. The task force was created to strengthen national preparedness and prevent the importation and spread of the disease following outbreaks in the DRC and elsewhere in the region.

It is chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, and comprises representatives of relevant ministries, departments and agencies, state governments and public health partners.

Its responsibilities include coordinating the national response, overseeing the implementation of Nigeria's Ebola preparedness plan, reviewing surveillance reports and coordinating decisions on emergency measures.

As part of the preparations, Tinubu approved the release of N10 billion in emergency intervention funding to strengthen the NCDC's operational capacity and support critical public health response activities.

The confirmation in Abuja now puts these preparedness arrangements to a practical test.

Expert Calls for Calm, Effective Risk Communication

Meanwhile, an infectious disease expert, Dr Oladipo Elijah Kolawole, has urged Nigerians to remain calm but vigilant following the federal government's confirmation of an Ebola case in the FCT.

Kolawole, an associate professor of infectious diseases, pathogen genomics and molecular epidemiology at Adeleke University and founder of Helix Biogen Institute, told LEADERSHIP that early detection and strict adherence to public health measures were critical to containing the disease and preventing wider transmission.

He advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid direct contact with the bodily fluids of sick individuals and promptly report suspected cases to health authorities.

The expert stressed that public vigilance and evidence-based interventions, rather than panic, were essential to managing the situation.

He urged the government to prioritise rapid case investigation, contact tracing, laboratory confirmation and effective risk communication to contain the infection.

Kolawole also called for stronger infection prevention and control measures in healthcare facilities, noting that transparency, preparedness and a coordinated public health response would be crucial to preventing further transmission.

Close 

How Ebola Spreads and What Nigerians Should Know

Ebola is a severe viral disease that can cause serious illness and death.

The virus spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died, or through contact with contaminated objects and materials.

It is not spread simply because an infected person is in the same room, nor through ordinary casual contact without the necessary exposure.

Symptoms

Symptoms can include fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting and diarrhoea. Some patients may develop bleeding, although this does not occur in every case.

The incubation period generally ranges from two to 21 days.

Precautions

The federal government has advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with the bodily fluids of anyone suspected of having the disease and report possible exposure to public health authorities.

Anyone who develops compatible symptoms after possible exposure should contact public health authorities for guidance rather than visiting a healthcare facility without prior notification.

People identified by contact-tracing teams should cooperate with health officials and follow instructions on monitoring and other recommended public health measures.

Assurance to Nigerians

The Federal Ministry of Health has said Nigeria successfully contained Ebola in 2014 and has the experience and public health systems to respond to the current case.

However, the ministry stressed that containing the disease requires everyone to play their part.

World.title: Nigeria: On That U.S.-Nigeria Mining Deal
World.content:
opinion

SOStainabilityWeekly

By Oke Epia, E-mail: sostainability01@gmail.com | WhatsApp: +234 8034000706

Washing and Hushing

Three weeks ago, this page demanded the public release of details of the much-publicised framework agreement on mining between Nigeria and the US. We believe we were echoing valid concerns among global industry watchers and stakeholders across the board who had begun to raise several questions about the deal. On Monday, ThisDay Newspaper published what appears to be the text of the agreement on pages 14 and 15. Although the publication was not attributed and the names and signatures of the officials were omitted, the fact that there is a movement in the transparency needle that should ordinarily thread such important bilateral cooperation between the two countries is worthy of mention.

However, the publication has raised cogent questions that deserve to be answered by the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and the United States Government. In the spirit of dialogue and to encourage more transparency and mobilisation of public support for the just exploration, processing, and value-addition of Nigeria's rare earth and transition minerals, there needs to be more awareness of the community safeguards, beneficiation, and social licence to operate covered in this framework. There needs to be more information and engagement on how Nigerian entities, especially the private sector, can benefit, to create multiplier effects on the economy. There needs to be more assurance on how the Nigerian government intends to protect and promote national interest in the face of the fierce geopolitics over these transition minerals. There are many more questions, so let the engagement continue.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Faces Prolonged Fuel Cost Pressure As Oil Price Relief Unlikely Before 2028
World.content:
Zimbabwe's fuel-import-dependent economy could remain exposed to international oil market volatility into 2027 after the International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that global energy markets are unlikely to return to normal next year.

IEA executive director Fatih Birol said there was no credible pathway for oil markets to normalise in 2027 as the conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt supplies, shipping routes and refining capacity.

Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, was trading above US$111 per barrel on Tuesday, October 20, reflecting renewed concerns over supply disruptions and the potential escalation of the conflict.

The crisis has placed additional pressure on global fuel markets, particularly diesel, as damage to refineries and constrained exports limit the availability of refined petroleum products.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Birol said the possibility of further disruptions could not be ruled out, warning that overlapping crises in the Middle East could prolong market instability.

The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global energy supplies, remains a major concern for oil traders and importers. Before the conflict, approximately one-fifth of global oil and natural gas supplies passed through the waterway.

The International Energy Agency has already coordinated the release of up to 400 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves held by member countries to help cushion the impact of supply disruptions. Further releases could be considered if market conditions deteriorate.

For Zimbabwe, sustained increases in international oil prices present risks for fuel import costs, transport operators, manufacturers, farmers and other businesses that rely on petroleum products.

Higher fuel costs can feed into freight charges, production expenses and the distribution of goods, potentially putting additional pressure on consumer prices and business margins.

Transport and logistics companies are particularly exposed because fuel is a major operating expense. An extended period of elevated diesel prices could force operators to increase charges or absorb higher costs, depending on competition and demand.

Agriculture and manufacturing could also face increased production costs through fuel-dependent machinery, generators and the transportation of raw materials and finished products.

Zimbabwe's exposure will depend on international crude and refined-product prices, regional supply conditions, exchange-rate movements and domestic fuel pricing arrangements.

Close 

The IEA's October oil market report projects global oil demand to fall by 2.6 million barrels per day in 2026 as higher prices, supply constraints and weaker economic conditions weigh on consumption. Although demand is expected to recover partially in 2027, the agency says global oil use will remain below 2025 levels.

The agency has also warned that depleted inventories and continuing supply disruptions could leave fuel markets vulnerable to further shocks.

For businesses, the outlook reinforces the importance of monitoring fuel-related expenses, reviewing logistics contracts and incorporating energy price volatility into operating budgets.

While a recovery in supply could eventually ease pressure on international markets, the IEA's assessment suggests that companies and fuel-importing economies should not assume a swift return to stable prices in the coming year.

The duration of the Middle East conflict, the restoration of disrupted production and refining capacity, and the security of major shipping routes will remain key determinants of the global oil price outlook.

World.title: Kurt Suzuki one-and-done with Angels after first 100-loss season as Moreno era nears end
World.content:
The Los Angeles Angels’ new ownership era will bring another familiar change: a new manager in the dugout.

Only the Colorado Rockies finished the 2026 regular season with more losses than the Angels. Los Angeles’ 100 defeats ultimately ended Kurt Suzuki’s one-season tenure, with the team declining its 2027 option on his contract.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Baseball operations consultant John Mozeliak announced the decision in a statement Wednesday. "Kurt has earned tremendous respect in our clubhouse, and I’ve seen firsthand how much he cares about our players," Mozeliak said. "I do not believe our record this year was a true reflection of his true abilities as a manager."

STAN KROENKE'S RECORD-SETTING LA ANGELS PURCHASE SHOULD MAKE LONGTERM MLB LOCKOUT LESS LIKELY

Suzuki’s time with the Angels may not be over, as the team has offered him an opportunity to remain with the organization as a special assistant.

Mozeliak said he made the decision in coordination with Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, which agreed Sept. 1 to purchase a controlling interest in the Angels from Arte Moreno.

The sale is not expected to close until next year, but the group led by Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke is already making significant changes to the beleaguered franchise.

The Angels ended the season at 62-100 under Suzuki, which marked the first 100-loss season in franchise history. Suzuki ended his 16-year major league playing career as a catcher for the Halos in 2021-22. Suzuki had never been a manager at any level before he was hired exactly one year ago by general manager Perry Minasian.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Suzuki had previously worked as Minasian's special assistant for the previous three seasons.

Minasian was fired by Moreno last June, and longtime St. Louis Cardinals general manager Mozeliak stepped in on a temporary basis to run the front office while leading the search for a permanent GM to replace him. However, that transition plan has been thrown into flux by Moreno’s decision to sell

Mozeliak’s current contract ends in December, with the possibility of an MLB work stoppage looming.

Angels pitching coach Mike Maddux and two staffers were let go in August after Mozeliak determined the team was not fully leveraging the technology and analytics available to its pitchers.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Suzuki’s replacement will be the seventh manager to lead the Angels in nine seasons since it parted with Mike Scioscia after the 2018 season. The Angels have had 11 consecutive losing seasons and 12 straight non-playoff seasons, both the longest active skids in the major leagues.

Two other MLB teams, the Seattle Mariners and Houston Astros, are also searching for new managers.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Kristaps Porzingis weighs NBA future as Warriors explore trade options amid recurring POTS symptoms
World.content:
Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis is away from the team indefinitely and reportedly weighing whether he has a future in basketball.

Porzingis is reportedly dealing with recurring symptoms tied to Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), which can cause dizziness and fatigue.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Porzingis addressed speculation about his health in an Oct. 14 post on X.

"I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap," he wrote, adding that he was "getting better and better." He also said it had been "frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint," alongside injuries throughout his career, and jokingly swatted online rumors on his health, posting, "I don’t have HIV or AIDS."

WARRIORS STAR KRISTAPS PORZINGIS ADDRESSES 'INTERNET DOCTORS' AMID HEALTH ABSENCE: 'I DON'T HAVE HIV OR AIDS'

As Porzingis considers his future, Golden State is reportedly exploring trade options. The Warriors signed him to a two-year, $40 million extension over the summer. He is owed $20 million this season, but only $3 million of his $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed.

The Warriors declined to comment on trade speculation or reports about Porzingis’ health. The team said conversations with Porzingis and his representatives would remain private and that it did not expect him to be around the team in the immediate future.

The New York Knicks selected Porzingis fourth overall in the 2015 NBA Draft. He later played for the Dallas Mavericks, Washington Wizards, Boston Celtics and Atlanta Hawks before joining Golden State.

His best season came with Boston in 2023-24, when he averaged 20.1 points and 7.2 rebounds and helped the Celtics win the NBA title. He is also a 2018 All-Star.

Boston traded him to Atlanta in 2025 after he played 99 regular-season games over two seasons with the Celtics. The deal helped the team reduce payroll and avoid second-apron restrictions.

Porzingis’ contract could appeal to a team looking to shed longer-term salary: It could acquire him in a trade, then waive him next summer before the rest of his salary becomes guaranteed, leaving it responsible for the $3 million guarantee.

His basketball future remains uncertain as he focuses on his health and the Warriors consider their options.
