Since emerging from Berlin’s underground electronic scene, the duo have built an international following through their studio albums, live performances and collaborations with artists including Radiohead frontman Thom Yorke, Tommy Cash, Flohio and Blixa Bargeld.

They also formed Moderat with producer Apparat and run the independent record label Monkeytown Records.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Festival Spectaculare (@spectaculare_music)

Berlin-based multi-instrumentalist Philipp Johann Thimm will open the evening. A longtime collaborator of Apparat, Thimm has worked across electronic and acoustic music as well as audiovisual projects. His work on Apparat’s album *LP5* contributed to a Grammy-nominated project, while his solo work explores the meeting point between electronic composition and live instrumentation.

World.title: Hungary shuts down bank: What happens to customers’ money?
World.content:
Hungary’s central bank has revoked Trive Bank’s operating licence and ordered its liquidation after finding that the lender no longer has sufficient capital to continue operating. Depositors are set to receive compensation within seven working days, up to the statutory limit.

The Hungarian National Bank (MNB) announced the decision on Wednesday, adding that the move would not threaten the stability of the country’s financial system.

The bank had fewer than 100 depositors, while its outstanding household loans amounted to less than HUF 2 billion (EUR 5.3 million). According to the MNB, its lending portfolio represented well below 0.01% of Hungary’s total banking market.

Will customers get their money back?

The National Deposit Insurance Fund (OBA) will pay eligible depositors within seven working days, up to the statutory compensation limit of EUR 100,000 per depositor per credit institution.

At the current exchange rate, this is worth more than HUF 36 million. The actual amount paid will depend on each depositor’s eligible balance and the applicable rules.

Customers do not need to submit a separate application to the OBA. The compensation process will be based on information provided to the fund by Trive Bank.

The MNB has appointed Financial Stability and Liquidation Non-Profit Ltd. (PSFN) to oversee the liquidation, in accordance with the relevant legislation. The process officially begins on the date the central bank’s decision is communicated.

Why was Trive Bank shut down?

The MNB said its ongoing supervisory activities had revealed that Trive Bank’s capital position no longer allowed it to continue operating in the market. The lender primarily offered small-value online personal loans, advertising a process that could reportedly take as little as 15 minutes.

The central bank had previously ordered the bank to ensure continuous compliance with legal requirements concerning its own capital, and had also imposed a fine. However, the bank failed to meet those requirements, according to the MNB.

The regulator said the decision was intended to ensure an orderly and regulated withdrawal from the market while protecting customers and maintaining confidence in Hungary’s banking sector.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

What is Trive Bank?

Trive Bank, which has Turkish roots, entered the Hungarian market offering digital lending services. Its online model focused on providing personal loans through a streamlined application process. Despite the bank’s closure, the MNB stressed that its limited size meant the decision would have no meaningful impact on Hungary’s financial markets.

The priority is the orderly settlement of the bank’s affairs and the repayment of eligible deposits under the deposit guarantee scheme.

World.title: Hungarian university breaks into world’s Top 100 with international business master’s
World.content:
Corvinus University of Budapest has secured a place among the world’s top 100 institutions in the 2027 QS International Trade Rankings, with its International Economy and Business Master’s programme ranking 99th globally. The university also achieved an impressive 32nd place in the Executive MBA category, becoming the only institution from Central and Eastern Europe to feature in that list.

The rankings, published by international higher education ranking organisation Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) on 14 October, assess programmes that prepare students for careers in international business and trade.

Corvinus is the only Hungarian university represented in either of the two rankings.

Corvinus excels in graduate outcomes and career support

The university performed particularly well in several individual indicators in the 2027 rankings. In the Executive MBA category, Corvinus ranked 15th worldwide for graduate outcomes and career support. It also achieved joint 18th place for innovative teaching and 20th for research performance.

Its International Economy and Business Master’s programme performed strongly in graduate outcomes, ranking 58th globally in the Master’s and MBA category, despite placing 99th overall.

These indicators assess different aspects of the programmes, offering prospective students a more detailed picture of their strengths beyond their overall positions.

Bruno van Pottelsberghe, rector of Corvinus University of Budapest, said the rankings provided valuable feedback for students, employers and the university itself. He added that the institution aimed to equip graduates with knowledge and skills relevant to the global marketplace, enabling them to tackle real-world business challenges with confidence.

If you missed it: Hungary’s Corvinus University breaks into global business rankings with multiple top positions

How does QS assess international trade programmes?

The QS International Trade Rankings are produced in collaboration with the Hinrich Foundation, with separate lists for Executive MBA programmes designed for experienced professionals and Master’s and MBA programmes.

To qualify, institutions must hold internationally recognised accreditation or an appropriate QS Stars rating. Their programmes must meet specific international trade curriculum requirements, while universities must also demonstrate sufficient research performance and academic reputation. QS assesses a maximum of one programme per institution in each ranking.

The methodology evaluates six criteria: international trade curriculum content, institutional reputation, graduate outcomes, industry engagement, innovative teaching and research.

Curriculum content accounts for 30% of the overall score in both rankings. Graduate outcomes and industry engagement each contribute 15%, while institutional reputation carries greater weight in the Executive MBA category.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Which universities lead the 2027 rankings?

The top positions went to institutions in the United States and the United Kingdom. In the Master’s and MBA category, the Thunderbird School of Global Management at Arizona State University took first place with its Master of Global Management programme.

The University of Cambridge led the Executive MBA rankings with its Global Executive MBA programme.

Against this international competition, Corvinus’s 32nd-place finish in the Executive MBA category and its Master’s programme’s entry into the global top 100 mark notable results for Hungarian higher education.

World.title: BREAKING: International arrest warrant issued for György Matolcsy’s son
World.content:
Hungarian authorities have issued an international arrest warrant for Ádám Matolcsy, the son of former central bank governor György Matolcsy, in connection with suspected economic fraud. Another man, György Stofa, is also wanted.

Ádám Matolcsy wanted over suspected economic fraud

An arrest warrant has been issued for Ádám Matolcsy, son of former National Bank of Hungary (MNB) governor György Matolcsy, according to the Hungarian police website. The warrant was issued on Wednesday afternoon by the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office in connection with suspected economic fraud.

Authorities are also seeking György Stofa, with reports indicating that international arrest warrants have been issued for both men. Their names appeared on the police website shortly after prosecutors announced developments in the ongoing investigation involving the central bank and its foundations.

Read more about the Matolcsy case:

Former Hungarian central bank governor Matolcsy detained

Prosecutors seek to arrest former Hungarian central bank chief Matolcsy

Development follows former central bank chief’s detention

The move comes on the same day that prosecutors detained György Matolcsy and questioned him as a suspect in a case involving the management of assets linked to the central bank’s foundations.

Prosecutors allege that a securities-lending agreement signed in February 2025 was used in an attempt to transfer control over the PADME Foundation’s assets to people who would remain under Matolcsy’s influence after he left office. According to the prosecution, the alleged arrangement was intended to enable the former governor and his son to make investments for their own benefit.

The alleged transaction involved Optima and the Central European III Private Equity Fund, represented by Quartz Befektetési Alapkezelő Zrt. Prosecutors say the agreement transferred ownership control over an asset manager overseeing assets with a market value of nearly HUF 200 billion (approximately EUR 547 million). The precise financial damage has not yet been established.

Prosecutors seek Matolcsy’s pre-trial detention

György Matolcsy was questioned for several hours on Wednesday but did not make a statement about the allegations, according to his lawyer, Pál Bátki. He was transferred to a police detention facility after the interrogation.

The Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office has requested his pre-trial detention, with a judge expected to decide whether to order it. Prosecutors have also detained two other people in connection with the case, while seeking international arrest warrants for two further individuals.

World.title: Prosecutors seek to arrest former Hungarian central bank chief Matolcsy – UPDATE: video of arrival at prison
World.content:
Prosecutors have requested the pre-trial detention of former National Bank of Hungary governor György Matolcsy following a lengthy interrogation over suspected economic fraud. A judge is expected to decide on Friday whether he will be remanded in custody.

Matolcsy did not make a statement during questioning

György Matolcsy’s questioning as a suspect ended shortly before 3.30 PM on Wednesday, 21 October, according to reports by Hungarian news outlets Telex and Index. His lawyer, Pál Bátki, said his client had not made a statement about the allegations during the several-hour interrogation, speaking only about his personal circumstances.

Bátki added that the investigating prosecutors had outlined the circumstances on which they based the suspicion against the former central bank governor and had requested his pre-trial detention.

“It was very difficult to process this five-page document containing a great deal of information. Until we see what evidence forms the basis of it, we cannot respond to it,” the lawyer said.

Matolcsy is suspected of economic fraud causing significant financial damage and the misdemeanour of using a forged private document.

Judge to decide on pre-trial detention

After the interrogation, Matolcsy was transferred from the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office to a police detention facility, where he is expected to remain until the hearing on the prosecution’s request. A judge is expected to rule on Friday whether to order his pre-trial detention. The court could also decide on a less restrictive measure, such as criminal supervision, instead of keeping him in custody.

Under Hungarian procedure, detention following arrest can last for up to 72 hours before a decision on further measures must be made.

Bátki had previously said that the defence had lodged a complaint against Matolcsy’s detention. He also argued that pre-trial detention would be unjustified, citing his client’s age, stable living conditions and close family ties.

If you missed it: BREAKING: Former Hungarian central bank governor Matolcsy detained

UPDATE: Video of Matolcsy arriving at prison in police car

Telex, among others, was present at the prison on Gyorskocsi Street, Budapest, when the police car carrying György Matolcsy arrived at the entrance. As can be seen in the video, there was a slight delay due to the gate not being open: the police car drove off, did a lap around the block, and then returned:

Prosecutors outline alleged scheme involving foundation assets

In a more detailed statement released on Wednesday afternoon, the Central Investigative Prosecutor’s Office outlined the specific transaction at the centre of this strand of the National Bank case. Prosecutors allege that Matolcsy and his associates used a sham securities-lending agreement signed on 28 February 2025 — one of the former central bank governor’s final working days — in an attempt to transfer control over the assets of the PADME Foundation to people who would remain under his influence after he left office.

The foundation originated from the Pallas Athéné foundations established by the central bank under Matolcsy’s leadership in 2014. According to prosecutors, these foundations received more than HUF 266 billion (approximately EUR 700 million) from the central bank’s exchange-rate gains. They merged in 2019 under the name PADME, with their assets managed by Optima Befektetési Zrt.

The alleged transaction involved Optima and the Central European III Private Equity Fund, represented by Quartz Befektetési Alapkezelő Zrt. Prosecutors claim the agreement was not a genuine securities-lending arrangement, but a means of transferring control over the foundation’s assets to a circle of people whom Matolcsy could continue to influence after his term as governor ended.

According to the prosecution, the alleged purpose was to enable Matolcsy and his son, Ádám, to make investments serving their own interests and to generate personal gains. The transaction transferred the shares of Optima Befektetési Alapkezelő Zrt. to the private equity fund, shifting ownership control over an asset manager overseeing assets with a market value of nearly HUF 200 billion (around EUR 547 million).

Prosecutors said the precise financial damage has not yet been established, but that it substantially exceeded the HUF 500 million threshold for particularly significant financial damage under Hungarian law.

Alongside Matolcsy, two other people were detained, while prosecutors also sought international arrest warrants for two further individuals. Searches were conducted at several locations and evidence was seized.

Investigation into the National Bank case continues

Investigating prosecutors detained Matolcsy early on Wednesday morning as part of the ongoing case involving the National Bank of Hungary (MNB). Investigative measures were also carried out at several locations.

According to Telex, other people were also detained in connection with the case, including the regular lawyer for companies belonging to Matolcsy’s son, Ádám, and a senior official at a company linked to Ádám Matolcsy and István Száraz.

World.title: Paks nuclear power plant hit by turbine failure: only one unit runs at full capacity
World.content:
A turbine-generator failure has forced Unit 1 of Hungary’s Paks Nuclear Power Plant to operate at half capacity. With another unit undergoing maintenance and a third out of service for an overhaul, only one of the plant’s four units is currently running at full power.

The incident occurred at 8:02 AM on Wednesday, when one of Unit 1’s turbine-generator units shut down following the activation of generator protection, MVM Paks Nuclear Power Plant announced.

As a result, the unit’s output fell by more than 100 megawatts and it is now operating at 50% capacity

Three of four units operating at reduced capacity or offline

Unit 1 is not the only part of the facility affected by reduced output. According to reports, Unit 2 was also scaled back to 50% capacity from Wednesday because of maintenance ahead of a major overhaul. Unit 4 has been undergoing a major overhaul since 18 September and is not generating electricity. This leaves Unit 3 as the only unit currently operating at full capacity.

Data from Hungary’s National Atomic Energy Authority showed that the plant was already generating around 1,274 megawatts on Tuesday, compared with its nominal capacity of just over 2,000 megawatts. The latest incident has further reduced the plant’s available output, although the operator has not announced how long Unit 1 will remain at half capacity.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Is the Danube’s low water level to blame?

The turbine failure was attributed to the activation of generator protection, not to the Danube’s low water level. The operator has not reported any connection between the two issues.

Nevertheless, low river levels have posed significant challenges for the plant in recent months, as the Danube supplies the cooling water needed for its operation.

On 13 October, Paks recorded the lowest water level ever measured there, according to Index. A submerged sill constructed over the summer raised the water level by around 61 centimetres, helping the plant avoid further production restrictions.

During the summer, seven of the plant’s eight turbines had to be shut down at one point because insufficient water was reaching their cooling systems. The military transported 38,000 tonnes of rock to the area to help construct the submerged sill between Paks and Dunapataj.

If you missed it: Átlátszó: Hungarian government building Paks bottom sill without environmental permit

The plant has already faced a historic shutdown

Drought conditions and exceptionally low Danube water levels forced the plant to gradually reduce output during the summer. On 2 August, it was shut down completely for the first time in its history. Paks returned to full output on 26 August, following improvements in water conditions and the measures taken to maintain water levels near the cooling-water intake.

World.title: “Prepare for your death” – Another 27 schools in Hungary receives bomb threats, message leaked
World.content:
A new wave of bomb threats has targeted 27 schools in Hungary’s Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County, with a further threat reported at a school in Budapest. Police are inspecting the affected buildings, and no explosives have been found at sites searched so far, authorities said.

Another 27 bomb threats two days after the previous messages

Hungary’s National Bureau of Investigation (Nemzeti Nyomozóiroda, NNI) is examining whether the latest threats are connected to previous incidents involving educational institutions. Dávid Janiczak, the mayor of Ózd, confirmed on social media that 27 schools in Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén County had been named in the latest threat and published a copy of the message.

The bomb threats were reported on Wednesday, 21 October. According to the authorities, a threatening email listing several schools in Northern Hungary was sent to the functional email address of a news website. A Budapest school received a separate message directly in its own inbox.

What does the message say?

The perpetrators in the email first mention the settlements, then list the institutions involved, while claiming they “have come for the young”. In the paragraph second to last, they claim the primary attack means detonating the explosive devices placed in the listed schools, and “if it does not seem effective enough”, their armed members “will continue to hold the targets accountable at the scene”. In the closing, they warn everybody to “prepare for death”, and they signed it as “your honorable fellow compatriots”.

Police inspect affected schools

Police are visiting the institutions concerned and coordinating their response with school management, following the procedures established during earlier incidents. In a statement, the National Bureau of Investigation said officers had found no explosives or devices suitable for detonation in buildings already searched. Inspections were continuing at the remaining locations.

The Pestújhelyi Primary School in Budapest’s 15th district was also targeted. District mayor Angéla Cserdiné Németh said the school had received another threatening message that morning and that police had begun inspecting the affected buildings. She added that children had been moved to safety at the Pestújhely Community Centre.

The school had also received a bomb threat the previous week. The National Bureau of Investigation has opened proceedings over threats to commit a terrorist act. Investigators are examining possible links between the latest messages and threats reported on 15 October and in other recent cases.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Series of threats raises concern

The latest incidents follow a series of bomb threats affecting schools across Hungary. On Monday, 19 October, more than 70 educational institutions reportedly received messages threatening that explosive devices had been planted on their premises. Police searched the affected buildings but found no explosives.

Further threats were reported on Tuesday, including at several practice schools and kindergartens associated with Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), as well as the Miklós Radnóti Practice School in Budapest’s Zugló district, where an extraordinary school closure was ordered.

Threats were also reported in Serbia on Monday, affecting schools in several cities, including Subotica, Novi Sad and Belgrade. Authorities have not established whether the incidents in Hungary and Serbia are connected. Hungarian investigators continue to examine the messages and their possible links to earlier threats as police work to ensure the safety of pupils and staff.

Stay up-to-date: More than 70 Hungarian schools targeted by bomb threats on Monday morning

World.title: Péter Magyar to AP News: public funds, similiarities with Viktor Orbán, chasing corruption
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar has pledged to hold former officials accountable for alleged corruption under Viktor Orbán while maintaining Hungary’s strict immigration policies, in his first interview with a global news organisation since taking office.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar gave an exclusive interview

Speaking exclusively to The Associated Press (AP) on Tuesday, the prime minister said his government was working to recover public assets allegedly misused during Orbán’s 16 years in power. However, he stressed that investigations must respect the rule of law.

“The Hungarian people obviously want to see results in holding those responsible accountable, punishing them and recovering stolen property,” Péter Magyar said. His centre-right, pro-European Tisza party defeated Orbán’s Fidesz in April, ending more than a decade and a half of government marked by disputes with the European Union (EU) over corruption, democratic standards and migration.

New push to recover public funds

Magyar’s government has established a National Asset Recovery and Protection Office with investigative and prosecutorial powers. He described it as a “superauthority” capable of coordinating with police, prosecutors and tax officials to speed up complex corruption investigations. Hungary has also applied to join the European Public Prosecutor’s Office, which investigates crimes involving EU funds — a significant departure from Orbán’s refusal to join.

Although some former officials have already been detained on suspicion of corruption-related offences, Péter Magyar acknowledged public frustration over the pace of progress. He insisted, however, that building a democratic state governed by law would take time. Reforms have helped pave the way for the EU to announce the release of EUR 16.4 billion in funding for Hungary that had been frozen under the previous government.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Migration remains a sticking point

Despite improved relations with Brussels, the 45-year-old politician said Hungary would retain strict border controls, including razor-wire fencing and the practice of escorting irregular migrants back across the southern border into Serbia. Hungary was fined EUR 200 million by the EU’s Court of Justice in 2024, plus EUR 1 million for every subsequent day of non-compliance with an earlier asylum ruling.

Magyar said Hungary had already lost EUR 1 billion through the penalties and expected an agreement to end the dispute by the end of the year. He also linked the issue to negotiations over the EU’s next seven-year budget, arguing that a common budget would be difficult to approve while the dispute remained unresolved.

Ukraine ties improve, but differences remain

Prime minister Péter Magyar has sought to repair relations with Ukraine, which deteriorated under Orbán. He welcomed new legislation expanding minority-language education rights, calling it an opportunity to open a new chapter in bilateral relations. However, he opposes fast-tracking Ukraine’s EU membership, arguing that accession should be merit-based and that a country at war should not join the bloc.

Stay up-to-date: PM Péter Magyar reveals how Hungary will fund minimum wage tax cuts in 2027

Wealth tax to fund social measures

Domestically, Péter Magyar’s proposed 2027 budget includes a 1% annual tax on net wealth exceeding HUF 1 billion (more than EUR 2.7 million), rising to 1.5% on wealth above HUF 100 billion (EUR 273.5 million). The government estimates the measure could affect around 15,000 people and raise HUF 200 billion (almost EUR 547 million) annually.

The revenue would help fund tax cuts for lower earners, doubled child benefits and an increase in the minimum monthly pension from HUF 28,500 to HUF 120,000 (from EUR 77.95 to EUR 328.23). Magyar defended the measures as a matter of fairness, saying that supporting poorer households does not make him a socialist or a left-wing politician, but reflected “humanity” and “social justice”.

Read also: Fidesz co-founder and former house speaker has surprising claims on party’s mistakes

World.title: MOL signs deal to buy Russian stake in Serbia’s NIS oil company – UPDATE: MOL reaction
World.content:
Hungarian oil and gas group MOL has signed an agreement to acquire the Russian-owned stake in Serbia’s NIS oil company, Serbian Finance Minister Siniša Mali has announced. The deal still requires regulatory approval, including clearance from US authorities.

The Russian shareholders and MOL have agreed on the sale, while the Serbian state has signed a separate shareholder agreement with the Hungarian company, Mali told Bloomberg Adria television, according to Hungarian news agency MTI.

The minister expects applications for regulatory approval to be submitted shortly to the competition authorities in Serbia and, as far as he knows, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The ownership change could then be completed within a relatively short period.

UPDATE: MOL says no relevant change has occurred

Several hours after Mali’s announcement, MOL issued a statement on the Budapest Stock Exchange website responding to the news reports.

The Hungarian oil and gas company said there had been no change in the ongoing NIS transaction that would require it to inform capital market participants.

MOL added that it would provide information promptly in accordance with applicable regulations if any new, relevant developments occurred.

The statement did not directly explain the discrepancy between the Serbian minister’s announcement that the sale agreement had been signed and MOL’s position. Therefore, it’s unclear precisely what has been agreed between the parties and whether the transaction has reached a new stage.

Serbia to increase its stake in NIS

Under the agreement, the Serbian state would increase its ownership in NIS from around 30% to 35%. Mali said a written agreement had already been reached, as Belgrade wanted its stake to exceed one-third.

However, the minister did not disclose the purchase price or the exact shareholding MOL would acquire.

The announcement is a significant step forward in negotiations that have dragged on for months. In early October, Serbian Forbes reported that talks had effectively collapsed because the Russian owners were unwilling to sell. MOL did not confirm that report at the time, saying the process was ongoing and the transaction would require several regulatory approvals.

MOL’s Százhalombatta refinery. Photo: MOL Group

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

US sanctions make the deal urgent

On 19 January, MOL signed a binding letter of intent with Russian oil company Gazprom Neft to acquire the Russian shareholders’ combined 56.15% stake in NIS.

In June, MOL also reached an agreement with the Serbian government on the company’s future management and the possibility of the state acquiring an additional five percentage points. The agreement also envisages MOL maintaining operations at the Pančevo refinery for at least ten years, at a capacity comparable to its pre-sanctions level.

The transaction is driven in part by US sanctions imposed on NIS in October 2025 because of its Russian majority ownership. The company has since received several temporary exemptions allowing it to continue operating.

The US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) most recently authorised NIS to continue operating, including importing crude oil and refining it, until 30 October. MOL was also given permission to continue negotiations over the purchase until that date.

US approval is therefore another key hurdle before the transaction can be completed.

Why NIS matters to Serbia

NIS is one of Serbia’s most important energy companies and operates the country’s only oil refinery, in Pančevo. It is also involved in crude oil production and fuel retailing.

Gazprom Neft currently holds a 44.9% stake in the company, while its parent company, Gazprom, owns a further 11.3%. The Serbian state holds approximately 29.87%, with the remaining shares owned by minority shareholders.

World.title: Multiple Arrests Across Serbia Ahead of Crucial Elections
World.content:
At least seven individuals were arrested or detained on Wednesday by Serbian police on suspicion that they were planning violent actions for election day this Sunday. Five of the individuals were arrested in the northern city of Novi Sad.

The Higher Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade said that the arrests were done in coordination with the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Novi Sad and members of the Security Intelligence Agency (BIA).

The five individuals in Novi Sad, all aged either 27 or 28, were arrested “due to reasonable suspicion that on the day of the parliamentary elections, Sunday, October 25, 2026, with the intent of undermining the constitutional order and security of Serbia, they planned to commit acts of violence, riots, as well as attacks on political opponents and police officers.”

They are suspected of recruiting people for “physical clashes” on Sunday. As the prosecution added, the plan was to come to Belgrade “for the violent alteration of the constitutional order and the overthrow of the highest state bodies.”

The press release stated that “This plan would be executed by using mobile teams operating outside the legal framework to attack political opponents and police officers using tools and weapons”, and that “the means for committing the criminal offences – balaclavas, wooden poles, flares, knives, and weapons” were to be provided by a member of the group.

The suspects have been detained for up to 48 hours.

Lawyer Rastko Naumov told BIRN that his client Srdjan Ilic, an opposition activist from Belgrade, was detained on Wednesday morning because of alleged planned actions during election day.

“They came this morning with an order from the Higher Court in Belgrade to search the house due to the criminal offence of ‘preparing an act against the constitutional order and security of Serbia’,” Naumov said.

He added that all electronic devices were temporarily seized from Ilic, including computers, phones, hard drives and similar items.

After the house search, he was handed a summons to give a statement to the police, where he went voluntarily, after which he was detained for up to 48 hours.

The informal organisation “Belgrade Stays” (Beograd ostaje), of which Ilic was a member, said on the social media platform X that “police appeared at the addresses of several of their activists”, but gave no other details.

In the town of Vrnjacka Banja in central Serbia one more activist was arrested on Wednesday, according to claims from Katarina Obradovic, the municipal coordinator of the opposition Student List.

Obradovic told N1 television that police officers raided the home of a member of the citizens’ assembly of Vrnjacka Banja around half past five this morning, conducted a search and detained him.

“They searched everything from the attic to the basement for no particular reason, and nothing suspicious was found. They asked the lawyer if there were any weapons. In the house, they only found promotional material for the Student List meant for information booths, and nothing else,” she said. His electronic devices were also taken.

Serbia has been facing mass anti-government student protests for nearly two years. The student movement nominated their Student List consisting of professors and experts they chose for snap elections that will be held on Sunday. The Student List is currently the strongest opponent to former President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, which has been in power since 2012.

Ahead of some of the larger protests during this period, Serbian authorities repeatedly arrested some of the most prominent activists.

World.title: Albania’s Students Demand the Fall of Rama and an End to Corruption
World.content:
In a meeting with the heads of educational institutions on Tuesday, Prime Minister Edi Rama said that the ongoing student protests that began as an expression of public discontent, had turned into an organised attempt to destabilise the country and hinder the EU integration process. He warned that he will respond to the protests with a new package of penal and administrative sanctions.

After the meeting, he published a video on Facebook that showed him placing a sign with the word “Dialogue” and 12 red chairs at the entrance to the Prime Minister's Office, indicating an offer to talk.

Jesmina Sengla, a student involved in the protests, responded with the comment: “In your dreams.”

According to Sengla, "Rama never meant his request to engage in dialogue. His invitation is not sincere. He is responding to the pressure of the international community to ask the protesters for dialogue and to present himself as willing to change.”

World.title: Leader of Kosovo Opposition Party PDK Steps Down
World.content:
PDK leader Bedri Hamza. Photo: BIRN.

The head of the Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK) Bedri Hamza, announced on Wednesday he is stepping down from the role he took less than a year ago.

Hamza said that the decision to step down opens the way for an internal election process in which party members should decide about the future leadership. He suggested a greater role for youth in the process.

“Every leader must know when it is time to pave the way for a new phase. I just finished the presidency meeting and today I have irrevocably resigned from the position of leader of the Democratic Party of Kosovo,” he said. PDK is the largest opposition party in Kosovo currently.

“I am not leaving the PDK. I am only leaving the position of chairman, but not from the belief in our political values. As long as I live, I will be a loyal PDK voter and a member of this great political family,” he said.

Hamza’s resignation comes five weeks after a Hague-based war crimes court convicted Hashim Thaci and Kadri Veseli, two previous PDK leaders, of war crimes and sentenced them to 25 and 18 years of imprisonment, respectively.

The PDK emerged from the senior ranks of the guerrilla Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) following the end of the 1998-1999 war in Kosovo. For years it was led by Hashim Thaci, the KLA’s wartime political director.

It first took power in 2007 and oversaw Kosovo’s declaration of independence from Serbia the following year.

When Thaci became president of Kosovo in 2016, the leadership of the party passed to Kadri Veseli, who previously led the shadowy Kosovo Intelligence Service (SHIK).

After 12 years in power, the PDK slipped into third place in terms of parliamentary seats in elections in 2019. In the June elections this year, it won 22 out of 120 seats in the assembly, far behind the ruling party Vetevendosje of Prime Minister Albin Kurti, which won 53 seats.

World.title: Kosovo Court Sentences Serb for War Crimes
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Bos/Hrv/Srp



Milorad Djokovic at the Pristina Basic Court, October 21, 2026. Photo: BIRN

On Wednesday, the Pristina Basic Court found Kosovo Serb Milorad Djokovic guilty of war crimes during the war in Kosovo. He was sentenced to 10 years in prison.

Djokovic was found guilty of having been involved in murders, raids, beatings, arrests, torture and inhumane and cruel treatment of ethnic Albanian civilians in the village of Ozdrim in the western municipality of Peja/Pec, during the 1998-1999 war in Kosovo.

According to the prosecution, Djokovic was part of the Serbian armed forces that surrounded and attacked Ozdrim in May 1999.

“The village was surrounded and then attacked from three directions by Serb military and police forces. Six Albanian civilians were killed and three others were wounded during these actions,” the indictment said. The remains of five of the people who were killed have not been found.

“Those three wounded people were sent to Peja/Pec hospital and then executed and buried in the village of Lutogllave,” the indictment said.

According to the indictment, the armed group that included Djokovic arrested around 40 civilians. Twelve of them were released after three days “deprived of food and water and suffering torture”, while 28 others were sent to Peja/Pec prison and then transferred to Leskovac prison in Serbia after the war.

They were released after the intervention of the International Committee of the Red Cross, the indictment said.

After the verdict, Halit Gashi, one of the damaged parties in this case told media that “no sentence can bring back the lives of those who were unjustly taken”.

“I don’t know what kind of sentence this is. It’s ridiculous,” Gashi added.

Djokovic had pleaded not guilty in July 2023.

His arrest in 2022 sparked angry reactions from the Serbian government, which claimed that it was an example of the intimidation of Serbs in Kosovo.

World.title: Serbians Abroad Organize to Vote Amid Obstacles
World.content:
With polling stations few and far between, Serbians abroad are joining solidarity networks to arrange rides and accommodation, while some face voting in the middle of the night.

“Everything is done on a voluntary basis. People who have often never met before are now opening their homes to one another, picking people up at airports and helping them get to the polling station,” Duska Vujovic from Toronto told BIRN.

Canada has only two polling stations, in Toronto and Ottawa, forcing some voters to travel thousands of kilometres.

“Those travelling the furthest are coming from Vancouver and Victoria, covering approximately 4,000 kilometres each way. The journey also involves crossing several time zones,” Vujovic said.

Despite Serbian diplomatic and consular missions in western Canada, no stations were opened in Vancouver or Calgary, although more than 800 people had registered in Vancouver. Toronto-based volunteers are providing accommodation and transport.

In Italy and Spain, voters are using Facebook groups to organise shared journeys and accommodation. Many are also turning to VoteBnB, a platform whose creators reported 1,343 accommodation offers and 742 people offering rides.

The creators told BIRN the idea emerged after Serbs abroad learned they could not vote locally. A prototype was online by 3am, and hundreds signed up within days. More than 30 cities now have local organisers coordinating transport and accommodation, they said, describing the initiative as part of efforts to reverse Serbia’s democratic backsliding under Aleksandar Vucic.

Serbia’s authorities approved just 93 polling stations abroad, amid criticism that the network is inadequate for the number of registered voters. Sunday’s election pits Vucic’s ruling Serbian Progressive Party against opposition forces led by students, whose movement has become a major challenge to its long-standing dominance.

In Australia, voters from Brisbane are preparing to travel about 900 kilometres to Sydney by minibus, car or plane after the Serbian Electoral Commission (RIK) declined to open stations in several cities.

Nemanja Djurovic, a Serb living on the Gold Coast, said 130 people registered in Brisbane had contacted his group and expressed support for the student movement.

“People are furious, and everyone who could possibly take a day off work decided they didn’t care how much the ticket would cost,” he told BIRN. “We specifically want to travel by bus to send a message. We can’t exactly cycle or walk like the students have been doing, but through this journey, we want to join their fight.”

In France, voters from Toulouse, where 107 people registered but no station was opened, have arranged a minibus and shared cars to Paris. Another group from Montpellier has hired a minibus, while some travellers will collect students from Bordeaux en route.

Milena Mihajlovic, a member of an informal citizens’ group in Toulouse, told BIRN that organisers in Paris had arranged free accommodation for those needing it. Although not everyone who registered can make the journey, she said, turnout was expected to be high.

In California, US, where only one polling station was opened in Los Angeles, voters are also organising shared rides and accommodation. Milos Milenkovic, a Serbian citizen in San Francisco, told BIRN that organisers had recorded around 680 registrations across the state, while about 50 Los Angeles residents had offered their homes to travelling voters.

Voting in Los Angeles is scheduled from 11pm on October 24 until noon the following day, local time.

World.title: Russian Despatch: Kremlin Clings to Balkan Buddies Dodik and Vucic
World.content:
Over the past four and a half years, Russia’s war against Ukraine has devoured an immense number of human lives and resources but failed to lessen the Kremlin’s determination to pursue its aggressive tactics in hope of an eventual triumph. Vexed by the protracted stalemate at the front, Moscow is now annihilating Ukraine’s economic capacity with massive daily bombings. It has also embarked on a sabotage campaign in Europe to try to frighten Europeans into ending their assistance to Kyiv.

Now, as if being rewarded for its obduracy, Russia has scored a major diplomatic victory with the US. with Donald Trump’s administration temporarily suspending sanctions on Russian diesel in an attempt to bring down fuel prices ahead of US mid-term elections.

In the Balkans, the resilience of Moscow’s influence is also in evidence. Despite numerous setbacks in recent years, Russia is still eager to assist its local allies and ready to resort to intelligence operations in order to sabotage the region’s integration into the EU and NATO.

World.title: NATO’s ‘False Solidarity’: Fico Says Neutrality Would Better Suit Slovakia
World.content:
‘An invitation to Moscow’

Yet Fico’s comments could still have damaging effects in the real world and have been criticised both from within the governing camp in Slovakia as well as from the opposition and figures elsewhere in the region.

President Pellegrini, who was once the leader of the coalition Hlas party, said he accepted only one interpretation of the prime minister’s remarks: NATO members should avoid provoking Russia and risking an attack on an alliance country. “I do not accept any other interpretation and would reject it,” Pellegrini said, adding that Slovakia could not suggest it might stand aside during a conflict.

Parliamentary speaker Richard Rasi, from Pellegrini’s Hlas party, warned against treating collective-defence commitments as merely formal. “If we were to describe this commitment as merely formal or unenforceable, we would also have to accept that our allies might one day take the same position towards us,” he said.

Opposition politicians also inevitably criticised Fico. Progressive Slovakia leader Michal Simecka accused him of questioning the basic pillar of the country’s defence. Ivan Korcok, a former foreign minister, warned that publicly undermining confidence in NATO amounted to sending Moscow “an invitation”.

“If someone wanted to attack Slovakia, they know that they would not be facing a country of 5 million, but the strongest alliance in the world,” Korcok said.

Christian Democrat deputy leader Viliam Karas rejected neutrality as a realistic alternative, arguing that Slovakia lacked both the military strength and financial resources to defend itself independently.

“Whoever questions our readiness to help our allies also weakens their willingness to help us,” Karas said. “One day we may be the ones who need Article 5.”

The controversy also reached Prague. Czech President Petr Pavel, a former chairman of NATO’s Military Committee, called them “extremely serious” and warned against questioning solidarity between allies. It was not their first clash: the two have previously disagreed publicly over Russia’s war against Ukraine and how the conflict should be described.

Fico responded that Pavel, a former NATO general, “would like to fight”, while he preferred peace. Pavel said he had heard the same argument before, that a general wants war while others want peace, during the 2023 Czech presidential campaign.

Former Czech foreign minister Jan Lipavsky pointed to what Czech forces are already doing for Slovakia. Czech soldiers are serving in the country, while Czech aircraft have helped protect Slovak airspace. If Fico questions military assistance between allies, Lipavsky asked, why should the Czechs help defend Slovakia?

Prime Minister Andrej Babis said the Czech Republic was preparing to deploy two mechanised brigades if Russia attacked a Baltic NATO member. He had previously said Prague would respect Article 5, while declining to comment on Fico’s remarks.

Germany added its voice on September 29, when Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul visited Bratislava for talks with his Slovak counterpart, Juraj Blanar.

“The greatest threat to freedom on our continent comes from Moscow. The greatest danger to Europe is Putin’s belligerent imperialism,” Wadephul said. “Questioning these facts is not only lacking in solidarity, but it would also be irresponsible.”

Wadephul warned that countries casting doubt on NATO’s collective deterrence put themselves at risk and weakened security guarantees for other alliance members.

Security analyst Radovan Branik says Fico is technically correct about Article 5’s obligations: the clause does not automatically require every NATO member to deploy combat troops when another member is attacked and governments can provide different forms of assistance according to capabilities and circumstances. “On the facts, he is right,” Branik says.

His concern is how Fico’s statements affect deterrence. A potential aggressor cannot know in advance precisely how NATO members would respond to an attack. Branik argues that publicly discussing limits on Slovakia’s possible involvement could weaken that uncertainty.

Retired Slovak general Pavel Macko also questions how Slovakia could defend itself without allied guarantees. With roughly 16,000 soldiers, he argues, the country could not defend even one major city alone against a large-scale attack.

Macko rejects neutrality as a guarantee of security, citing Belgium, whose neutral status failed to prevent German invasions during the world wars.

“Not every country has the same capabilities,” he says, pointing to Iceland, which has no standing army, and Luxembourg, whose armed forces are small. “It is still one for all and all for one, but everyone within their capabilities.”

Macko says Slovakia could restrict how its troops are deployed under NATO command, but limiting them to Slovak territory would be deeply at odds with allied solidarity.

Practical constraints remain, too: Slovakia still lacks the fully capable heavy mechanised brigade NATO expects under its force requirements. According to Macko, it may not be ready until 2035 or later.

Pavel Havlicek of the Prague-based Association for International Affairs (AMO) argues that Slovakia lacks the military capacity to repel a major Russian attack independently. Even a war that did not reach Slovak territory would bring refugees, inflation and economic disruption, he says.

Branik also questions who would determine whether a NATO member had “provoked” Russia, as Fico suggests. He noted that Moscow has already characterised Slovak arms production as provocative.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also recently raised concerns about the credibility of Article 5. Citing intelligence assessments, he warned that Russia could launch drone or missile strikes against NATO countries on its eastern flank, cause damage and then portray the incidents as accidents rather than deliberate attacks.

He argued that such incidents could weaken NATO’s willingness to respond collectively and undermine confidence in its defence commitments. The aim would be to convince alliance members that Article 5 is “more theoretical than practical”, while giving politicians an excuse to argue that their countries should not have to fight for allies such as Latvia or Lithuania.

That confidence in Western hesitation was on display in a recent BBC interview with Sergei Karaganov, honorary chairman of Russia’s Council for Foreign and Defence Policy. Asked whether Europe would retaliate against a Russian nuclear strike, Karaganov dismissed the possibility. “No, there will be no response from Europe,” he said, expressing confidence that neither the UK nor the US would risk nuclear retaliation.

Fico may have his own political reasons for questioning NATO solidarity, but his remarks give Moscow further reason to believe its strategy is working.

World.title: Trump Associates Attended Rally for Bosnian Serb Nationalist Party
World.content:
On October 6, two days after the elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the New York Times reported that two Trump associates had been paid for a pre-election engagement in Republika Srpska. This paid trip came as electoral campaigns are in full swing for US elections in November.

The US media has since published more stories on this trip.

The New York Times later confirmed that at least six US advisers close to Trump had travelled to Bosnia and Herzegovina. The sources the reporting relied on claimed that Blair and LaCivita did not do work for SNSD and only worked for the government of Republika Srpska, which has paid lobbyists and consultants close to Trump and the Republican Party more than four million dollars since the beginning of last year.

According to the US Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) register, the lobbying firm Continental Strategy was paid almost 240,000 dollars from the Republika Srpska budget between February and the end of August.

The New York Times reported that Blair and LaCivita were each paid several hundred thousand dollars by the law firm Boies Schiller Flexner, which represents Republika Srpska. Smith also works at the law firm and was reportedly hired by the Republika Srpska government, which the New York Times wrote is “essentially one and the same” with the party that controls it.

The arrival of Trump’s advisers in Republika Srpska drew criticism from members of the Republican Party, with some officials criticising the president’s advisers for spending time making money from foreign consulting instead of devoting themselves to the Republican electoral campaign in the US.

Trump said that Blair and LaCivita do not work directly for him and that there is no obstacle to them being paid by others for their services as his outside advisers.

On October 7, Trump wrote on his social network Truth Social that he had no idea who else they worked for but would ask them: “If there’s a conflict, I will terminate them, immediately!”

Later the same day, answering questions from the media, Trump said the two advisers were independent and that he did not think there was a conflict of interest.

“If I thought they had a conflict here, I would terminate,” Trump said.

Previous reporting in the US and Bosnia and Herzegovina relied on unnamed sources for the advisers’ trip to Republika Srpska. Of the firms involved, only Continental Strategy confirmed that its partner, Alex Garcia, was in Republika Srpska on October 4, election day.

In footage from local televisions stations and in photographs published by the SNSD from the Borik Hall rally, Garcia can be seen standing behind Dodik.

According to American media, Garcia is a partner at the lobbying firm Continental Strategy. Katie Wiles, the daughter of Trump’s current chief of staff Susie Wiles, also works for the firm.

Garcia did not immediately respond to a request from BIRN for comment.

Melissa Stone, a spokesperson for Continental Strategy, told The New York Times that the firm “meticulously complies with every ethical and legal requirement.” According to the newspaper, it was Garcia who recommended Blair and LaCivita to the government of Republika Srpska.

Asked by the online media outlet Semafor whether Continental Strategy had helped organise Blair and LaCivita’s trip, a spokesperson for the firm replied that Garcia was the only employee in Republika Srpska on October 4 and the only one who lobbies the US government on the firm’s behalf.

Citing three sources, Semafor reported that Continental Strategy had helped organise the trip. After publication, Stone said this information was incorrect.

None of the advisers answered BIRN’s question as to whether, apart from attending the party rally, they had advised the SNSD while being paid from the entity’s budget.

According to Transparency International’s Korajlic, “All this lobbying that Dodik financed from the budget, and which was actually for his personal interests – lifting sanctions and everything else – is questionable, but none of our institutions will deal with it.”

In mid-September, a few weeks before the elections, the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina banned all payments from the Republika Srpska budget related to a consulting services contract concluded between the Republika Srpska representation office in Vienna and the company Dickens & Madson Canada Inc.

The ban also applies to other lobbying activities whose aims are contrary to the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the decisions of the Constitutional Court and the institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

State prosecutors had earlier decided not to open an investigation into a complaint about payments made through the Vienna office for lobbying for Republika Srpska’s independence.

World.title: Croatian Government Gives 15,000 Unlicensed Apartments 4 More Years
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The Croatian Government has given in on certain aspects of the Hospitality Activity Act, providing 15,000 unlicensed apartments 4 more years to operate.

The Croatian Government has now accepted the final proposal of the Hospitality Activity Act, which extends the validity of temporary decisions for around 15,000 landlords by an additional four years, the Ministry of Tourism and Sport announced. Index reports that these temporary decisions – on the basis of which apartments and rooms operate in buildings that do not have all the necessary papers, an occupancy permit, or are still waiting for the completion of the legalisation process – were due to expire at the end of this year. If the law had remained unchanged, thousands of landlords would have had to lock up, but with the new legislative proposal the Government has moved the deadline all the way to the 31st of December 2030.

protecting the livelihoods of family landlords

Tourism and Sport Minister Tonči Glavina said that this protects the livelihood of family landlords and ensures the continuity of their business so that they have enough time to legalise their properties and obtain permanent permits. “This is an important measure, especially when we take into account that at the end of 2024 around 15,000 landlords were operating on the basis of temporary decisions,” Glavina stated.

unique registration numbers as of 2027

In addition to extending the permits for legalisation, the law also brings novelties aimed at combating unregistered rentals. A unique registration number is being introduced for accommodation units advertised via online platforms such as Booking and Airbnb, but this provision will not enter into force immediately – only from the 1st of May 2027 so that the market has time to adapt. The state plans to establish direct data exchange with the platforms, which means that properties without a valid registration number would no longer be allowed to be advertised online. At the same time, county bodies are obliged to submit accurate data on the number of resolved cases and temporary decisions to the Ministry once a year, by the 30th of June.

higher penalties and closer inspections

The new legal framework also provides for higher misdemeanour fines for violations of the regulations, expanded powers for tourism and tax inspectors, and the digitisation of administrative procedures through the eTurizam system. Another novelty is that the rental of rooms and apartments in family houses will in future also be able to be registered through a craft or a limited liability company (d.o.o.), and not only in the status of a private landlord as has been the case until now. The bill has been sent to the parliamentary procedure for a second reading.

World.title: €3,000 Parking Fine Arrives a Year After Dubrovnik Trip – Poles Outraged
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – A €3,000 parking fine arrived at the addresses of tourists following their Dubrovnik trip an entire year later, and it’s safe to say they’re not happy…

Fines that some former visitors to Dubrovnik “earned” by parking their cars around the historic city centre are arriving months after they return from their holidays, and the case has attracted plenty of attention in the Polish media. Morski reports that one of the fined tourists contacted Croatia’s well known media outlet Index, claiming that because of two entries into the restricted zone he received two fines of €1,500 each, meaning the total sum amounted to €3,000.

“I’m writing to you on my own behalf and on behalf of many Polish tourists who, instead of returning with nice memories from a holiday in Croatia, specifically Dubrovnik, came back deeply disappointed by the greed and inhumane rules that apply in that city,” he wrote.

The Polish tourist claims that the fines reached him more than one year after his trip to Croatia. “Personally I received two separate fines of €1,500 each. In addition, the law firms hired by the city authorities don’t even reply to e-mails and it’s extremely difficult to communicate with them,” he stated. According to him, the problem has caused a lot of dissatisfaction among Polish tourists, and television stations and internet portals are reporting on it.

In addition, this particular Polish tourist complained that traffic signs warning about the entry restriction are in place, but he considers that it is nowhere near clear enough to tourists what they must do in order to be allowed to enter the zone by car, and that the fines are disproportionate to the offence. On the 2nd of June 2025, the City of Dubrovnik introduced a special traffic regime zone around the historic centre in order to reduce traffic congestion and protect the area that has been exposed to a large number of vehicles for years.

The City of Dubrovnik otherwise prescribed fines of €260 for natural persons, €660 for craftspersons and persons performing independent activities, and a significantly higher €1,320 for legal entities. The responsible person in a legal entity can be fined an additional €260.

World.title: Montenegro EU Accession: “Without Croatian Consent There is No Progress”
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – The issues surrounding Montenegro and its EU accession closely involve Croatia, with EU Commissioner Marta Kos saying that without Croatian consent there can be no progress.

Complicated, war-mired bilateral issues between Montenegro and Croatia are not part of the negotiating process with the European Union, but they must be resolved, said EU Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos. She explained that Montenegro’s further progress depends on the consent of all 27 member states. Anadolu/Index reports that Commissioner Kos emphasised that Croatia has its own interests, but that she is encouraged by the steps Montenegro has taken towards resolving these open issues. She considers the signing of the accession treaty by the summer of 2027 to be a realistic goal and that Brussels supports the plan for Montenegro to become the 28th EU member in 2028.

the differences between politics and eu accession negotiations

She also commented on the possibility that Croatian demands could become official Brussels conditions and explained that a distinction should be made between the technical part of the negotiations and the political support of the member states. “Here, I’d like to separate the technical process from the support that every candidate country must receive from all 27 European Union members. What you in Montenegro have achieved in the last three years truly happens once in a lifetime. You have made enormous progress and I’m genuinely proud of you. I hope you in Montenegro are also proud of yourselves,” Kos said.

She stressed that the consent of all member states is necessary for the continuation of the European path. “At that level you have done almost everything; we are just a little short. But if we want to go further in this process in Brussels, we need the consent of all 27 members. Croatia has its interests and speaks openly about them,” she stated. “I’m glad that Montenegro has taken certain steps in recent days and that dialogue between Croatia and Montenegro exists. I think you are on the right path to resolve these bilateral issues as well. They are not part of the negotiating process, but because of everything I have explained they must be resolved,” she added.

one step closer to formal eu membership

Kos also referred to the decision of the Montenegrin Parliament to accept constitutional changes relating to the integrity check of candidates for government members. “The Montenegrin Parliament has brought your country one step closer to the goal, which is full membership of the European Union. This is an excellent result that shows that your MPs also understand why it is now important that, in sporting terms, you are in the final of one of the most important matches in Montenegro’s history,” Kos said. She emphasised that the adoption of the constitutional changes brings Montenegro closer to closing Chapter 23 and then to the completion of the accession negotiations themselves.

the painful issue of war crimes committed against croatia

Kos also answered a question about Parliament Speaker Andrija Mandić. His removal did not succeed in parliament, and the opposition criticised him for expressing condolences to the family of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić. Kos stated that only the Parliament decides on its leadership. “Only the Parliament can decide on its leadership, no one else. In the EU, there is truly no place for glorifying war criminals. It’s important, as President Ursula von der Leyen and I personally have stressed, that reconciliation and respect for the victims are values that mean a great deal to us in Europe,” Kos said.

“The painful history of the former Yugoslavia is full of open wounds. I think it is good to talk about this, but not by looking backwards, but forwards. It is important to say if something is not right or if someone has not acted well. These are our values, and these European Union values are one of the reasons why Montenegro wants to join the EU.”

Ahead of the upcoming Berlin Process summit in Budva, Kos assessed that Montenegro is in the focus of European leaders and that its results are increasingly of interest to the member states. She believes that the summit in Budva, after the one in Tivat, will further strengthen Montenegro’s international visibility and its European perspective. “European leaders see how much Montenegro has achieved and it is clear to Europe who will be our next member. In June at the summit in Tivat the French President Emmanuel Macron was present for the first time, and today the German Chancellor is coming. I believe each of them is delighted when they come here,” Kos said.

She added that, along with regional cooperation, one of the primary topics will be the way in which the EU can help Montenegro complete the negotiations and become a full member.

World.title: Croatia Wants to Host the 2030 UEFA Futsal Championship
World.content:
October the 22nd, 2026 – Croatia has officially put its bid in to host the 2030 UEFA Futsal Championship, with Split and Zagreb as the proposed host cities.

The Croatian Football Federation has formally applied to host the 2030 European Futsal Championship, it was announced on the federation’s official website. As Slobodna Dalmacija reports, the European football federation UEFA has received seven candidacies, including Croatia’s as well as those of Finland, France, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Poland and Spain. As host cities, the Croatian Football Federation has registered Zagreb (Arena Zagreb) and Split (Spaladium Arena).

Interested federations must submit the final bid documentation by the 8th of June 2027, and the UEFA Executive Committee will decide on the host in September 2027. The bidding process was launched on the 29th of June this year, and national federations were invited to submit expressions of interest by the 13th of October 2026. The European Championship will be held during the months of January and February 2030.

As a quick reminder, Croatia was a successful organiser of the 2012 European Futsal Championship, when the host cities were also Zagreb and Split, and it still holds the record for attendance at a single match at the European tournament. At the semi-final match between Croatia and Russia in Arena Zagreb, 14,300 spectators were present.

In addition to Croatia, candidacies to host the 2030 UEFA Futsal EURO have also been submitted by Finland, France, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Poland and Spain.

World.title: Croatia is the Leading Camping Destination by Quality in Europe for 2027
World.content:
October the 21st, 2026 – Croatia is the leading camping destination in terms of quality in Europe for 2027, following very significant improvement and offer diversity.

Croatian camping has significantly improved the quality and diversity of its accommodation offer, facilities and services over the past two decades, further strengthening its position on the European tourism market. Continued investment in quality, adaptation to market changes and responding to increasingly demanding guest expectations are key to the further development of the sector. Glas Istre/The Voice of Istria reports that these are the main topics of the jubilee 20th Croatian Camping Congress, organised by the Croatian Camping Association (KUH), taking place from the 19th to the 21st of October at the Well Hotel in Terme Tuhelj.

“This is a fantastic day for Croatian camping and the realisation of the dreams of all tourism workers who have worked for years to make Croatian camping the best in Europe in terms of quality. Recent research by PiNCAMP, the camping platform within ADAC, confirms that Croatia has become the leading camping destination by quality, which we can all be very proud of. This is an additional incentive for the further development of Croatian camping, and at the same time confirmation that investments, especially over the last ten years or so, pay off and that guests recognise them. Further development will also depend on the legal framework regulating camping activities in the areas of spatial planning, maritime domain and the sea, and tourism. We expect that conditions and frameworks will be defined in all three areas that will enable further investments. Without new investments there is no raising of quality, and I believe that in the coming years we will see an additional flourishing of Croatian camping and a new rise, especially thanks to the positioning of Croatia as the highest-quality camping destination in Europe,” emphasised Veljko Ostojić, President of the KUH Executive Board and Director of the Croatian Tourism Association.

croatia leads the european ranking

According to the announcement by PiNCAMP, the camping portal of ADAC (the largest German and European and the second-largest automobile club in the world), Croatia will for the first time lead the European ranking of campsite quality in 2027, while the number of Croatian campsites with the ADAC Superplatz label is rising to 29. ADAC PiNCAMP expects continued strong demand from the German and Dutch markets for the next season. How to maintain competitiveness on the European market and create conditions for sustainable growth of the sector is one of the key questions of this year’s Croatian Camping Congress.

“The next step in the development of Croatian camping is not only accommodation, but the complete quality of the stay – from the pitch, sanitary facilities and shade to service and facilities that give the guest a reason to come even outside the summer season. It is important to preserve the diversity of the offer, from places for tents and campers to mobile homes, as well as small family campsites and large resorts. Research should help us direct investments towards specific groups of guests, and technology should facilitate reservations and leave employees more time for the guest. For such development, professional people and clear, predictable business conditions are equally important,” said Adriano Palman, Director of the Croatian Camping Association.

These changes are particularly visible in the development of accommodation quality. According to data from the Ministry of Tourism and Sport, in 2007 Croatia had 13 four-star campsites, while there were no five-star campsites. By 2025 the number of four-star campsites had risen to 82, and nine had entered the five-star category. Thus, as many as 58% of the capacity of Croatian campsites falls into the 4- and 5-star category. This development reflects continuous investments in infrastructure, improvement of the existing offer and development of facilities, with which Croatian camping responds to the increasingly demanding expectations of guests.

a huge transformation over the last two decades

“The camping industry has transformed significantly over the last 20 years. Today, 50 percent of Croatian campsites have four or five stars, and they account for 20 percent of all overnight stays in Croatia. The level of their quality is also confirmed by guest loyalty, as shown by the latest research. As many as 50 percent of guests have returned to Croatian campsites seven or more times, which speaks of the competitiveness of this tourism segment,” emphasised Monika Udovičić, State Secretary at the Ministry of Tourism and Sport.

From 1 January to 11 October 2026, Croatian campsites recorded almost 3.4 million arrivals and 21.4 million overnight stays, maintaining results at the level of the same period last year, which was a record year in the history of Croatian camping. Germany, Slovenia and Austria remain the leading markets, with more than 60 percent of total overnight stays in campsites, while domestic guests recorded 9.7 percent more overnight stays than in the comparable period last year. The importance of camping for Croatian tourism is confirmed by its 23 percent share of overnight stays in commercial accommodation, with an average stay of 6.2 days – the longest among all types of accommodation.

The continuation of the programme also includes European examples of campsite adaptation to climate change, from the arrangement of green areas and creation of shade to infrastructure adaptation. Business topics cover the development and retention of employees, energy efficiency, and a review of ten years of online reservations in Croatian campsites.

continued investment in the camping sector

A special part of the programme also opens the question of how Croatian campsites present themselves to guests through artificial intelligence. The research covered four leading AI assistants that were asked 100 questions about Croatian campsites on five source markets, with almost 2,000 answers analysed and the accuracy of the claims made and sources used verified. The results provide insight into the reliability of the information that potential guests receive and the opportunities for campsites to improve their visibility and the availability of accurate data in the digital environment.

The professional programme is accompanied by an exhibition of mobile homes, glamping tents, equipment and digital solutions for campsites. The Congress thus connects research and exchange of experience with a concrete offer for investment and business improvement. From the first edition in 2007 to last year’s Congress, around 5,200 participants from Croatia and abroad have taken part in these gatherings. As the central meeting place for representatives of campsites, the tourism sector, institutions and related industries, the Congress encourages the exchange of experience, presentation of innovations and discussion of trends and challenges that shape the future of camping.

The jubilee Congress ends tomorrow with the presentation of the Croatia’s Best Campsites and OK Mini Camps awards, as well as the Naj Kamp Adria 2026 award, which recognise the quality and development of the camping offer.

World.title: SafeJournalists Demands Official Croatian Reaction After Threats to Media
World.content:
October the 21s5, 2026 – The organisation SafeJournalists is currently demanding an official Croatian reaction after imagery of hanged journalists and other threats to the media have come to light.

Extreme condemnation of morbid threats made against journalists in Croatia have come from the international SafeJournalists network following their reporting on Nazi and antisemitic outbursts by Torcida members in Split, Morski reports. Specifically, the organisation has warned about the publication of journalists’ photographs, calls for their liquidation, and banners depicting hanged journalists from Croatian media.

They demand urgent protection of the threatened journalists from the Croatian authorities and prosecution of those responsible. SafeJournalists warns that a campaign of intimidation against journalists has since begun, with them being accused of creating hysteria and conducting a campaign against Torcida. Today, Interior Minister Davor Božinović himself spoke out, saying that the police have launched an investigation into messages aimed at intimidating journalists while they perform their work.

“I have some information about this, the police has launched a criminal investigation precisely because of inscriptions intended to intimidate journalists,” Minister Božinović said before the HDZ Presidency session. “No one has any authority to frighten or intimidate anyone in this country, especially not those who are merely doing their job,” the minister and Deputy Prime Minister stated.

On the 18th of October, the Facebook page Narodni reporteri published photographs of 11 Croatian journalists and one political analyst under the title “12 horsemen of the Croatian apocalypse.” According to SafeJournalists, some commenters called for the journalists to be expelled from Croatia and banned from working, while others suggested finding their home addresses, expressed a desire for their death, or mentioned compiling a liquidation list. The next day, the 19th of October, photos of new threatening messages appeared in the Facebook group Torcida Split 1950.

On one wall in Dalmatia, the following message was written: “Torcida remembers and does not forgive! Journalists are worms.” Particularly disturbing was a banner on which journalists were called “the greatest evil of Croatian society.” The banner showed a tree with hanged journalists from Slobodna Dalmacija, Index, Jutarnji list, Večernji list and 24sata.

The SafeJournalists network expressed particular concern about the political messages accompanying the incidents. They singled out a press conference that Domovinski pokret president Ivan Penava held today in Split. Penava condemned Nazi and fascist chants, but at the same time accused the police and the media of conducting a campaign against Torcida. He also questioned the publication of photographs of suspects sought by the police and criticised the Croatian Journalists’ Association for its warnings about threats against journalists.

SafeJournalists considers that such political rhetoric further worsens the atmosphere in which journalists are exposed to intimidation.
