World.title: Georgia’s party ban: Court to begin hearing government case against opposition on 21 October
World.content:
At noon on 21 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearing on the merits a case brought by the ruling Georgian Dream party, which is seeking to ban five opposition parties and political groups. The hearings will take place in Batumi and continue on 22 and 23 October.

Four of the five parties intend to defend their positions in court, while the fifth will boycott the proceedings. Some opposition groups also plan to hold protests in Batumi and Tbilisi alongside the hearings.

The Constitutional Court’s full bench will hear the case, meaning all its sitting judges. The court has nine seats, but only seven judges currently serve on it, with two vacancies. On 13 October, Manana Kobakhidze, one of the founders of Georgian Dream, left the court. She had previously asked to recuse herself from the case, but the court rejected her request. Kobakhidze said she had made the decision to leave the court independently and for personal reasons.

Georgian Dream MPs Archil Gorduladze, Giorgi Kakhiani, Tengiz Sharmanashvili and Tornike Cheishvili will represent the party in court.

Under the law, the court must deliver its ruling by 24 June 2027.

Why is Georgian Dream seeking to ban the parties?

The claimants — 88 Georgian Dream MPs — argue that all five parties have violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits political parties that aim to overthrow or forcibly change the constitutional order.

According to information released by the court, the claimants cite alleged human rights violations between 2004 and 2012, when one of the parties, the United National Movement (UNM), was in power. They also point to the parties’ current refusal to recognise Georgian Dream’s legitimacy. The claimants say the parties have rejected the government’s legitimacy since 2016 and are pursuing a common goal.

The claimants also accuse the parties of attempting to overthrow the government. In the case of the United National Movement, they further allege that it undermined the country’s independence and territorial integrity, citing the August 2008 war.

The opposition parties reject all these accusations.

What do the parties facing a ban plan to do?

United National Movement

The party will attend the court hearings, said Irakli Pavlenishvili, chair of its governing council. He called on members of the public to gather outside the courthouse in Batumi on the days of the hearings.

The UNM’s jailed founder and Georgia’s third president, Mikheil Saakashvili, has also demanded that he attend the proceedings. In a statement released on 17 October, he said he wanted the authorities to bring him to Batumi so he could “fully expose this so-called court and its master for their historic betrayal”. Much of the case against the parties concerns Saakashvili’s time in power, from 2004 to 2012.

The party’s leader, Levan Khabeishvili, who is also in prison, has likewise demanded permission to attend the hearings.

The UNM belongs to the opposition alliance and takes part in its protests.

What is the Opposition Alliance? The Opposition Alliance “Unity for Victory” was formed by nine pro-Western Georgian parties on 2 March 2026, following months of negotiations. Its members are the United National Movement, Ahali, Girchi – More Freedom, Droa, the Federalists, European Georgia, Strategy Aghmashenebeli, Freedom Square and the National Democratic Party. The alliance says its goals are to end the rule of Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder and honorary chairman of Georgian Dream, restore Georgia’s Euro-Atlantic course, release political prisoners and form a coalition government after Georgian Dream loses a free election. The parties retain their ideological independence but have agreed on a joint strategy for protests and communications. The alliance’s largest rally to date took place in Tbilisi on 26 May 2026, Georgia’s Independence Day. Two other major opposition parties, Lelo and For Georgia, led by Giorgi Gakharia, have not joined the alliance. Lelo chose to operate independently, while For Georgia rejected an alliance with the United National Movement and parties that split from it.

Coalition for Change

The coalition will also take part in the hearings. Its member parties — Ahali, Girchi – More Freedom and Droa — also belong to the Opposition Alliance. On 15 October, Nika Gvaramia, leader of Ahali, announced the launch of a joint campaign by the alliance.

Gvaramia said their struggle would not be confined to the courtroom. “We will be everywhere, including on the streets of Tbilisi,” he promised.

Strong Georgia – Lelo

Lelo will attend the hearings and has asked the Public Defender (ombudsman) to submit a legal opinion on the case. As of 19 October, the ombudsman’s office had not responded.

Lelo is not a member of the alliance. The party’s political council says it has several scenarios and an action plan ready in case the court approves the ban.

For Georgia

The party announced in a statement on 20 October that it would take part in the proceedings. However, it insists that the court consider the case against it separately, rather than together with the other parties.

The party of former Georgian prime minister Giorgi Gakharia does not belong to the Opposition Alliance. It was the only one of the five parties that refused to surrender its parliamentary mandate in protest and nevertheless entered parliament.

The Federalists

The party has decided not to attend the hearings, saying it does not want to lend the proceedings a veneer of legal legitimacy.

According to party leader Tamara Chergoleishvili, the Federalists will travel to Batumi but protest against the court proceedings outside the courthouse rather than in the courtroom.

Why does it matter whether the parties attend the hearings?

The parties’ attendance could affect their chances of appealing the verdict to the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) in Strasbourg.

Sandro Baramidze, a lawyer with Transparency International Georgia, explains that the ECHR requires applicants to raise and document their arguments through domestic legal proceedings first. If a party does not attend the hearing, its application to the court in Strasbourg could therefore be declared inadmissible.

Who is organising the protests?

As Georgian Dream seeks to ban the parties listed above, the Opposition Alliance has announced a protest campaign.

The first demonstration will take place at 11:00 on 21 October in Batumi, outside the Constitutional Court. Freedom Square, a member of the alliance, is organising the protest.

At 19:00 on 25 October in Tbilisi, outside the first building of Tbilisi State University, the Opposition Alliance will launch a joint campaign aimed at organising a large demonstration in Tbilisi on 28 November.

As of 20 October, Lelo and For Georgia had not said whether they would join the protests.

What is the rest of the opposition doing?

In addition to the parties facing a ban, the Opposition Alliance includes European Georgia, Strategy Aghmashenebeli, Freedom Square and the National Democratic Party. These parties are not named in the lawsuit but take part in all the alliance’s protests.

Levan Tsutskiridze, leader of Freedom Square, believes that banning the parties would create a bigger problem for Georgian Dream itself.

He says a ban will not make the country’s problems disappear. Instead, it will “close off the political path to solving these problems and guarantee an even worse end for Georgian Dream”.

Viktor Kipiani, leader of the party For Georgia First, points to the same risk:

Banning opposition parties through the courts effectively brings the political process to a standstill, while making change through elections virtually impossible.

He believes this will accelerate radicalisation in the country.

The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association has now issued its independent legal assessment of the case for the third time, arguing that the lawsuit aims to eliminate political competition.

What is the European Union saying?

EU institutions have reacted strongly to the Georgian authorities’ attempt to ban opposition parties:

The European Parliament adopted another critical resolution, calling for the immediate withdrawal of the lawsuit and saying it was considering personal sanctions against those who initiated the proceedings.

Christian Wigand, a European Commission spokesman, said Brussels was closely monitoring developments. He said the attempt to abolish leading political forces, alongside the Georgian authorities’ earlier statements and legislative changes, pointed to a worrying instrumentalisation of the justice system. This directly threatens democratic pluralism and fundamental freedoms.

On 20 October, Georgia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded that questioning the legitimacy of the proceedings before the court had even examined the case amounted to an attempt to pressure the court and interfere in the country’s internal affairs. The ministry urged EU representatives to refrain from statements that prejudge the proceedings.

What happens if the court upholds the lawsuit?

If the court upholds the lawsuit, the five parties will legally cease to exist. According to official figures from the Central Election Commission, a total of 784,820 voters backed the five parties in the 2024 parliamentary election.

Under current legislation, the court may also, at the claimant’s request, ban people associated with the dissolved parties from engaging in political activity. The law also provides a 14-day procedure for banning a successor party.

The hearings scheduled for 21–23 October mark the first stage in the proceedings. It remains unclear how long the case will take or when the court will deliver its ruling.

World.title: Kazakhstan's oil deliveries to IEA members to rise 21.9% in 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 22. Kazakhstan's crude oil deliveries to IEA member countries are expected to increase in 2026 and 2027, following significant fluctuations in quarterly and monthly volumes this year.

This was reflected in a publication issued by the International Energy Agency (IEA).

According to the report, deliveries of selected Kazakh crude streams to IEA member countries are estimated to average 1.17 million barrels per day (mb/d) in 2026, up 21.9% from 0.96 mb/d in 2025. The figure is projected to rise further to 1.35 mb/d in 2027, an increase of 15.4% compared with 2026, according to Trend’s calculations.

The quarterly figures show a sharp decline at the beginning of 2026, followed by a strong recovery. Deliveries averaged 1.39 mb/d in both the third and fourth quarters of 2025, before falling to 0.92 mb/d in the first quarter of 2026. They then climbed to 1.48 mb/d in the second quarter, up 60.9% quarter-on-quarter, Trend reports.

Monthly data also point to considerable volatility. Deliveries reached 1.57 mb/d in May 2026, before declining to 1.26 mb/d in June, a decrease of 19.7%. They subsequently recovered to 1.49 mb/d in July, rising 18.3% month-on-month, Trend’s calculations show.

The report’s figures do not specify the reasons for these quarterly and monthly changes. However, Kazakhstan’s oil export flows faced operational disruptions during 2026. Reuters reported that maintenance at the Tengiz field and interruptions to loading operations at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) terminal affected shipments. In July, the temporary suspension of terminal operations following attacks on tankers led to production cuts, while CPC exports increased in August as loading activity stabilised. These developments provide broader context for fluctuations in oil flows, although the available information does not establish a direct link between individual incidents and the IEA’s selected-stream delivery figures.

World.title: U.S. has imposes sanctions on a law firm that supplies Iranian products
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 22. The United States has added a law firm with offices in Greece and Panama to its Iran-related sanctions list.

This was stated in a statement issued by the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

The U.S. restrictive measures target Karnakis and Karnakis. According to the Treasury Department, the law firm facilitated the illegal supply of Iranian products to international markets, thereby allegedly helping Tehran obtain funds for weapons development and the advancement of its nuclear program.

Inclusion on the sanctions list entails the freezing of assets located in the United States, as well as a ban on U.S. citizens and companies conducting business with the listed entities and individuals.

The sanctions list also includes five individuals allegedly linked to the company. The U.S. Treasury Department has issued a general license authorizing transactions necessary to wind down dealings involving Karnakis and Karnakis until November 20.

World.title: Resolution to conflict in Ukraine is closer than ever – Trump
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. A resolution to the conflict in Ukraine is now closer than ever before.

U.S. President Donald Trump said this during a roundtable discussion held at the White House.

"I recently spoke with Vladimir Putin about resolving the war with Ukraine. We are moving toward such a resolution. We are now closer to it than ever before," noted Donald Trump.

The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has held a series of contacts and negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv aimed at ending the Russia-Ukraine war since 2025. Separate meetings between U.S. representatives and Russian and Ukrainian delegations were held in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, in March 2025. The discussions focused on safe navigation in the Black Sea, halting strikes on energy infrastructure, and resolving the conflict.

In August 2025, Trump met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Alaska and subsequently held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European leaders at the White House. The meetings focused on reaching a peace agreement, providing security guarantees, and arranging a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy.

On October 21, 2026, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff met with Putin in St. Petersburg to discuss the resumption of negotiations and the settlement of the war. Following the meeting, it was reported that the Russian side had agreed to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine under U.S. mediation. Abu Dhabi is being considered as a possible venue for the meetings, starting on November 10.

World.title: Chronicles of Victory: October 22, 2020
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 22. The Azerbaijani Army launched a counter-offensive operation, later called the "Iron Fist", on September 27, 2020, in response to the large-scale provocation of the Armenian armed forces along the frontline.

The erupted 44-day Second Karabakh War ended with the liberation of Azerbaijan’s territories from nearly 30-year Armenian occupation and the restoration of territorial integrity.

Chronicle of the 26-th day of the second Karabakh war:

- On the official Twitter page of President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev, a publication was posted on ensuring full control over the state border (bordering with Iran).

- A publication was posted on the official Twitter page of President Ilham Aliyev, due to the liberation from the occupation of 3 villages of Fuzuli district, 4 villages of Jabrayil district.

- President Ilham Aliyev received the Ombudsman of Türkiye.

- The Azerbaijani Defense Ministry has disseminated information about the latest situation at the front. Volunteers in the Armenian Armed Forces fled, leaving their combat positions. Information was disseminated about the wounding of the commander of the Armenian Armed Forces regiment, the killing of his deputy and the battalion commander.

- The Armenian Armed Forces fired 3 ballistic missiles at Siyazan, 2 at Gabala and 1 at Kurdamir. A 17-year-old civilian was wounded as a result of a missile attack by the Armenians on Gabala.

- Armenian servicemen refused to fight. Video footage of another captured military equipment of the Armenian Armed Forces was distributed.

- Another tactical UAV of the Armenian Armed Forces, which attempted to fly in the direction of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic of Azerbaijan, was destroyed. The Azerbaijani artillerymen continued to deliver precise strikes at the firing points of the Armenian Armed Forces.

- The Azerbaijani flag was hoisted in the village of Aghband, Zangilan district.

- The Ministry of Defense of Azerbaijan presented video footage of the destruction of a significant number of personnel and equipment of the Armenian Armed Forces.

World.title: Families of missing Azerbaijanis hold rally in Brussels (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. On October 21, 2026, families of missing Azerbaijanis held a rally organized by the public association "Karabakh Families of Missing Persons" Public Unionin Brussels’ central Schuman Square—home to the main institutions of the European Union. This event followed a demonstration held the previous day in the square in front of the European Parliament in Brussels.

This was reported by the Agency for State Support to Non-Governmental Organizations of Azerbaijan.

During the event, it was emphasized that Armenia has still not provided information regarding the fate of 4,010 missing Azerbaijanis and continues to withhold information about them. Particular attention was paid to the importance of providing information about missing persons as part of advancing the peace agenda.

Families of missing Azerbaijanis have stated that the European Parliament—which consistently advocates for Armenia and is viewed in international relations as an example of anachronism and atavism—has never once raised the issue of the missing Azerbaijanis.

Konul Behbudova, chair of the "Karabakh Families of Missing Persons" Public Union, stated that actions dedicated to the missing persons will continue.

As part of the event, a special installation was presented, featuring photographs of missing Azerbaijani citizens, along with their clothing and envelopes containing letters. The poignant messages, written on behalf of those who have gone missing, left a deep impression on visitors. Attendees expressed their solidarity with the families of the missing by leaving words of support, tying commemorative ribbons, and laying flowers.

The "Families of the Missing in Karabakh" Public Union has emerged as a winner in the 2026 grant competition held by the Agency for State Support to Non-Governmental Organizations of Azerbaijan, with its project titled "Echo of Absence."

World.title: Families of missing Azerbaijanis meet with EU representatives in Brussels (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. A meeting with members of the “Karabakh Families of Missing Persons” public association was held on October 21 at the European External Action Service (EEAS) of the European Union in Brussels.

The families of missing Azerbaijanis met with Okke Bouwman, Political Adviser to the EU Special Representative for the South Caucasus and the crisis in Georgia, and Marco Cardinali, Coordinator for Relations with Azerbaijan.

During the meeting, which lasted about an hour, the families of missing Azerbaijanis stated that Armenia had provided no information about their loved ones, even after the end of the conflict.

Konul Behbudova, chairperson of the public association, noted that on October 20, the previous day, families of missing Azerbaijanis had held a protest at Place du Luxembourg in front of the European Parliament in Brussels and adopted a statement.

She stressed that Armenia bears direct responsibility for the fate of missing Azerbaijanis and is obliged to share information with Azerbaijan about the locations of mass graves. Behbudova noted that 32 mass graves have been discovered to date in Azerbaijan’s territories liberated from occupation.

The meeting also addressed another protest held by families of missing Azerbaijanis in Brussels that day, at the central Schuman Square. It was emphasized that the families would not remain silent until they received information about their loved ones and would continue to hold regular protests.

World.title: Heydar Aliyev Foundation VP Leyla Aliyeva tours Eternal City complex in Samarkand (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. As part of her visit to Uzbekistan, Leyla Aliyeva, Vice-President of the Heydar Aliyev Foundation, familiarized herself with the Eternal City complex in Samarkand on October 21.

World.title: Dumped Victorian Liberal candidate demands party brings him back
World.content:
A dumped Liberal candidate has issued a legal letter demanding he be reinstated for the Victorian election, claiming the party's decision to remove him weeks out from the election breached the party's constitution.

Grant Hutchinson was last week removed as the candidate for Croydon for next month's state election, with Opposition Leader Jess Wilson at the time claiming "new information" had come to light about ongoing litigation with his own law firm.

The internal drama will be an unwanted distraction for Ms Wilson just four weeks before early voting opens, following years of turmoil for the party that Liberals hoped had finally settled to focus on the campaign.

Mr Hutchinson was replaced by Toby Wooldridge as the candidate at last Monday night's meeting.

In a legal letter to the party's state executive on Wednesday night, lawyers for Mr Hutchinson demanded he be reinstated by this Friday.

Grant Hutchinson was the Liberals' candidate for Croydon until last week, but the candidacy has since gone to Toby Wooldridge. (Instagram)

It provides "formal legal notice" to preserve all records about his disendorsement.

The letter, issued by RV Lawyers, claimed the party failed to give Mr Hutchinson a right of reply, and rejected the allegation that Mr Hutchinson had failed to disclose legal proceedings with his former law firm.

"That assertion is factually false," the letter states.

"Those proceedings had been disclosed during his vetting and preselection process," the letter states.

It further demanded the party provide any evidence of any new information about his civil proceedings.

"By excluding our client from the meeting, the committee acted upon an incomplete, selective, and misleading representation of the facts, without allowing our client to demonstrate that the matters had been fully disclosed and vetted."

Mr Hutchinson and Liberal headquarters both declined to comment on Wednesday night.

Pressed on the matter on Thursday morning, Ms Wilson said: "That's a matter for the Liberal Party."

Victorian Opposition leader Jess Wilson said new details had come to light about ongoing litigation. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

The letter further alleges members of the state executive were not given proper notice to consider the meeting, because they were not given any prior warning they would be voting on Mr Hutchinson's candidacy or endorsing Mr Wooldridge.

"Our client contends that the meeting was not validly convened to determine those matters and that both disputed resolutions are consequently invalid."

Solicitor Rod Veith, acting for Mr Hutchinson, further challenges the endorsement of Mr Wooldridge for failing to follow preselection processes.

He called for the party to hand over all written notices of the meeting, agendas and minutes of the meeting, a list of those who attended, and any submissions.

Mr Hutchinson is staunchly from the party's religious right and his endorsement last year astounded some Liberal members.

Last week, he wrote directly to the executive objecting to his removal.

"My concerns are not simply about the cancellation of my endorsement,'' he wrote.

"They are about the rights of members, the integrity of our preselection processes and whether the Victorian Liberal Party remains a political home for those who hold traditional Liberal and conservative values."

David Hodgett implored the government to stay committed to its plan and to not revert to remote learning. (ABC News)

Mr Hutchinson added that: "A party that abandons its principles, disregards the decisions of its grassroots members and excludes those who hold differing convictions risks losing not only its identity, but the very people who have sustained it."

The senior lawyer previously launched a civil lawsuit against his own law firm, prompting a counterclaim, as reported by The Guardian last year.

Longstanding member for Croydon, David Hodgett, is retiring at the election after 20 years in parliament.

The Liberal Party holds the seat by a margin of just 1.4 per cent but would expect to extend its lead in the electorate at the November 28 election.

World.title: Alleged gangster illegally deported from Türkiye, prosecutors say
World.content:
Prosecutors hoping to save their double murder case against an alleged Sydney gangster have admitted he was illegally deported back to Australia in 2023.

The admission came four days into Masood Zakaria's legal challenge in the NSW Supreme Court against the charges.

Mr Zakaria, an alleged member of the Alameddine crime family, is charged over the 2021 murders of Salim and Toufik Hamze.

He was later apprehended in Türkiye after police alleged Mr Zakaria left Australia on a fishing vessel before he could be charged.

The case centres around whether he was illegally deported from Istanbul after the Australian Federal Police (AFP) paid $1.1 million to two companies to secure his return.

Mr Zakaria's lawyers claim he was "kidnapped" by a private security company. (Supplied: NSW Police)

Mr Zakaria's legal team have previously compared the operation by Skytraders and security giant Hart International to "a kidnapping".

His lawyers also claim Mr Zakaria had a right to remain in Türkiye while an appeal against his deportation was still before Turkish authorities.

Prosecutor's admission on deportation

On Thursday, NSW Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) prosecutor Chris Tan told the court Mr Zakaria "was prohibited from being deported" while awaiting the outcome of his deportation appeal.

The courtroom showdown has seen the accused gangster challenge the actions of some of the nation's most high-profile crime fighters in bringing him back to Sydney.

This week, some of NSW Police's most experienced law enforcement officers were quizzed over their pursuit of the man one described as a "highly" wanted fugitive.

Chief Inspector Glyn Baker leaves court after giving evidence on Wednesday. (ABC News: Abubakr Sajid)

Among them have been Organised Crime Directorate boss Grant Taylor, Criminal Groups Squad Chief Inspector Glyn Baker, and two investigators tasked with looking into the Alameddine crime family.

In July, the ABC revealed AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett and former commissioner Reece Kershaw had been called to give evidence in the case.

The court will on Thursday hear arguments over whether they, and other AFP witnesses, will be forced to testify.

Hart International security contractor Robert Scheeres, who is now a Transport for NSW bureaucrat, denied on Monday that he and six colleagues had ever restrained Mr Zakaria.

The court was later shown images of Mr Zakaria in "flexi cuffs" on the plane surrounded by Hart employees in face coverings.

The hearings before Justice Edward Muston continue.

World.title: Breaking: ABC reporter saves man from floodwaters
World.content:
A driver has been rescued by two bystanders, including an ABC reporter, from his sinking car in floodwaters north of Brisbane.

The man drove his four-wheel-drive at speed through water on Buchanan Road at Morayfield.

The car stalled and started to sink.

ABC reporter Will Murray swimming to a sinking car in flood waters. (ABC News)

ABC reporter Will Murray and another man swam out to the car and pulled the driver out of the vehicle.

About 170 millimetres of rain has fallen in the area since this morning.

World.title: US orders diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
World.content:
The United States has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis.

The State Department order came as attacks in Saudi Arabia killed at least one person and injured eight others at a civilian airport in Dammam, while two people were killed in a drone attack on an oil field.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a post on X.

A diplomatic source in the Middle East told AFP that some families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn in the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, but Mr Pigott stressed the order was for the departure of non-emergency embassy staff and their families in Saudi Arabia only.

Four US officials told Reuters that US missions in other Gulf states would also be ordering family members to leave.

The 'huge problem' Saudi Arabia faces in its conflict with the Houthis The Houthis are trying to increase their leverage against Saudi Arabia while the kingdom is reportedly finding it harder to defend against attacks.

Saudi Arabia has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates.

On Wednesday, local time, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two.

"The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement.

It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones.

One person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, aviation officials said.

Last Friday the Australian government raised its travel advice for Saudia Arabia to "do not travel", due to the "volatile security situation" in the country.

Last week multiple strikes hit King Khalid International Airport in the capital Riyadh. (AP)

It came after a strike on the King Khalid International Airport killed at least 13 people and wounded more than 300.

The airport partially reopened on Wednesday with a limited number of inbound and outbound flights, two days after authorities notified airlines that they could resume operations.

In June, a four-year-old truce in Yemen's civil war collapsed, reviving the conflict that dates back to 2014. The Saudi-led coalition has backed the internationally recognised government since 2015.

Iran explosions

The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February and again in July, before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes.

Late on Wednesday, Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions in the southern Hormozgan province overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, breaking a spell of relative calm.

"A few minutes ago, the sound of several explosions was heard in the Karpan area of Sirik, in Hormozgan Province," the official IRNA news agency said.

It added that "local sources have not yet disclosed the nature of these explosions".

In late February, the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran, killing the country's supreme leader, along with senior military commanders.

Iran has attempted to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, demanding all ships seek its authorisation to cross. In peacetime, the strategic waterway carried around a fifth of the world's oil supplies.

In retaliation, the US has imposed a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and ships.

AFP/Reuters

World.title: Former Australian sprint champion charged with child sex offence
World.content:
Australian sprint champion Jake Doran has been charged with a child sex offence.

The 26-year-old from Magnetic Island off Townsville was arrested last week after a police investigation into alleged indecent treatment of children between January 2025 and September 2026.

Mr Doran has been charged with one count of indecent treatment of a child under 16.

He was granted bail in Townsville Magistrates Court.

Australian Athletics ban

Australian Athletics said in a statement that based on information provided, it had imposed a provisional ban on Mr Doran, preventing him from attending club events or participating in athletics training.

"The former international athlete has no paid or unpaid role within Australian Athletics," a spokesperson said.

"The safety and wellbeing of all participants in our sport is paramount, and we take all allegations of this nature very seriously."

Jake Doran was arrested in Townsville. (Instagram)

Mr Doran is Australia's equal ninth fastest 100m sprinter with a personal best time of 10.15 seconds.

He made the semifinal at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games in 2022.

He previously won two national titles and represented Australia at two world championships.

Mr Doran's social media accounts and LinkedIn have recently been deactivated.

The case will return to court on November 5.

World.title: Australians facing spike in data breaches after 'critical' flaw uncovered
World.content:
Australians should expect an increase in future data breaches as a result of critical software flaws that have forced major government websites, education platforms and web hosts to go offline.

The AI-assisted discovery of a vulnerability in a crucial piece of web architecture used by most websites, known as PHP, has set off a global scramble to patch millions of devices as major tech companies warn that bad actors have begun seizing on it.

The flaws, dubbed "PHP2shell", have been present for more than a decade, but are so serious that cybersecurity experts have urged widespread action to avoid major breaches.

"You have to patch it very, very quickly, or the suggestion is to take it offline," Australian web security expert Troy Hunt told ABC News Breakfast.

What you can do to protect yourself Read more Read more There is not much an individual can do about a server they do not control, so the practical advice is the same hygiene that always pays off: Use unique passwords or even better, use passkeys and a password manager so a breach at one site doesn't unlock your other accounts

Keep an eye on card statements over the coming weeks

Be extra wary of unexpected prompts to log in or download something, even on sites you trust

What happened?

Yesterday, the organisation behind PHP issued a security alert about the discovery of two "critical" vulnerabilities.

PHP is used in the back end of an estimated seven in 10 websites and applications, including Wordpress and Wikipedia.

These vulnerabilities would allow attackers to run their own code on affected servers without logging in, a major cybersecurity flaw that would allow unauthorised control to do anything from extracting user data to implanting other malware.

PHP works on the server behind a website, producing content for a visitor's browser. The flaws can let attackers run their own code on affected servers without logging in, according to PHP's security advisory.

The risk varies with the way a server is set up, but PHP's developers urged all users serving web pages to update immediately.

The PHP Foundation, a non-profit organisation maintaining and developing the PHP ecosystem, released a fix early this morning and urged all operators to update immediately.

AI helped discover the "critical" vulnerability. (ABC News: Scott Preston)

Amazon Web Services, a subsidiary of the US tech giant offering cloud computing platforms, said it had already seen evidence of attempts to exploit the vulnerability as early as October 17.

"The targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure," it said in a blog post.

Major organisations go dark

Australia's own cybersecurity agency, the Australian Signals Directorate, put out a rare critical alert about the flaw directed at everyone from government and critical infrastructure to individuals and families.

Major Australian organisations took drastic steps to avoid falling victim until they were able to ensure that they had patched their own devices.

GovCMS, which hosts many major Australian government websites, blocked direct access to its servers while keeping cached copies of public pages available.

Moodle, an Australian education technology company whose software powers hundreds of thousands of university and schools' online learning platforms, also took its website offline as a precaution, before beginning to restore them after applying security fixes.

Australian hosting provider VentraIP restricted some of its file uploads on customer hosting, warning that forms accepting attachments could fail.

Even smaller website operators such as those running Australian forum for customising computer hardware went down as a precaution.

PHP is used to power an estimated seven in 10 websites and applications. (ABC News: Lauren Pezet)

Mr Hunt said there was little Australians needed to do, but the worst-case scenario was a breach of websites holding their personal information.

"We just need to expect that we may have some elevated instances of the data breaches that we're already seeing every day," he said.

AI helped discover 'critical' flaw

US-based security firm Calif said it had identified a critical flaw using OpenAI's AI models as part of a cybersecurity program it was running.

While the bug appears to have been present in versions of PHP released as far back as 2012, Calif said it took existing research that theorised about a possible attack vector and used AI to confirm the existence of a legitimate vulnerability.

The PHP Foundation said a developer had found the first signs of the underlying problem behind one of the flaws in 2024, but its work repeatedly stalled amid difficult technical choices and limited resources.

AI helped assess reports, the foundation said, while humans remained responsible for decisions and fixes.

"A person makes every call and works on every patch," it said.

OpenAI warned that the same capabilities helping defenders find vulnerabilities could help attackers rapidly develop tools to exploit them.

Additional reporting by national technology reporter Ange Lavoipierre

World.title: Potential PNG signing helping to heal Cooper Bai's family rift
World.content:
Marcus Bai has explained how he and son Cooper moved past the rift that fractured their family, as the Gold Coast forward edges closer to signing a deal with the PNG Chiefs.

Cooper was warmly greeted by his father at Port Moresby's Jacksons International airport yesterday after being granted permission to explore his options ahead of the opening of the November 1 contracting window.

The 19-year-old has been high on the Chiefs' list of targets since the club got the green light to enter the NRL in the 2028 season, with the forward proving a hit with local crowds in Papua New Guinea across his two-Test international career.

PNG Chiefs unveil new logo ahead of 2028 NRL entry The PNG Chiefs logo brings together elements representative of the country ahead of its NRL debut in 2028.

But Cooper's journey hasn't always been smooth, and last year he invoked the ire of his legendary Kumul father when he turned down a deal with Melbourne Storm to remain at the Titans.

"He promised one thing … and then he went and did the other thing, and I was cranky with him," Marcus told AAP.

"I said you've got to be fair and square, that's not how you treat the clubs and people.

"It's not good for us as a family, I was really pissed off with him for that, and I was really angry at him.

"Now [with the chance to join the Chiefs], I said go and have a look and you and your girlfriend sit down and [think through] before making a decision."

Cooper Bai angered his father Marcus (pictured) by going back on his word with regards to signing for the Storm. (Getty Images: Shannon Morris)

Marcus said Cooper had shown maturity by speaking to the Gold Coast to ask permission to visit the Chiefs.

Cooper was due to visit PNG on a family holiday after he was ruled out of the Kumuls' World Cup campaign with a hamstring injury.

"He's only young. He's still finding his feet, and if he comes here there will be a lot of pressure on him," Marcus said.

"The crowd here are tough, they tell you straight up [if they're not happy]."

The chance for Cooper to join the Chiefs would represent a full circle moment for the Bai family.

Marcus left Papua New Guinea in the 1990s to pursue a career as a professional rugby league player, going on to win titles in the NRL and Super League.

He would likely stand down from the Chiefs board if Cooper was to sign a deal to join the club for its inaugural season in 2028.

"I'm proud of his achievements, it is hard to do what he's done and to be able to have an interest from many clubs, it's pleasing for me as a father," Marcus Bai said.

AAP

World.title: Sperm whale stranded near Devonport in Tasmania's north-west
World.content:
Authorities are responding to a large sperm whale found stranded in shallow waters west of Devonport on Tasmania's north-west coast.

Last night, Tasmania Police said they were managing the whale at Turners Beach, along with members of Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service.

Members of the public are asked to avoid the area and not enter the water or the incoming tide due to the "anticipated danger".

Turners Beach resident Haydn says it is a distressing scene.

The sperm whale was reported by a member of the public yesterday. (Supplied: Haydn Pett-Crear)

"Unfortunately the whale is still stranded … there is unfortunately a lot of blood in the water," he said.

"There were about 100 residents here this morning looking on.

" Right now we've got two rangers here just basically babysitting the whale, making sure no-one goes in the water because of the risk of sharks. "

A department of Natural Resources and Environment spokesperson said they were responding to the stranded sperm whale.

"The whale was reported to the marine mammal hotline by a member of the public late on Wednesday," they said.

"Marine Conservation Program wildlife experts and Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service staff are attending the site to assess the whale and appropriate response options.

"Whales are large, powerful animals. Members of the public are asked to keep their distance to maintain human safety and animal welfare.

"It is an offence to interfere with wildlife."

Stranded whales can be reported to the Marine Mammal Hotline on 0427 942 537.

World.content:
BusinessCompaniesElon Musk Opinion Sky’s not the limit: $5 trillion sci-fi deal could bring Musk closer to Mars Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist October 22, 2026 — 12:26pm

October 22, 2026 — 12:26pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

The industrial and financial logic of a merger of SpaceX and Tesla, which Elon Musk has revealed is being evaluated, is compelling – for shareholders, and for the world’s richest man personally. The prospective combination being assessed by a special committee of both companies’ boards would create an entity with a $US3.6 trillion ($5.1 trillion) market capitalisation, ranking behind only Nvidia ($US5.7 trillion), Apple ($US4.9 trillion), Alphabet ($US4.1 trillion) and Microsoft ($US3.8 trillion) in market value. Market size isn’t an end in itself, but it would make it easier for Musk to raise the massive volumes of equity and debt needed to feed the voracious appetite for capital that the two companies require for their increasing investments in artificial intelligence. Merging SpaceX with Tesla makes a lot of sense, both for the company and for Elon Musk personally. Bloomberg It would give Musk access to Tesla’s cash and free cash flows –$US15.22 billion and $US1.53 billion in the September quarter – to help fund SpaceX’s accelerating spending on AI. About $US16.4 billion of SpaceX’s $US19.6 billion of capex in the third quarter was devoted to AI, and it has said its total capex in the December quarter could be as much as $US40 billion.



At face value, combining SpaceX’s rockets, satellites, AI and social media platform with Tesla’s electric vehicles, batteries and solar might not appear as compelling, but there would be plenty of potential synergies available if they were merged. Apart from the fact that Tesla does supply SpaceX with billions of dollars worth of batteries, graphics processing units, software and even Cybertrucks, and is joint-venturing a chip-making factory with SpaceX, Tesla is increasingly an AI company itself – its self-driving vehicles and robots are powered by AI. Tesla also has a $US2 billion investment in SpaceX from that company’s acquisition of another Musk business, xAI. While there is a sci-fi feel to the merger concept, it does, on paper at least, appear to make significant sense. Tesla’s energy storage expertise and robots could also aid SpaceX, if it is to pursue Musk’s bold ambition of building data centres in space and colonising Mars. While there is a sci-fi feel to the merger concept, it does, on paper at least, appear to make significant sense, even though it could restrain Tesla’s ability to invest in developing its mainstream auto business.



It also makes sense for Musk at a personal level, bringing together the two largest entities that he controls and removing the conflicts of interest that flow from their swelling strands of related-party dealings. The deal would create cleaner governance and tighter focus for Musk and would also bring significant personal financial benefits for the mega-billionaire. Related Article Updated

Mergers & acquisitions Elon Musk’s $5 trillion monster: Tesla and SpaceX exploring the biggest merger in history Musk has an economic interest of about 42 per cent in SpaceX (it would be materially higher if his unvested shares were included), but a voting interest of a little over 80 per cent thanks to his “super-voting” shares. He has a more conventional 20 per cent voting and equity interest in Tesla. Both companies have awarded him share-based incentives that, if he were able to meet all their (extremely ambitious) hurdles, would give him trillion-dollar payouts.



If there is a merger, it is probably going to be done through SpaceX, with the larger market capitalisation, acquiring Tesla via a share-based deal. If it were a nil-premium merger, Musk would probably end up with an economic interest in the enlarged SpaceX closer to 30 per cent (40 per cent if all his unvested shares were to vest), but retain a voting interest of close to 75 per cent. That could be an obstacle at the Tesla level – shareholders would go from being able to outvote Musk comfortably (in theory at least, given that the Tesla board and shareholders appear to be in thrall of him) to being locked into a company where he has absolute control. That concession may argue against a nil premium deal. For Musk, a change of control at the Tesla level would probably trigger immediate vesting of his performance-based incentives, without having to achieve the performance hurdles. That could add tens of billions, if not hundreds of billions, to the paper wealth of the world’s richest man. There are some potential obstacles, even if Musk and his boards commit themselves to the merger.



Musk and his companies have a raft of contractor relationships with the US government, including some that would have national security implications and others that might fall foul of antitrust laws, particularly if the Democrats were able to gain control of Congress and the White House. China would also have a say and might not be enthusiastic, given SpaceX is a US defence contractor. About half of Tesla’s global EV production is based in China, so there would be significant commercial implications if Beijing opposed the deal. Tesla could spin off its operations in China or sell them, of course, but that would gut its international EV business. Loading The third-quarter results released this week for both companies provide some sense of what the mega company would look like, although the related-party revenues and Tesla’s interest in SpaceX would be excised in a merger and their assets would be revalued (probably significantly higher) on a mark-to-market basis.



In crude terms, however, the combination would have generated revenue of roughly $US43 billion and profits of more than $US5 billion in the September quarter. It would have combined debt and finance leases of close to $US50 billion and shareholder funds of about $US260 billion, with about $US135 billion of cash and investments. Tesla is cutting back severely on its capex. Its spending was about $US1 billion lower than in the second quarter and about $US3 billion less than the market expected. Its free cash flow was $US1.53 billion where the market expected it to burn $US5 billion. Related Article Opinion

AI These three kings of AI have a plan. It could blow everything up Stephen Bartholomeusz Senior business columnist SpaceX, which has been renting out computing power in a market where “compute” is becoming scarce as demand is rising rapidly even as the rate at which data centres are being built is slowing, had negative free cash flow in the quarter – probably close to $US10 billion – with the gap from $US6.9 billion of capex in the same quarter last year to $US19.6 billion the obvious cause. The potential revenues from the compute deals SpaceX has been striking with companies like Anthropic and Google, where it is selling capacity for about $US1 billion a month in three-year deals, will increasingly help fund Musk’s extremely expensive visions of the future.



His engineers appear to be able to build AI infrastructure faster and more efficiently than others and, in a market increasingly short of compute, that is a very attractive position to be in. It can generate substantial high-margin revenue while SpaceX’s own AI demand for compute falls well short of the capacity it has today and on its drawing boards. Musk’s dream of data centres in space and colonies of Mars would be more easily funded and realised, however, by combining Tesla’s balance sheet, cash and cashflows, its robots and batteries and energy storage expertise with SpaceX’s AI intellectual property and hard assets, its rockets and its satellites. The deal would create an integrated entity with better and probably cheaper access to equity and debt than both companies can get on their own today. Professional kitchens that specialise in one kind of dish have existed since professional kitchens were invented. London’s jellied eel stalls. Fukuoka’s tonkotsu ramen shops. The smashburgers at Robs in Rozelle.

In 2023 when Lingqi Yang found it hard to track down the cheung fun she grew up with in Guangzhou, she opened Taste of Canton next to a car wash (the original has closed, but the Ultimo outpost still pumps), bringing the rippled, silky steamed rice noodle rolls to Sydneysiders.

Made to order by steaming a rice flour mixture in a car bonnet-sized pan, each serve comes with your choice of egg, prawn, pork or giving brisket in a rich, savoury chu hou sauce.

Pork buns, black bean ribs and (a very good) preserved egg congee bulk up the menu, and don’t forget to help yourself to the house-made garlic and mushroom soy sauce from the condiment station.

Sitting in the clutch of shops at the centre of breezy Freshwater, this white-brick, warm-hued Mexican bar and restaurant feels as quintessentially coastal as the waves washing the shoreline mere blocks away.

Plates are easy to like: tacos that offset slow-cooked pork with chicharron crunch and lime juice, say, or a tostada loaded with smoked barramundi and avocado crowned with orbs of scallop.

Order the confit mushrooms and the accompanying sauce is a fresh take on the moles more commonly found in Sydney – this one’s white, and humming with almonds, peach and pecans.

It would be remiss not to consider sipping something from the long list of tequila and mezcal, while a wobbly flan is as smooth and golden as the best of beach evenings. NB: Book ahead, even mid week – the locals (here, and at the Avalon outpost) are big fans.

World.content:
Updated NationalQueenslandWeather Flood warning as first severe storm of the season looms, second front develops Catherine Strohfeldt Updated October 22, 2026 — 12:16pm ,first published October 22, 2026 — 7:58am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. A severe thunderstorm is forecast to hit outer Brisbane suburbs, with the weather bureau warning residents in the city’s north-west, while a second front threatened residents south of the city on Thursday. The Bureau of Meteorology issued a warning for flash flooding between the Sunshine Coast and the state border – including Brisbane, Caboolture, and Ipswich – across Thursday. Loading “This [storm] will be the first big one and certainly the one that’s bringing the most intense rainfall,” senior meteorologist Angus Hines said. The south-moving storm dumped up to 170 millimetres of rain on Caboolture and Morayfield over three hours from 4.30am.



Between 4.45am and 7.45am, Burpengary recorded 141 millimetres. Further north, parts of Elimbah recorded up to 163 millimetres over three hours by about 8am. While the weather bureau initially predicted the storm would move over Brisbane between 7am and 8am, the system slowed across the morning. A storm headed for Brisbane has stalled over Caboolture. Bureau of Meteorlogy Several hours later, a second storm developed over the Gold Coast hinterland, which the weather bureau also tracked as moving south. Meteorologist Tristan Sumarna said the weather system hanging over the region was unstable and active.



He said the storm at Caboolture could remain contained to the region, with residents of Brisbane’s north-western suburbs directly in the firing line, and new storms could develop across the rest of the day. The downpour in Brisbane’s CBD during the morning rush hour on Thursday. Rosanna Ryan Police reported almost 40 SES call-outs over 24 hours from 6.30am on Wednesday for sandbagging and setting up tarps across Moreton Bay, Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Logan. Swift-water rescue crews also responded to multiple stranded vehicles, including one at an intersection in central Caboolture. Residents were advised to move vehicles away from trees or park them undercover, secure pets and close windows.



The weather bureau also strongly discouraged driving as the storm passed overhead. Hines said the storms were inside a larger rain system that had been sitting over much of the state since Monday. “Even without the stormy weather, we’ve got this broad rain band, so pretty much everyone across the south-east will get a decent drop of rain today,” he said. “Then wherever those thunderstorms pop up, embedded in this overall rain band, those rainfall numbers will climb much more sharply [and] much more rapidly.”



Hines said areas outside the storm’s path could still receive up to 30 millimetres of rain on Thursday. Energex recorded four outages across the south-east at 9.15am, affecting more than 1700 homes. By 11am four more outages occurred, although many homes cut off by earlier outages had been reconnected. Bowman Parade in Bardon has been closed since 8.30am. The Department of Transport and Main Roads warned water across the road had closed lanes along Gympie Arterial Road, in Brisbane’s north. Other roads throughout the city were closed – including Vulture Street in South Brisbane – across the morning.



While the system was not expected to bring intense winds, Hines said gusting could cause isolated instances of swirling wind that could “kick through in any direction”. The senior meteorologist predicted wet conditions would last until Monday afternoon. “Temperatures will climb a little bit [over the weekend] because the thick cloud cover and the rain band will break apart a bit,” he said. “Even though we’ve still got showers in the forecast, we’re much more likely to get some good spells of sunshine.” But Hines said temperatures would remain between 3 and 6 degrees below the October average – 28 degrees – until the larger rain band lifted. The dining room opens up onto the street.

5 / 5 The dining room opens up onto the street.

Always packed and trilling with the sound of workhorse woks, this hole-in-the-wall is a two-decade-old institution that doesn’t shirk on heat, flavour, ingredients or buzz.

You will queue. You will squeeze onto seats. But efficient staff and short cooking times reward the wait as signature dishes such as gang som cha-om goong – a brothy tamarind-rich sour and spicy curry piled with fat, chilli-flecked prawns – arrive. Or a glistening, sweet-hot hillock of pad prik pao with wonderfully crisp deep-fried pork belly lolling in chilli jam, cherry tomatoes, spring onion and smile-wide shards of red chilli.

Go harder with freshly shredded green papaya salad featuring snake beans, crunchy dried shrimp and crushed peanut which is grip-the-table hot, or cool down with tom kha gai, charged with lemongrass, galangal and makrut lime, followed by a tall glass of oliang – sweet Thai iced coffee – to get your pounding heart back to a regular rate.

World.title: Shri Refreshment Bar
World.content:
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

If you aren’t local to Harris Park, think of Shri Refreshment Bar not as the final destination, but a beginning. A takeaway perched on the corner of Wigram and Marion streets, with snacks sitting pretty under lights and basic furniture set up abutting a lane and a couple of parking spaces, it’s far removed from the comforts that many of the other restaurants in Sydney’s Little India offer.

There’s still time for the Mumbai street food at Chatkazz, the northern-style dishes at Not Just Curries, the syrupy desserts at Jaipur Sweets, but first: chaat. Vada pav, say, consisting of a fluffy bread roll stuffed with a crisp-fried spiced potato patty. Or samosa chaat, the golden pastry smashed to pieces and overloaded with chaana masala, yoghurt and chutneys. This is snack city, with good dhal, paratha and a pani puri stand to boot. How refreshing.

World.content:

Remove items from your saved list to add more.

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Elusive signage and a nondescript front space give little indication of the grill-your-own deliciousness ahead. Out back, you’ll find a garden courtyard where large groups convene over heroic quantities of skewered meat to a soundtrack of whizzing fans and hissing coals.

A vast menu includes plenty of beer-friendly gnarly bits (tongue, skin and cartilage) and prices are more than reasonable. The 20-skewer-per-table minimum is easy to reach. A generous order of fatty lamb skewers, liberally dusted with cumin-heavy seasoning, is essential, and for spice fanatics there are tabletop shakers of whole cumin seeds. Double-skewered half-quail cooks up a treat, smoky and blushing thanks to cleverly designed grills.

It’s also worth exploring some of the seafood or vegetable options, such as the cold buckwheat noodles and crisp potato pancake which, with a tight banchan spread, keep everything nicely in check.

World.title: The Rover
World.content:
You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.

It can be tricky to get your head around The Rover. The bold tartan carpet says “British pub roasts”, but then the menu is oysters and burgers. Those burgers say “craft beer please”, but this is a cocktail bar with an extensive wine list.

Our advice? Don’t overthink it, and instead dive into a dozen of those oysters, paired with a bone-dry sparkling Chablis. Nice. Move, then, to The Gidley burger, care of The Rover’s sister establishment in the CBD. A double beef patty is engulfed with American cheese and comes with hunky pickles on the side; the chips are thin and crisp.

You could spend your entire night at cosied up in a booth or balanced on a bar stool, but the place is perhaps best for pre- or post-dining, for oysters and sparkling to kick the night off (or a very well made Old Fashioned), and a whisky – neat – to wind it down.

Best for: Pre-dinner snacks or post-meal whisky.

The downpour in Brisbane’s CBD during the morning rush hour on Thursday. Rosanna Ryan Police reported almost 40 SES call-outs over 24 hours from 6.30am on Wednesday for sandbagging and setting up tarps across Moreton Bay, Brisbane, the Gold Coast and Logan. Swift-water rescue crews also responded to multiple stranded vehicles, including one at an intersection in central Caboolture. Residents were advised to move vehicles away from trees or park them undercover, secure pets and close windows.



The weather bureau also strongly discouraged driving as the storm passed overhead. Hines said the storms were inside a larger rain system that had been sitting over much of the state since Monday. “Even without the stormy weather, we’ve got this broad rain band, so pretty much everyone across the south-east will get a decent drop of rain today,” he said. “Then wherever those thunderstorms pop up, embedded in this overall rain band, those rainfall numbers will climb much more sharply [and] much more rapidly.”



Hines said areas outside the storm’s path could still receive up to 30 millimetres of rain on Thursday. Energex recorded four outages across the south-east at 9.15am, affecting more than 1700 homes. By 11am four more outages occurred, although many homes cut off by earlier outages had been reconnected. Bowman Parade in Bardon has been closed since 8.30am. The Department of Transport and Main Roads warned water across the road had closed lanes along Gympie Arterial Road, in Brisbane’s north. Other roads throughout the city were closed – including Vulture Street in South Brisbane – across the morning.



While the system was not expected to bring intense winds, Hines said gusting could cause isolated instances of swirling wind that could “kick through in any direction”. The senior meteorologist predicted wet conditions would last until Monday afternoon. “Temperatures will climb a little bit [over the weekend] because the thick cloud cover and the rain band will break apart a bit,” he said. “Even though we’ve still got showers in the forecast, we’re much more likely to get some good spells of sunshine.” But Hines said temperatures would remain between 3 and 6 degrees below the October average – 28 degrees – until the larger rain band lifted. The dining room opens up onto the street.

5 / 5 The dining room opens up onto the street.

Always packed and trilling with the sound of workhorse woks, this hole-in-the-wall is a two-decade-old institution that doesn’t shirk on heat, flavour, ingredients or buzz.

You will queue. You will squeeze onto seats. But efficient staff and short cooking times reward the wait as signature dishes such as gang som cha-om goong – a brothy tamarind-rich sour and spicy curry piled with fat, chilli-flecked prawns – arrive. Or a glistening, sweet-hot hillock of pad prik pao with wonderfully crisp deep-fried pork belly lolling in chilli jam, cherry tomatoes, spring onion and smile-wide shards of red chilli.

Go harder with freshly shredded green papaya salad featuring snake beans, crunchy dried shrimp and crushed peanut which is grip-the-table hot, or cool down with tom kha gai, charged with lemongrass, galangal and makrut lime, followed by a tall glass of oliang – sweet Thai iced coffee – to get your pounding heart back to a regular rate.

World.content:

If you aren’t local to Harris Park, think of Shri Refreshment Bar not as the final destination, but a beginning. A takeaway perched on the corner of Wigram and Marion streets, with snacks sitting pretty under lights and basic furniture set up abutting a lane and a couple of parking spaces, it’s far removed from the comforts that many of the other restaurants in Sydney’s Little India offer.

There’s still time for the Mumbai street food at Chatkazz, the northern-style dishes at Not Just Curries, the syrupy desserts at Jaipur Sweets, but first: chaat. Vada pav, say, consisting of a fluffy bread roll stuffed with a crisp-fried spiced potato patty. Or samosa chaat, the golden pastry smashed to pieces and overloaded with chaana masala, yoghurt and chutneys. This is snack city, with good dhal, paratha and a pani puri stand to boot. How refreshing.

Elusive signage and a nondescript front space give little indication of the grill-your-own deliciousness ahead. Out back, you’ll find a garden courtyard where large groups convene over heroic quantities of skewered meat to a soundtrack of whizzing fans and hissing coals.

A vast menu includes plenty of beer-friendly gnarly bits (tongue, skin and cartilage) and prices are more than reasonable. The 20-skewer-per-table minimum is easy to reach. A generous order of fatty lamb skewers, liberally dusted with cumin-heavy seasoning, is essential, and for spice fanatics there are tabletop shakers of whole cumin seeds. Double-skewered half-quail cooks up a treat, smoky and blushing thanks to cleverly designed grills.

It’s also worth exploring some of the seafood or vegetable options, such as the cold buckwheat noodles and crisp potato pancake which, with a tight banchan spread, keep everything nicely in check.
